Project Summary: This project increases output and lowers the costs of a small organic dairy processing plant serving underserved producers in economically distressed areas. By supporting a full-time sales position, it expands market access both for existing organic dairy producers and for dairy producers transitioning to organic. It does this through co-packing, two processor-affiliated brands, and other marketing channels it has developed and will continue to expand. Plant upgrades include adding packaging options optimized for food service and food product manufacturers that represent over a third of the national demand for dairy products. The desire central outcome of these activities is to develop product market matches that successfully generate sustained income for organic dairy producers by meeting the needs of existing sales outlets more efficiently and completely.
llm_summary: This project aims to increase output and lower costs for a small organic dairy processing plant, supporting farmers and processors within economically distressed areas. The core activities involve expanding market access for both established organic dairy producers and those transitioning to organic practices through co-packing initiatives and two processor-affiliated brands, alongside the expansion of marketing channels. A key component of this project is the addition of plant upgrades, specifically incorporating packaging options optimized for food service and food product manufacturers, representing a significant portion – over a third – of national demand for dairy products. The anticipated outcome is the development of successful product market matches that will sustainably generate income for organic dairy producers by more efficiently and completely meeting the requirements of existing sales outlets. These activities will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors, contributing to increased revenue streams and reduced operational expenses. Ultimately, the project seeks to create a robust system where dairy products from this plant can reliably reach consumers and food manufacturers, ensuring a consistent and profitable market for the organic dairy producers involved. This will strengthen the overall dairy supply chain and facilitate the growth of organic dairy production within these targeted communities.

Project Summary: Agoge, a sustainable organic product-focused company, has spent 2 years and significant funds researching developing a foundational set of products with organic ingredients to support improved health outcomes. The ingredients in its products are isolated hempseed proteins, certified Organic by the USDA. In short, Agoge is introducing the USA’s first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate (OHPI). The project aims to open the OHPI market and drive the expansion of the upstream (supply) and downstream (demand) supply chain for this organic, sustainable rotational crop through education, marketing, and consumer buyer outreach. The objectives include: 1) Opening the OHPI market by providing the food ingredient sector with the USA’s very first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate products a deeply researched foundational ingredient and its first 3 formulated finished goods. 2) Targeting and educating 8,000 consumers a month using traditional and digital marketing campaigns through education events targeting dietitians, nutritionists, doctors, etc., and 3) Hosting a 20x20 exhibitor booth at 10 of the USA’s biggest ingredient and food conferences. The project will include OHPI industry connector events twice a year for 2 years across 4 different cities.
llm_summary: Agoge is undertaking a project to establish the USA’s first Organic Hemp Protein Isolate (OHPI) market and drive the expansion of its associated supply chain, focusing on a sustainable rotational crop. The project’s core activities include the development and introduction of OHPI products, beginning with a foundational ingredient and three initial formulated finished goods, and will be supported by extensive marketing and consumer outreach initiatives. Anticipated outcomes include significant market penetration for the OHPI product line, leading to increased demand from processors, retailers, and ultimately, consumers. Agoge intends to reach approximately 8,000 consumers monthly through targeted marketing campaigns designed to educate dietitians, nutritionists, and physicians. Furthermore, the project involves a substantial presence at ten key ingredient and food conferences, each featuring a 20x20 exhibitor booth, and the hosting of twice-yearly industry connector events across four different cities. The project aims to provide a readily available source of this organic ingredient, benefiting farmers cultivating the rotational crop and supporting the growth of the downstream supply chain. Ultimately, Agoge’s efforts will contribute to increased market access for this certified organic ingredient, benefiting all stakeholders involved in its production and distribution.

Project Summary: The Schmitt’s Farm converted to 100% organic in 2018. The farm grows spring wheat, hulless oats, lentils, yellow peas, chickpeas, hemp grain, canola, alfalfa, and flax. It has a crop rotation of 25% cereal grains (wheat, oats, etc), 25% Legume (peas, chickpeas, alfalfa), 25% oil seeds (flax, hemp seed, canola) and 25 % fallow with cover crop. A number of innovative practices are being tested continuously to get closer to notill or minimum tilling using cover crops, interseeding multiple crops together and relay seeding crops together. The purpose of this project is to help address a current bottleneck in the organic marketplace: which is a lack of organic grain processing infrastructure. Goals include: 1) strengthening and expanding farm capacity 2) Providing grain cleaning services to other organic growers, and 3) increasing access to organic grains. The purchase of this equipment will allow Schmitt’s Farm to increase its annual gross income, increase storage capacity by 13,500 bushels, decrease annual miles traveled by 60,000 miles per year, and increase processing capacity of organic grains by 800,000 bushels per year. The main equipment beneficiaries will include Schmitt Organic Farms and other farms in the region that will now have local or more regionalized access to organic grain processing. This will have a trickle-down effect leading to greater access to organic grain throughout the entire North west region. This will also positively impact buyers as 3 Schmitt’s Farm will be able to more reliably provide them with products. In turn, consumers, bakeries, and restaurants will also have greater access to organic grains.
llm_summary: Schmitt’s Farm has initiated a project to address a critical need within the organic marketplace: a lack of sufficient grain processing infrastructure. This project centers on the purchase of equipment designed to strengthen and expand farm capacity, provide grain cleaning services to other organic growers, and increase access to organic grains for farmers and stakeholders throughout the Northwest region. Specifically, the investment will result in an increase of 800,000 bushels per year in processing capacity, alongside a 13,500 bushel expansion in storage capacity. Furthermore, the acquisition is projected to reduce annual miles traveled by 60,000 miles, streamlining operations and reducing transportation costs for processors and distributors. The anticipated outcomes will benefit a wide range of stakeholders, including organic grain buyers, regional food processors, and ultimately, consumers who will gain greater access to reliably sourced organic grains. This initiative is expected to bolster Schmitt’s Farm’s annual gross income, establishing a more robust and accessible supply chain for organic grains within the Northwest region.

Project Summary: Dairy is the largest organic commodity in the United States, with 1.6 billion in annual sales, yet organic milk represents just 2 % of the nations dairy production and is declining. USDA’s Organic Dairy Market News reports that year-to-date sales of organic milk products are down 1.6 % from the prior year. As organic dairy production costs have increased in recent years, the price premium of fluid organic milk over conventional milk has eroded, leaving organic dairy producers, most of them small family farms, with shrinking on-farm profits that threaten their livelihood. To address this challenging issue, Rumiano Cheese Company, seeks to expand in-house processing capacity to make and market innovative, high-demand organic dairy products in channels that offer a higher price premium over fluid. Activities to be performed will include 1) installing a state-of-the-art processing line to upcycle organic cheese trim into value-added sauces, dips and spreads; 2) acquiring additional equipment to create artisanal specialty cheese wheels inhouse; and 3) expanding marketing, sales, and innovation to gain retail access and build consumer demand for the expanded volume produced through this project. This venture’s goals are to process an additional 32,372,700 pounds of fluid milk and cheese trim, generating approximately $31.5 million in sales revenue and benefiting 27 Northern California pasture-based organic dairy producers during the project period.
llm_summary: Rumiano Cheese Company is undertaking a project to expand its in-house processing capabilities and market innovative organic dairy products, addressing a critical need within the organic dairy sector. This initiative will involve the installation of a state-of-the-art processing line specifically designed to upcycle organic cheese trim into a range of high-demand value-added products, including sauces, dips, and spreads. Furthermore, the company will acquire additional equipment to enable the creation of artisanal specialty cheese wheels entirely within their facility. The project’s goals are to process an additional 32,372,700 pounds of fluid milk and cheese trim, ultimately generating approximately $31.5 million in sales revenue. These activities will directly benefit 27 Northern California pasture-based organic dairy producers, supporting their operations and enhancing their profitability. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased market access for these producers and a greater supply of organic dairy products to consumers. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of milk and trim processed, the revenue generated, and the overall impact on the livelihoods of the participating farmers and stakeholders. This expansion represents a strategic investment aimed at capitalizing on the growing demand for organic dairy products and strengthening the position of Rumiano Cheese Company within the market.

Project Summary: Heal the Earth at Wild Acres Farm, a San Diego County nonprofit and avocado farm, will improve and grow the long-term viability of the domestic organic avocado market by coordinating a direct to consumer valuechain and launching a comprehensive regional marketing campaign. This project will facilitate the flow of avocados into regional markets by leveraging the expertise of, and building on the work done in partnership with, the Avocado Growers of California, the City of Escondido, and other stakeholders. Collaborative efforts will include marketing and outreach to buyers and consumers, promoting opportunities to sell and buy US-grown avocados at a local food hub, a feasibility study, and resulting strategic promotional efforts tailored to the needs of domestic organic avocado growers and US consumers. Heal the Earth will expand staff capacity, build and maintain relationships with certified organic growers, establish new and expanded markets for organic avocados, and develop and execute a marketing plan that differentiates the organic, US-grown product to both buyers and end consumers. Heal the Earth will 1) build relationships between organic avocado producers and consumers, 2) create alternative market channels for organic avocados and ancillary organic farm products, 3) increase consumer awareness of the benefits of locally-grown, 7 California-produced avocados. There is a growing demand for avocados, and organic fruit both supports local farmers and climate-smart growing practices.
llm_summary: Heal the Earth at Wild Acres Farm is undertaking a project to improve and grow the long-term viability of the domestic organic avocado market by establishing a direct-to-consumer value chain and launching a comprehensive regional marketing campaign. This initiative will facilitate the flow of avocados into regional markets through collaboration with key stakeholders, including the Avocado Growers of California, the City of Escondido, and other partners. The project will involve the creation of a local food hub to support the sale and purchase of US-grown avocados, alongside a feasibility study to inform strategic promotional efforts tailored to the needs of domestic organic avocado growers and US consumers. Ultimately, Heal the Earth aims to build relationships between organic avocado producers and consumers, and to develop alternative market channels for organic avocados and related farm products. The project will increase consumer awareness of the benefits of locally-produced avocados. This will positively impact farmers and processors involved in the avocado industry, as well as consumers seeking this agricultural product. Heal the Earth’s activities will directly support the growth of the organic avocado market and stimulate demand for this agricultural commodity. The expected outcome is a strengthened position for domestic organic avocado producers and greater access to these products for consumers.

Project Summary: This project paves the way to making regenerative kelp farming a viable industry for rural seaside farming communities that rely on volatile wild-caught seafood. Historically, kelp farming within the US has not been considered a lucrative industry because of perceived competition from Asian markets and a lack of profitable end markets for US-grown kelp products. As a result, 95% of seaweed products sold in the US are imported from Asia. Consumers are already proving they are ready for kelp-based snacks, so now is the time to invest in scaling up the kelp industry, spurring demand for more kelp farmers to grow a regenerative and ocean-friendly crop. The major limitation for kelp farmers is a lack of processing and product manufacturing capacity to transform kelp into high-value products. By providing a profitable end market for kelp 12 Tides solves this issue. This project scales up the production of a highly sought-after product line that provides high quality, consistent revenue to rural kelp farmers. Kelp is easy to grow, produces low CO2-equivalent emissions than corn, and can be reliably harvested year after year while mitigating ocean acidification and increasing marine biodiversity. This provides economic stability for farmers in communities historically reliant on increasingly volatile seafood industries as well as a healthy snack product for consumers. This grant allows 12 Tides to scale its processing capacity, support a nationwide launch, and expand the supply chain by purchasing from 27 new organic farms, while employing 144 staff, and supporting 275 kelp farming jobs in the U.S.
llm_summary: 12 Tides’ project aims to establish regenerative kelp farming as a viable industry for rural seaside farming communities reliant on fluctuating seafood markets. This initiative will focus on scaling up the production of a highly sought-after product line, utilizing a new processing capacity and purchasing kelp from 27 newly certified organic farms across the United States. The project anticipates generating high quality, consistent revenue streams for farmers and providing a healthy snack option for consumers. Specifically, 12 Tides will build significant processing and manufacturing infrastructure, resulting in the creation of 144 jobs and supporting an additional 275 kelp farming positions throughout the nation. The expected outcome is a substantial increase in the availability of domestically produced kelp, addressing a critical gap in the market and fostering economic stability for farmers. By concentrating on the development of this new industry, 12 Tides intends to significantly expand the supply chain, bolstering the economic prospects of its stakeholders and creating a reliable source of a valued agricultural product.

Project Summary: ZEGO is a woman-owned B Corp-certified brand focusing on supply-chain transparency and purity testing using Montana Gluten Free’s hull-less, high-protein, organic oats. ZEGO sells products in 1500+ stores nationwide. The project will increase processing and consumption of organic, gluten-free, high-protein oats and rotational crop millet in Montana and the surrounding growing region by creating a collaborative integrated value chain (CVIC). The goals are to 1) expand organic processing capacity at Montana Gluten Free (MGF) to alleviate a regional grain processing bottleneck that forces farmers to sell premium crops for bird and animal feed at 50% of full value; 2) develop more products from organic specialty grains for people with medically restricted diets due to allergies or gluten intolerance, toxin and pesticide concerns, or diabetes or to increase dietary plant protein; 3) increase special-diet consumer pull (demand) of organic grains by expanding product trials, adding sales channels, building consumer trust in organic food; and 4) benefit the environment by decreasing transportation miles and promotion of hulless oats, which produce 50% less carbon emissions, and drought-tolerant millet, which uses 1/3rd less water than other grains. In addition to the project goals Zego predicts that the project will 1) increase organic finished goods capacity 5 by integrating operations at MGF with faster and more efficient equipment for bag filling and improved processing efficiency; 2) upgrade food safety certification level; 3) establish a millet value chain by purchasing and installing equipment to dehull millet. It will also help setting up procurement contracts with regional farmer and developing 3-5 new organic specialty grain products, in collaboration with Snacktivist, targeting markets such as food service accounts and big box stores, and build B2B ingredient sales. The project will allow for the implementation of marketing strategies led by a specialized marketing director to increase awareness and adoption of organic specialty grains among special-diet and non-toxic living consumers; and collaborate with technology partner Food Vision to enhance ZEGO’s purity transparency system, making product information accessible and expanding the scope of information to include links to farmers.
llm_summary: ZEGO is undertaking a project to increase processing and consumption of organic, gluten-free, high-protein oats and rotational crop millet in Montana and the surrounding growing region by establishing a collaborative integrated value chain (CIVC). This initiative focuses on addressing a regional grain processing bottleneck, currently forcing farmers to sell premium crops for bird and animal feed at 50% of their full value, and aims to develop more products from these grains for consumers with medically restricted diets due to allergies, intolerances, or specific health concerns, as well as to expand dietary plant protein intake. The project will involve the purchase and installation of equipment to dehull millet and upgrades to MGF’s operations, including faster bag filling equipment and improved processing efficiency, alongside an upgrade to the food safety certification level. Anticipated outcomes include a five-fold increase in organic finished goods capacity, the establishment of a millet value chain through farmer procurement contracts, and the development of three to five new organic specialty grain products in collaboration with Snacktivist, targeting food service accounts and big box stores, alongside the creation of B2B ingredient sales. The project will benefit farmers and processors by providing new market opportunities for their organic grains, while offering consumers access to a wider range of specialty grain products. Furthermore, ZEGO is collaborating with Food Vision to enhance its purity transparency system, making product information accessible and expanding the scope of information to include links to farmers, ultimately strengthening trust among stakeholders.

Legal Name: Wehah Farm, Inc dba Lundberg Family Farms
Project Summary: In 2022, US farmers produced more than 16 billion pounds of rice to serve domestic and international consumers (USDA Economic Research Service). Still, less than 1% of the rice produced in the United States is organic, despite strong and consistent growth in US demand for organic food. With more than 82% of US households buying organic products regularly, the Organic Center notes demand in the US for organic rice exceeds domestic supply, encouraging significant competition from imports. In fact, US imports of rice have steadily increased over the past five years, growing more than 36% from the 2017/2018 crop year to the 2021/2022 crop year. This is primarily due to the major barriers that exist to producing, processing, and marketing organic rice, namely higher costs of production, and lack of processing and marketing infrastructure. To meet current US consumer demand and expand opportunities to build the US organic rice 8 market (project purpose), Lundberg Family Farms, the nation’s largest organic rice producer and processor, will launch a comprehensive effort to support current and transitioning organic producers in increasing organic rice production. Project activities toward removing barriers to entry for producers include grower outreach and technology adaptation expanding processing capacity to create more and better markets for organic producers and executing marketing and promotional activities that will help to build commercial markets for US organic rice products. This project’s goals (deliverables and expected outcomes) include achieving 3,000 new acres of organic rice processing and a $17 million increase in domestic regenerative organic rice sales by the end of the project period.
llm_summary: Lundberg Family Farms will launch a comprehensive project to support US organic rice producers and expand the domestic market for organic rice, aligning with the goal of increasing the availability of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. This initiative will focus on removing barriers to entry for producers and increasing organic rice production, specifically targeting the expansion of processing capacity and the creation of enhanced market opportunities for organic rice products. The project anticipates achieving 3,000 new acres of organic rice processing, which will contribute to a $17 million increase in domestic sales of regenerative organic rice by the end of the project period. This will benefit farmers, processors, and stakeholders involved in the rice industry, as well as consumers seeking organic rice products. The project’s activities include grower outreach and the adaptation of technology to improve production methods. Furthermore, the project will execute marketing and promotional activities to stimulate commercial markets for US organic rice products. Ultimately, this initiative aims to meet current consumer demand and strengthen the overall organic rice market within the United States.

Legal Name: Vista Livestock Co. dba Burroughs Family Orchards
Project Summary: Burroughs Family Orchards (BFO) is a certified organic and regenerative family farm committed to fostering a sustainable food system. This project is designed to increase consumption of BFO's organic almond and olive products, drive market interest, and meet the growing demand for high-quality organic products. BFO plans to broaden its market reach by expanding into new geographic regions, specifically in the Central and Southern U.S. territories. This strategic expansion will be facilitated through hiring a marketing contractor and a broker, who will work to increase the visibility and availability of BFO's organic almond and olive products. Additionally, BFO will invest in developing new and improved organic products, partnering with experienced consultants to expand their product range and drive market interest and demand for organic products. To meet the growing demand for organic almonds, BFO plans to enhance its storage and distribution capacity by investing in temperature and weatherproofing its existing warehouse storage space to ensure optimal freshness and shelf life of their products year-round. These enhancements will enable BFO to scale its operations in tandem with the rising demand for organic almonds. The project is expected to significantly improve BFO's ability to compete in the organic sector. It will advance their mission of promoting a sustainable food system, contributing to the growth of the organic market, and delivering high-quality, innovative almond and olive products to consumers across the nation.
llm_summary: Burroughs Family Orchards (BFO) is undertaking a strategic project designed to significantly increase the consumption of its certified organic almond and olive products, thereby driving market interest and meeting the growing demand for high-quality organic offerings across the nation. This initiative will be facilitated through the engagement of a marketing contractor and a broker, intended to expand the visibility and availability of BFO’s products in new geographic territories, primarily within the Central and Southern U.S. Alongside this market expansion, BFO will invest in the development of enhanced organic products through partnerships with experienced consultants, broadening their product range and stimulating demand. Furthermore, to optimize its operations and meet anticipated increases in demand, BFO will upgrade its existing warehouse storage space with temperature and weatherproofing measures, ensuring consistent product freshness and extended shelf life throughout the year. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial improvement in BFO’s ability to compete effectively within the organic sector, directly supporting farmers and processors involved in the production and distribution of these valuable commodities. The project will benefit consumers seeking high-quality organic options and contribute to the overall growth of the organic market by providing greater access to domestically produced almonds and olives. This project aims to strengthen BFO’s position as a key supplier within the organic agricultural landscape, ultimately fostering a more robust and sustainable food system.

Project Summary: The Rock Front Ranch’s (RFR) project goal is to increase market access to organic products by improving the efficiency of transporting organic fruit to organic minded consumers and generating employment opportunities in a community with persistent poverty. Rock Front Ranch (RFR) has provided organic jujube fruit to 29 Whole Foods in Southern California since 2017. Recently, the ranch has endeavored to serve Whole Foods and other organic stores in the Northern California region. Those efforts have been curtailed by lack of sufficient transportation capabilities and the prohibitive expense of contracting for 3rd party delivery. The addition of two delivery trailers would allow RFR to provide both fresh and dried organic jujube fruit to the entire network of Whole Foods in Northern California, an additional 39 stores, as well as other organic stores. Two trailers will provide the capacity to deliver fresh and dried organic jujube fruit to both Northern and Southern California markets simultaneously, increasing efficiency as well as creating two 4 to-four new employment opportunities for residents of the Cuyama Valley, a community with persistent poverty.
llm_summary: Rock Front Ranch’s (RFR) project aims to enhance market access for organic products by optimizing the transportation of organic jujube fruit to meet the demands of conscious consumers. The project involves the acquisition of two specialized delivery trailers designed to facilitate the simultaneous distribution of both fresh and dried jujube fruit to an expanded network of retail outlets. These trailers will enable RFR to serve a total of 68 Whole Foods stores – 39 in Northern California and the existing 29 in Southern California – along with other organic stores seeking this product. This expansion represents a significant increase in the company’s reach and capacity. The anticipated outcome is a substantial improvement in the availability of organic jujube fruit to a broader customer base. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers at Rock Front Ranch, retail stores, and consumers who prioritize organic food options. Furthermore, the project will create two new employment opportunities for residents of the Cuyama Valley, addressing a persistent challenge within that community. By streamlining the supply chain and increasing market access, RFR seeks to bolster the economic viability of the ranch and provide a valuable product to a growing number of stakeholders.

Legal Name: California Craft Maltings, LLC dba Admiral Maltings
Project Summary: The purpose of this project is to purchase and install milling equipment to allow for new product offerings and expanded organic capacity for milled raw grains. It is a natural extension of what Admiral Maltings already does to mill and package organic flour for bakeries and grist (raw grains) for distillers. Milling organic flour for bakers and distillers’ grist uses similar agricultural ingredients to what California Craft Maltings already sources. But it is a different process from malting organic grain and requires new equipment. This equipment purchase will allow Admiral Maltings to increase the contracted acreage of organically grown grain, increase land under organic certification, and create a more resilient, local agricultural economy to supply bakers and distillers. It will lead to aggregate efficiencies for growing, storing, and processing organic grains. There is increased consumer demand to know who grows their food, where it is grown, where it is processed, and who mills it.
llm_summary: Admiral Maltings is undertaking a project to purchase and install milling equipment, a key expansion of its existing operations to facilitate new product offerings and significantly increase organic capacity for milled raw grains. This initiative directly supports the company’s current activities of milling organic flour for bakeries and grist for distillers, utilizing similar agricultural ingredients as already sourced. The purchase of this specialized equipment will enable Admiral Maltings to expand its contracted acreage of organically grown grain, further increasing land under organic certification, and ultimately contribute to a more resilient, local agricultural economy. The anticipated outcomes include aggregate efficiencies for the growing, storing, and processing of organic grains, directly benefiting farmers and processors involved in the supply chain. These efficiencies will support the production of grist for a wider range of applications within the distilling and baking sectors. The project’s success will positively impact stakeholders by creating greater market access for organic grains and bolstering the local agricultural landscape, while enhancing the availability of milled grains for consumers and businesses alike.  Ultimately, this equipment investment represents a strategic move to meet growing market demands and establish Admiral Maltings as a prominent supplier of high-quality organic milled grains.

Project Summary: California Certified Organic Farmers (CCOF), Inc. has over fifty years of experience working with organic producers and is now the largest member-based organic agriculture organization in California, and owns the largest organic certification company in the U.S. The purpose of this grant is to improve and expand market access for small and underserved organic farmers. The three goals for this grant are: 1) to address two key obstacles restricting growth in organic sales: which are the lack of consumer clarity on what “organic” means and a perceived lack of consumer confidence in the seal; 2) to create market paths for small and underserved organic producers by linking them with buyers actively looking to source their products; and 3) to educate and provide farmers with tools to talk to consumers and buyers about organic. These goals will be achieved by launching a multi-channel marketing campaign, creating a marketing toolkit, marketing trainings for farmers, and updating and disseminating an organic sourcing directory to school and retail buyers. The expected outcomes of this project are that consumers and buyers will gain knowledge about organic products and that small and underserved producers will increase organic production to meet the increased demand through direct-market channels and buyer business transactions.
llm_summary: California Certified Organic Farmers (CCOF), Inc. is undertaking a project focused on expanding market access for small organic producers across California. The primary goal of this project is to address key obstacles limiting organic sales, specifically a lack of consumer understanding regarding the meaning of “organic” and a perceived absence of confidence in the certification seal, alongside creating market pathways for small organic producers by connecting them with buyers actively seeking to source their products. This initiative will be achieved through the launch of a multi-channel marketing campaign, the development of a comprehensive marketing toolkit, and the creation and dissemination of an updated organic sourcing directory targeted at school and retail buyers. The anticipated outcome of this project is that consumers will gain knowledge about organic products, and small organic producers will increase their production to meet heightened demand through direct-market channels and business transactions with established buyers. Ultimately, this project will support farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the organic agricultural sector. By improving consumer awareness and facilitating direct connections between producers and buyers, CCOF aims to strengthen the organic market and support the growth of California’s organic agriculture industry.

Project Summary: Straus Family Creamery, Inc. has over twenty-five years of experience processing raw organic dairy sourced from a network of farms in the Northern Bay Area region of California into value-added products. The goals of this grant proposal are to 1) Expand local dairy processing capacity and increase revenues for organic dairy farmers in the Northern Bay Area region of California 2) Help producers find solutions to rising expenses and improve their overall climate resiliency, 3) Support continued growth opportunity for organic dairy producers, and 4) Ensure opportunity for the next generation of organic dairy producers and, thereby, the future local organic dairy supply. To achieve these goals Straus Family Creamery will install new processing equipment, increasing yogurt and ice cream-making capacity by 200%. This expanded capacity will allow Straus Family Creamery to increase fluid milk purchases by over three million gallons per year at a 12.5% organic premium price to farmers. Straus Family Creamery will pursue national distribution for these products through existing key retail partnerships, increasing the value of organic yogurt and organic ice cream supply by $10.4 million. To further address the crisis facing regional organic dairy producers the business will offset the cost of creating Carbon Farm Plans for up to ten dairies in its network, contributing to a reduction of feed costs and a strengthening of climate resiliency for these farms. Straus Family Creamery will also work with Chico State University to provide education and technical assistance to dairy students interested in transitioning their family dairy to organic and or pursuing a job in organic dairy.
llm_summary: Straus Family Creamery, Inc. is undertaking a project to expand local dairy processing capacity and bolster the organic dairy supply within the Northern Bay Area region of California. This initiative will involve the installation of new processing equipment, dramatically increasing yogurt and ice cream-making capabilities by 200%, and will facilitate the purchase of over three million gallons of fluid milk annually from local organic dairy farmers at a 12.5% premium price. Straus Family Creamery intends to pursue national distribution channels for its expanded product line of organic yogurt and organic ice cream, projecting an increase in the value of these supplies to approximately $10.4 million. A key component of this project is the development of Carbon Farm Plans for up to ten dairies within the Creamery’s network, designed to offset the cost of feed reduction and thereby strengthen the resilience of these farms. Furthermore, Straus Family Creamery will collaborate with Chico State University to provide technical assistance to dairy students interested in transitioning their family dairy operations to organic production or pursuing employment within the organic dairy sector. The anticipated outcomes of this project include an amplified supply of organic dairy products available to consumers, increased revenues for participating farmers, and a strengthened local organic dairy market. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass organic dairy farmers, processors, and the wider consumer base seeking high-quality organic products. This project directly supports the economic viability of organic dairy operations and the long-term sustainability of the regional organic dairy supply chain.

Project Summary: Despite having a high density of small farms, Southern California significantly lacks certified organic processing facilities, an issue that negatively affects small and underserved farms that rely on timeconsuming, costly hand labor to process and add value to their organic commodities. To address this 9 bottleneck, The Ecology Center (TEC) proposes to expand its processing and distribution capacity for valueadded products (VAP) made from organic corn, legumes, and fruit, by providing a shared processing service to facilitate market access for small organic farms. Project activities include 1) renovating its processing warehouse to accommodate new equipment for high-demand VAP including jams, tortillas, dried beans, and sauces, 2) expanding partnerships to benefit at least 15 organic farms, and 3) expanding TEC’s current DTC sales model that reaches 70,000 consumers to larger channels, by leveraging partners’ channels and relationships with regional groceries. This project will increase processing by 80,000 lbs. of organic corn, legumes, and fruit processed into 372,000 units of organic VAP. It will reach at least 40,000 more repeat consumers, influencing up to 400,000 new consumers by the addition of 10 or more sales channels. This project will facilitate market access for 15 or more Southern Californian organic producers (at least 10 of which are small, beginner, or underserved farms). It will also increase their profitability with access to processing equipment and increase consumption of locally made organic products–inducing approximately $2.2 million in sales by the project’s third year.
llm_summary: The Ecology Center (TEC) proposes a project to address a critical need within Southern California’s agricultural sector by expanding its processing and distribution capacity for value-added products (VAPs) derived from organic corn, legumes, and fruit. This project will involve renovating TEC’s processing warehouse to accommodate new equipment for the production of high-demand VAPs, including jams, tortillas, dried beans, and sauces. TEC anticipates increasing processing by 80,000 pounds of these commodities, resulting in the creation of 372,000 units of organic VAPs. The project aims to benefit at least 15 Southern Californian organic farms, with a priority on supporting small, beginning, or nascent operations, ultimately reaching and influencing an additional 40,000 repeat consumers and potentially up to 400,000 new consumers through the leveraging of expanded sales channels. These efforts will support farmers by providing access to processing equipment and facilitate approximately $2.2 million in sales within the third year of the project. The expanded reach of TEC’s direct-to-consumer sales model will support increased consumption of locally made organic products, benefiting stakeholders across the supply chain, including processors and regional grocery partners.

Project Summary: Turning Green continues integrating local, organic food into California’s K-12 school meal programs. This project will leverage the massive purchasing scale of the school food sector to grow the organic supply chain by bringing together school food networks, small disadvantaged organic farmers, and local agricultural support organizations. The project will provide added training and technical support to school food service teams and organic farmers to align planning, implementation, logistics, and metrics to grow the sale of organic products to schools in California. Given that much of the current food purchased and served in schools is not organic, this segment is an attractive and burgeoning opportunity to expand the organic marketplace. Turning Green has facilitated and supported procurement and has served fresh, local, organic, nutritious food in K-12 schools. In 2020/21, during the pandemic, they worked with a local school district of 28,000 students to transition its entire meal program to 100% organic with 41 new vendors, resulting in over $17 million that flowed into the organic supply chain. Since then, Turning Green has partnered with seven more school districts to spur demand and enlist support from many small organic farmers to grow supply. Working with producers and school districts, Turning Green identifies gaps and market barriers while creating innovative systemic solutions for crop planning, delivering, and consuming high-quality goods. An experienced team is equipped to expand their work in building the organic market with school food programs. Leveraging local agricultural support organizations and school food networks, the project will provide added training and technical support to school food service teams and small disadvantaged farmers to align planning, implementation, logistics, and metrics to meet school requirements.
llm_summary: Turning Green is undertaking a project to integrate local, organic food into California’s K-12 school meal programs, leveraging the significant purchasing power of the school food sector to expand the organic supply chain. This initiative will connect school food networks with small, disadvantaged organic farmers and local agricultural support organizations, focusing on the procurement of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in the volume of organic products supplied to schools, with the potential to generate over $17 million in revenue for organic producers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic agricultural commodities, as well as the consumers – the students – who will ultimately benefit from access to fresh, local, organic food within the K-12 school meal program. Turning Green has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of this approach, having partnered with seven additional school districts since 2020/21, where they facilitated the transition of a 28,000-student school district’s entire meal program to 100% organic, utilizing 41 new vendors and stimulating considerable growth in the organic supply chain. This project aims to address a critical need for expanded market pathways for domestically produced organic agricultural products, ultimately driving greater demand and supporting the development of a robust organic food system within the school sector.

Project Summary: Ferreira & Son Dairy has been certified organic since 2007 and became certified grass fed in 2016. Historic drought and increasing feed costs in recent years have forced local dairies to make decisions about the future of their generational businesses. In response to these industry and climate -based challenges, Ferreira & Son Dairy has embarked on a five-year plan to remain self-sufficient by expanding and diversifying production, taking over their own distribution thereby cutting the costs of middle distributors. During the first year, 2021-2022, Ferriera & Son Dairy completed the first phase of this expansion, building Humboldt County’s first truly local milk processing and bottling plant. The milk is processed right from the tank, bottled into glass bottles, then distributed directly to local stores. The next phase of the project is the 11 acquisition of equipment to expand production. The funds from this opportunity will enable the dairy to purchase equipment that will quadruple production from 300 to 2000 gallons per week of milk with diversified fats percentages that can be used to develop, produce and distribute other products that will generate more income for the dairy and increase growth of the market for organic products overall in the local economy.
llm_summary: Ferreira & Son Dairy has embarked on a five-year plan to ensure self-sufficiency through expansion and production diversification, directly addressing the challenges posed by recent industry pressures and feed costs. This project will see the construction of Humboldt County’s first local milk processing and bottling plant, utilizing equipment that is anticipated to quadruple weekly milk production from 300 to 2000 gallons. The dairy’s objective is to transform its operations, beginning with the immediate processing of milk from the tank, followed by bottling into glass bottles and direct distribution to local stores, thereby eliminating reliance on middle distributors and controlling costs. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is a significant increase in the volume of milk produced, supporting the development of a broader range of products with varied fat percentages, ultimately generating additional income for the dairy and stimulating growth within the local market for organic goods. This expanded capacity will benefit farmers and ranchers who supply the dairy, as well as consumers seeking locally sourced organic products. The project’s success will strengthen the economic viability of Ferreira & Son Dairy, providing stability for its operations and supporting the growth of the organic products market within the surrounding region. The dairy’s expanded production will create a greater supply of organic milk, benefitting processors and retailers alike, and contributing to the overall economic growth of the local community.

Project Summary: Alexandre Dairy (the “Dairy”), is the 1st Certified “Regenerative” US organic dairy, producing 100% A2/A2, grass-based milk, and organic hay and silage, is seeking funding to replace antiquated milk collection, cooling, and storage equipment and to purchase post-harvest hay collection equipment to increase domestic supply chain capacity and facilitate expanded market development. As a vertically integrated company, the Dairy supplies organic milk to Alexandre Family Creamery (“AFC”) for processing into Alexandre Family Farm (“AFF”) branded, as well as co-packaged, products. Nationwide demand for organic, A2/A2 grass-based, certified regenerative milk has significantly increased but the outdated raw dairy milk collection equipment cannot keep up with weekly demand and projected brand growth, and the Dairy’s ailing harvest equipment curtails its ability to collect and store feeds within a short harvest season. The Dairy currently produces 55% of its organic livestock forage annually and can increase production by 10- 15% simply by upgrading equipment, helping to reduce regional pressure on organic livestock forages. Investment in new equipment supporting milk collection/storage, post-harvest hay/silage processing, and transport to provide on-farm resiliency, will support the Dairy’s investment in national market penetration of its organic farm-gate products. The project would benefit Pavel’s Yogurt Company and Kefir Lab, which AFC co-packs for and the Farm sells organic raw dairy, Rumiano Cheese, which the Dairy supplies with 25% of its weekly organic milk volume, and Humboldt Creamery which also uses 22% of the Dairy’s production to make organic fluid milk, ice cream and milk powder. In addition, the West Coast’s organic, pasture based dairy producers which support 85% of California’s organic fluid production will benefit from the Dairy’s brand penetration into new and expanded regions educating consumers about the importance of California climate friendly milk, innovative on farm certifications that add margin, and models for small organic family farm expansion and innovation focused on genetics, grass-fed and flash grazing practices.
llm_summary: Alexandre Dairy is seeking funding to modernize its raw dairy milk collection, cooling, and storage equipment, alongside purchasing post-harvest hay collection equipment, with the primary purpose of increasing domestic supply chain capacity and facilitating expanded market development for its organic products. This investment will encompass the acquisition of new equipment to support enhanced milk handling processes, optimized storage capabilities, and the efficient collection and preservation of hay and silage. Anticipated outcomes include a 10-15% increase in annual organic livestock forage production, directly benefiting farmers and ranchers involved in organic dairy operations. The project will support a range of stakeholders, including processors like Pavel’s Yogurt Company and Kefir Lab, as well as manufacturers such as Rumiano Cheese and Humboldt Creamery, who utilize the Dairy’s organic milk supply. Furthermore, the upgraded operations will bolster the Dairy’s ability to penetrate new regional markets, educating consumers about the value of California’s organic milk production and innovative on-farm certifications. The successful completion of this project will positively impact the broader organic dairy sector, particularly West Coast organic pasture-based dairy producers, by promoting the adoption of on-farm strategies and strengthening the supply chain for organic fluid milk, ice cream, and milk powder.

Project Summary: The project proposes a planning and implementation process for the development of a permanent certified organic, dry bean processing facility located in Olathe, Colorado. The facility will provide a certified organic process for the cleaning of dry beans received directly from field harvesting and enable versatile packaging of dry beans. The planning process will consist of completing Technical and Economic Feasibility analyses and Marketing and Business Plans for such a facility. The first goal is to optimize the technical aspects of processing to ensure efficiency and increase capacity in a certified organic dry bean cleaning and packaging facility. This will provide a finished product, packaged in various weights, which accommodate market needs and consumer demand. The project will develop a Marketing and Business plan to optimize economic benefits and purchase of equipment to implement a facility. Project is expected to improve access for producers in the Western Slope to sell products into regional and national organic dry bean markets, provide incentives to expand the volume and varieties of organic dry beans grown in these regions, and increase regional organic dry bean sourcing accessibility for buyers and consumers.
llm_summary: The Olathe Dry Bean Facility project proposes the development of a permanent, certified organic dry bean processing facility located in Olathe, Colorado, designed to optimize the cleaning and packaging of dry beans. This project will encompass the completion of Technical and Economic Feasibility analyses alongside a Marketing and Business Plan, ultimately guiding the purchase and implementation of equipment necessary to establish a fully operational facility. The anticipated outcomes of this project include the creation of a facility capable of processing beans from direct harvesting, enabling versatile packaging options in various weights to meet market demands and consumer preferences. This facility will significantly improve access for farmers in the Western Slope to sell their products into regional and national organic dry bean markets, incentivizing increased volumes and a broader range of organic dry bean varieties cultivated in these regions. The project will increase regional accessibility for buyers and consumers seeking organic dry bean sourcing. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and stakeholders involved in the organic dry bean supply chain, as well as consumers who desire access to these products. The facility will facilitate the increased production and availability of organic dry beans, contributing to a strengthened market position for regional producers and expanding consumer choices.

Project Summary: In 2022, a farm partner company received a grant to purchase equipment to turn organic peaches into puree that could be used in food service and production of beverages and value-added foods. The goal was 12 to make Colorado’s celebrated peaches available year-round. An additional goal was to upcycle waste peaches. Tons of peaches go to waste each year because of minor imperfections or because they are too ripe to travel through traditional distribution channels. This summer, that company began puree production for restaurants, breweries, and other food producers. This project includes two goals; 1) to market this local resource year-round in ways that honor the goodness and flavor of the fruit and 2) to celebrate this local resource within the community, in ways that can nourish ALL community members. One solution is to package the puree in squeeze popsicles that are shelf-stable, to be frozen on-demand. The joy of a squeeze popsicle is a true celebration of local flavors. The plan is to keep the fruit content near 100 percent. This means that these organic popsicles will be healthful for everyone. This equipment grant will allow Honey Rock to purchase a popsicle machine, and supporting equipment, to make delicious, safely-produced servings of fruit. This will help keep costs down and make these items affordable for distribution to community schools, hospitals, and the food bank. This product is in line with the farm’s initiatives to reduce food waste by upcycling peaches to 1) adopt the most earth-friendly practices, 2) level the farm’s working hours by adding off-season work to solve local production and storage problems that keep local institutions from serving more local fruit, and 3) bring greater awareness to and appreciation of local agricultural resources.
llm_summary: Honey Rock Farm initiated a project in 2022 with a grant to produce organic peach puree for a range of applications, including food service and beverage production, with the primary goal of making Colorado’s celebrated peaches available year-round. This project involves the purchase of specialized equipment, specifically a popsicle machine and associated supporting equipment, to facilitate this production. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a marketable product that will reduce peach waste and provide a healthful option for consumers. The project will primarily benefit farmers, processors, and other stakeholders by offering a new outlet for their organic peach harvest. The farm intends to make the puree available to community schools, hospitals, and a food bank, assisting those organizations in providing local fruit options. Honey Rock Farm plans to package the puree in shelf-stable, on-demand frozen popsicles, maintaining a near 100% fruit content, and this product will reduce peach waste by upcycling the fruit. The farm’s initiatives align with efforts to reduce waste and address local production and storage challenges, ultimately increasing the availability of locally sourced agricultural resources to the community.

Project Summary: By working with several high-influence partners in the organic food space, the Colorado Grain Chain (CGC) will enhance market opportunities for producers, processors, and value-added product makers of organic grain for human consumption. Although grains make up an average of 30-50% of dietary intake, the organic grain market for human consumption is relatively limited, with little emphasis on local sourcing. Since the inception of the Colorado Grain Chain in 2019, the non-profit organization's mission has been to grow and connect a community-centered grain economy in the state of Colorado. This work involves connecting the membership base of 50+ Business and Consumer Members to educational and marketing resources, partners, and technical assistance. CGC’s membership base ranges from farmers, processors (millers and maltsters), to artisanal makers (bakers, brewers, distillers, chefs), food hubs, and institutions. The Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) will allow Colorado Grain Chain to support stakeholders in the grain supply chain through the promotion of organic grains in value-added marketplaces in alignment with the Colorado Grown Grains marketing initiative, while building off and expanding current program models to organic grains. Specifically, the project seeks to support connections through the grain supply chain that a) incentivize the cultivation of diverse organic grains through Microgrants for small businesses/farms, b) enhance distribution of organic grains through increased visibility in value-added market channels, and c) increase market awareness and demand for locally sourced, food-grade, organic grain through event coordination and the continuation of the Colorado Grown Grains co-brand strategy.
llm_summary: Colorado Grain Chain will enhance market opportunities for farmers, processors, and value-added product makers of organic grain for human consumption through the Organic Market Development Grant. This project aims to support stakeholders across the grain supply chain, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and value-added product manufacturers, by incentivizing the cultivation of diverse organic grains via Microgrants and expanding visibility of these grains in value-added market channels, aligning with the Colorado Grown Grains co-brand strategy. Specifically, the project seeks to increase market awareness and demand for locally sourced, food-grade, organic grain, ultimately benefiting consumers who seek these products. The Colorado Grain Chain will achieve this through a multi-faceted approach focused on connecting members, promoting local grains, and increasing their presence in markets. This initiative will facilitate the growth of a community-centered grain economy within Colorado by supporting the production and distribution of organic grains and expanding access to these products for consumers. The overall anticipated outcome is a strengthened local grain supply chain and a greater number of stakeholders involved in the production and sale of organic grains within the state.

Project Summary: Hobbs Meyer, LLC DBA Pueblo Seed Food Co (Pueblo Seed) is a family farm located in Southwestern Colorado. The farm has been certified organic since 2001 by the Colorado Department of Agriculture and specializes in open pollinated vegetable seeds, varietal garlic, and heritage grains and legumes on 30 acres. This project will allow Pueblo Seed to purchase equipment to increase capacity in its facility to scale up processing and develop new products from these crops for seed feed and food markets. During the COVID19 pandemic, the farm began producing a line of 7 value-added grain products and working towards opening a seed and bakehouse. In 2021, the farm purchased a 5300-square foot commercial building in downtown Cortez. In 2022-2023, the farm purchased a food grade seed cleaning line and other grain processing equipment for making products and providing seed cleaning services to partner growers. During 2023, the farm increased the seed of 10 species of drought and heat tolerant grains and legumes. Organic drought hardy heritage grains and cover crops, in particular, are in extremely short supply in the U.S. (Hubbard et al., 2022). Pueblo Seed’s goal is to become a central organic supplier of cowpeas, tepary beans, finger millets, pearl millets, amaranths, grain sorghums, culinary ryes, culinary barleys, select wheat, and flour maize. The business will utilize its existing seed customer list and long-term relationships with national seed companies to increase the seed market and work through food hubs, food pantries, and institutions to increase food market share.
llm_summary: Hobbs Meyer, LLC DBA Pueblo Seed Food Co (Pueblo Seed) is undertaking a project to significantly expand its processing capabilities and product offerings, primarily focused on increasing capacity within its newly acquired commercial facility in downtown Cortez, Colorado. This initiative involves the purchase of key equipment, including a food grade seed cleaning line and other grain processing machinery, enabling the farm to produce a wider range of value-added grain products and provide seed cleaning services to partner growers. Pueblo Seed’s ambition is to become a central supplier of specific organic grains and legumes, particularly focusing on cowpeas, tepary beans, finger millets, pearl millets, amaranths, grain sorghums, culinary ryes, culinary barleys, select wheat, and flour maize, responding to a recognized need within the market. The anticipated outcome of this project is to broaden the range of organic seeds and grains available, supporting farmers and processors seeking these specialized crops. By leveraging its existing customer base and relationships with national seed companies, alongside distribution through food hubs and institutions, Pueblo Seed aims to increase its market share and benefit stakeholders throughout the agricultural supply chain. This project directly supports the production of drought and heat-tolerant grains and legumes, a critical area of need in the U.S. agricultural sector, and will ultimately contribute to improved access for consumers to these vital crops.

Project Summary: Consumer awareness about Connecticut’s certified organic producers and handlers is largely unknown. The Connecticut Department of Agriculture will use these grant funds to increase market access for certified organic producers, producers transitioning to organic farming, and certified organic handlers in Connecticut by coordinating with Transition to Organic Partnership (TOPP) partners, including the University of Connecticut (UConn) Extension and the Connecticut Northeast Organic Farming Association (CT NOFA). The goal of this project is to strengthen new and emerging markets, strengthen farm to institution market channels, increase producer and handler knowledge and skills to market their organic products, and foster consumer education to increase demand for organic products. Proposed goals will be accomplished by 1) evaluating the current market for CT Grown organic products in CT to understand consumers’ perceptions and understanding and to evaluate areas for growth and improved market access; 2) examining 14 opportunities for CT Grown organic product sales specifically for farm-to-institution; 3) implementing new communication strategies to reach consumers in the state to increase awareness and highlight CT Grown organic products and producers (which considers the information gained through the market evaluation), and 4) developing and conducting a workshop series for transitioning and certified organic producers and handlers to implement new marketing strategies and capitalize on areas for improvement identified by the results of marketing research.
llm_summary: The Connecticut Department of Agriculture will undertake a project to significantly increase market access for certified organic producers, producers transitioning to organic farming, and certified organic handlers within the state. This initiative aims to strengthen new and emerging markets, bolster farm-to-institution channels, and elevate producer and handler knowledge and skills related to marketing their organic products. The project will accomplish this through a comprehensive four-part approach: first, a thorough evaluation of the current market for Connecticut Grown organic products will be conducted to assess consumer perceptions and identify areas for growth; second, a detailed examination of fourteen specific opportunities for CT Grown organic product sales focused on farm-to-institution channels will be undertaken; third, new communication strategies will be implemented to raise awareness of CT Grown organic products and producers among consumers; and fourth, a workshop series will be developed and delivered to producers and handlers, utilizing insights from the market evaluation to refine marketing approaches. The anticipated outcomes of this project include an expanded range of market opportunities for Connecticut’s organic sector, increased consumer demand for organically produced goods, and enhanced operational capabilities for farmers, ranchers, and processors. This project directly benefits farmers and ranchers seeking to expand their customer base, as well as processors involved in the handling and production of organic commodities. Ultimately, the project seeks to support stakeholders throughout the organic supply chain, leading to greater availability and consumption of domestically produced organic agricultural products.

Project Summary: The Latino Farmers Association’s (LFA) project aims to foster equitable participation in the organic marketplace for historically underserved and socially disadvantaged farmers and ranchers, veterans, and beginning farmers, with a concerted effort to combat food deserts in the District of Columbia, Maryland, and Virginia. To do so, LFA will pursue four key objectives. First, LFA will expand the organic vendor capacity of the Van Ness Farmers Market, in the District of Columbia, by facilitating a transition to an exclusively organic market and obtaining organic certifications for vendors via partnerships with the Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP) Regional Lead, Pennsylvania Certified Organic, and the Organic Trade Association. Second, LFA will open three new organic farmers markets in healthy food priority areas in the District of Columbia and one in Southwest Virginia. Third, the association will develop a scalable Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) producer-to-consumer system supported by a Virtual Marketplace, which will connect market vendors with individual and institutional consumers. LFA will develop a diversified marketing strategy to build robust relationships with institutional buyers, distributors, grocery stores, and food co-ops. Finally, LFA will enhance market accessibility for producers by acquiring one box truck, one mobile market, and one delivery van. This will enable LFA to increase the scale and variety of product offerings that are now limited by transport and storage constraints. By providing an enhanced distribution process that reduces the cost of transport to market and includes eggs, meat, dairy and value-added products, LFA will diversify the producers’ income streams and cash flow, while lowering the collective carbon footprint.
llm_summary: The Latino Farmers Association’s project is designed to expand access to organic agricultural products and establish new market channels for farmers and ranchers. This initiative will encompass several key activities, including the transformation of the Van Ness Farmers Market in Washington, D.C., into an exclusively organic market, facilitated through partnerships with the Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP) Regional Lead, Pennsylvania Certified Organic, and the Organic Trade Association. Furthermore, the association will establish three new organic farmers markets in designated healthy food priority areas within the District of Columbia and one in Southwest Virginia, alongside the development of a scalable Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) producer-to-consumer system supported by a Virtual Marketplace. To support this expansion, the Latino Farmers Association will acquire one box truck, one mobile market, and one delivery van, enhancing the ability of farmers and ranchers to transport and distribute their goods. These vehicles will enable a wider variety of product offerings, including eggs, meat, dairy, and value-added products, ultimately increasing the income streams and cash flow for these producers. The anticipated outcome is to create new market opportunities for farmers and ranchers and to increase the availability of organic agricultural commodities for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic goods. This expansion of market access will address the need for additional pathways to support producers and stimulate demand for domestically produced organic agricultural products.

Project Summary: Little Sesame will expand the domestic certified organic chickpea market by increasing aggregation, processing, and distribution of its consumer-packaged line of hummus while simultaneously growing consumer demand through enhanced sales and marketing capacity. Over the past several years, droughts, flooding, and war in top chickpea-producing countries have led to an increased market demand for domestically grown chickpeas. That, paired with a growing interest in plant-based foods that rely on chickpeas and other legumes, creates a unique opportunity for organic chickpea producers in the United States. Yet, the market remains underdeveloped. Northern Plains farmers in the U.S. have difficulty finding direct sales relationships for chickpeas, a crop abundantly grown in rotation with wheat due to its soilbuilding properties. By achieving SQF certification, investing in manufacturing improvements, and implementing a shopper, trade, and field marketing program, Little Sesame will leverage market demand and create a much-needed direct market for 10 domestic chickpea farmers, purchasing 800,000 pounds of chickpeas annually across 2,000 production acres. Marketing efforts targeted at distributors, retailers, grocery stores, and household consumers will highlight the value of choosing products sourced from domestically grown certified organic chickpea growers and bring increased opportunities for certified organic producers for years to come.
llm_summary: Little Sesame is undertaking a project to expand the domestic certified organic chickpea market by increasing aggregation, processing, and distribution of its consumer-packaged line of hummus, a venture that will directly benefit farmers and consumers alike. This initiative will involve the purchase of 800,000 pounds of chickpeas annually, sourced from 2,000 production acres cultivated by ten domestic chickpea farmers, and the implementation of SQF certification alongside significant manufacturing improvements. The core objective is to create a much-needed direct market for these chickpeas, supporting processors and other stakeholders within the agricultural supply chain. The anticipated outcomes include the establishment of a robust domestic supply of certified organic chickpeas, which will then be distributed through a comprehensive marketing program targeting distributors, retailers, grocery stores, and household consumers. This marketing effort will highlight the value proposition of choosing products sourced from domestically grown certified organic chickpea growers, ultimately boosting demand and creating long-term opportunities for certified organic producers. The project’s success will be measured by increased market access for these farmers and the enhanced availability of certified organic chickpeas to consumers seeking plant-based food options. Through this focused approach, Little Sesame aims to solidify its position as a key player in the organic chickpea market, providing a viable pathway for growers and meeting consumer demand for high-quality, domestically sourced ingredients.

Project Summary: The project will stimulate the demand for and increase the sales of organic products by promoting the science-backed benefits of USDA certified organic products and farming to consumers. Organic is an umbrella term that addresses several individual product claims; however, consumers remain confused about the wholistic requirements of the USDA organic label and how they translate to benefits for people and the planet. By providing consumers with access to more credible information about what organic production and processing means and the benefits it provides, consumption of organic will increase. This joint project by The Organic Center and the Organic Trade Association (OTA owns the TOC) will be done in collaboration with Organic Voices and an Industry Advisory Committee (including TOPP regional leads) to develop fresh creative content on the regulatory and science-based environmental, animal, and human benefits of organic. Targeted content that motivates consumers to purchase pinpointed products like organic dairy, grain, and fiber will be prioritized. The creative content will be promoted through a full-scale integrated marketing campaign leveraging TOC and Organic Voices' existing consumer networks and paid advertising. Targeted efforts will ensure that promotion reaches beyond the mainstream organic markets into regions and communities where organic production is not already thriving. The Industry Advisory Committee will include partners from underserved communities and pinpointed markets to ensure the 16 creative and promotional campaign meets industry needs and expectations. The project will culminate by sharing learnings and successes in the creation of effective organic consumer marketing strategies, content, and messaging with the organic industry at large to increase their return on investment for future marketing opportunities. Printed copies of the final report will be disseminated to all addresses listed in the Organic Integrity Database (approximately 27,400 addresses), which includes around 19,000 producers (livestock and crop scopes) and 8,400 buyers (handler scopes).
llm_summary: The Organic Center, in collaboration with the Organic Trade Association, Organic Voices, and an Industry Advisory Committee, is undertaking a project designed to stimulate demand and increase sales of organic products by providing consumers with credible information regarding USDA certified organic production and processing. This initiative will focus on developing fresh, creative content that clearly communicates the regulatory and science-backed environmental, animal, and human benefits of organic farming and processing, with particular emphasis on pinpointed products such as organic dairy, grain, and fiber. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased consumption of these targeted organic products among farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders. The project will leverage existing consumer networks and paid advertising through the established channels of The Organic Center and Organic Voices to reach consumers in both mainstream and emerging organic markets. The Industry Advisory Committee, comprised of regional leads, will ensure the campaign’s relevance to the needs of producers and buyers. The project will culminate in the sharing of learnings and successful strategies, allowing the organic industry to optimize their marketing investments for future opportunities. Final project results will be disseminated to approximately 27,400 addresses, including roughly 19,000 producers and 8,400 buyers, to facilitate expansion of organic markets.

Project Summary: New Universe Food, LLC is a small business committed to promoting a healthier lifestyle by selling organic products. This grant will allow New Universe Food to purchase a much-needed refrigerated delivery van, allowing fulfillment of the promise to deliver fresh, high-quality organic products to a larger customer base along with supplying underserved communities who lack access to healthy, organic food. This van will further help them source organic produce from local and out of state organic growers and vendors that they can process as well as deliver to markets. The purpose of acquiring a refrigerated van allows New Universe Food to fulfill the promise of delivering fresh, high-quality organic products, and will also enable to reach a larger customer base. The company will be able to expand market reach and promote organic products by traveling to (and serving at) farmers markets, a range of food expos, community bazaars and fairs. The van will also be used for picking up organic fruits, vegetables and grains from other farms and vendors to process at the factory and to deliver to markets.
llm_summary: New Universe Food, LLC is undertaking a vital project to expand access to fresh, high-quality organic products, driven by a commitment to promoting healthier lifestyles. This project will result in the acquisition of a refrigerated delivery van, a critical investment designed to facilitate the efficient sourcing, processing, and distribution of organic produce. Specifically, the van will enable New Universe Food to connect with local and out-of-state organic growers and vendors, procuring a diverse range of fruits, vegetables, and grains for processing and subsequent delivery to markets and participating in events such as farmers markets and food expos. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is a significantly broadened market reach, allowing New Universe Food to serve a larger customer base and provide access to organic ingredients for processors and manufacturers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders within the organic food supply chain, as well as consumers seeking access to fresh, organic goods. The expanded distribution capabilities will allow New Universe Food to meet increased demand and strengthen relationships with key partners. Ultimately, the project aims to improve the availability of organic products and support the growth of the organic food sector.

Project Summary: The goal of this project is to create a new market and enhance the value of certified organic peanuts produced and processed in Georgia. The project will forge a new partnership between the Georgia Organic Peanut Association, a farmer-owned marketing cooperative, and Oliver Oil Company, a small family-owned processor of cold-pressed culinary oil.
