Together, they will acquire parallel processing equipment that will enable, for the first time in the Southeast, the production of Certified Organic peanut oil by expanding processing capacity and preventing commingling of organic and non-organic products. This new enterprise 17 will be supported by a joint marketing campaign to stimulate demand. As a result of the project, one processing facility and one storage facility will obtain organic certification for the first time, fostering a new local supply chain for Certified Organic commodities. Marketing through the Georgia Organic Peanut Association, farmers will increase the production, processing, and sales of Certified Organic peanuts grown in the region by 50%. The project will have a beneficial financial effect on no fewer than 15 farmers in the Southeast, including two beginning farmers and two socially disadvantaged producers, and create one new job.
llm_summary: The Georgia Organic Peanut Association, in partnership with Oliver Oil Company, is undertaking a project to establish a new market for certified organic peanuts produced in Georgia and to create the first certified organic peanut oil within the Southeast. This initiative will involve the acquisition of parallel processing equipment, enabling the simultaneous processing of organic and non-organic peanuts, thereby preventing contamination and expanding processing capacity. The anticipated outcome of this project is a significant increase in the production, processing, and sales of certified organic peanuts by farmers in the region, with an expected rise of 50% driven by a joint marketing campaign spearheaded by the Georgia Organic Peanut Association. This project will positively impact at least fifteen farmers across the Southeast, including two beginning farmers and two socially disadvantaged producers, contributing to increased market access and revenue streams. Furthermore, the project will create one new job within the processing sector. The Georgia Organic Peanut Association and Oliver Oil Company will work together to certify one processing facility and one storage facility for the first time, facilitating the development of a new local supply chain for certified organic commodities. The expected results will benefit farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking high-quality, certified organic peanut products. This collaborative effort is designed to stimulate demand and support the growth of the certified organic peanut industry in the Southeast.

Project Summary: Our goal is to increase access to certified organic transplants and meet the demand of local certified and practicing organic farmers, local non-profits supporting community gardens and urban farms, and educational non-profits serving the Metro Atlanta area. Certified-organic transplants are essential to maximizing vegetable production and overall profitability for organic vegetable producers. The closest regional supplier is 250 miles away and has become inconsistent after being purchased by a national company. Many farmers in the region decreased or limited their production due to the uncertainty this caused. Increasing processing to meet the growing demand from regional organic producers means purchasing pot-filling, media-mixing, and other propagation tools that will increase Love is Love’s capacity to produce and deliver certified organic transplants. In addition, it will also increase material-handling capacity while decreasing costs and production variables to ensure a consistent and sustainable product for the organic vegetable farmers in the region. This equipment allows Love is Love to expand and secure its capacity to produce organic transplant so that the local farmers, educators, and non-profits can focus on what they do best growing, educating, and supporting local, organic food.
llm_summary: Love is Love’s project aims to significantly increase access to certified organic transplants, directly addressing a critical need within the Metro Atlanta region. The core of this initiative involves the strategic purchase of equipment necessary to substantially expand processing capabilities, specifically focusing on pot-filling and media-mixing systems. This expansion will directly translate to a heightened capacity for Love is Love to produce and deliver a consistent supply of certified organic transplants, a vital component for maximizing vegetable production among local farmers. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened supply chain for organic vegetable producers, enabling greater profitability and increased yields. These enhanced operations will support a range of stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and non-profit organizations supporting community gardens and educational institutions. By securing a reliable source of certified organic transplants, Love is Love will empower these groups to focus on their core activities: cultivating, educating, and supporting the local food system. Ultimately, this project seeks to bolster the capacity for producing certified organic transplants, providing a foundational element for increased agricultural output and economic stability within the Metro Atlanta region.

Project Summary: The Big Island Organic Packaging Project will increase the packaging efficiency and capacity of Hawaii’s organic producers of macadamia nuts and other organic agricultural products in Hawaii. Additionally, the project will allow for Island Harvest to offer co-manufacturing services to other organic producers. The main goal of the project is to purchase and install an automated packaging system with the capacity to pack up to 1800 pouches of organic macadamia nuts per hour. Currently, there are limited and inefficient 18 options for organic producers to package their products, and the installation of packaging equipment will help to alleviate this bottleneck and allow for the growth of the market for organic agricultural products. The increased capacity of packaging will allow Hawaii‘s organic producers to compete with non-organic consumer packaged goods, in online and in-store outlets, throughout Hawaii and the United States. This will improve the availability of organic products to consumers and reduce the cost for Hawaii’s organic producers to bring their product to market.
llm_summary: The Big Island Organic Packaging Project aims to significantly enhance the packaging capabilities for Hawaii’s organic macadamia nut and other organic agricultural product producers. This project will involve the purchase and installation of a state-of-the-art, automated packaging system designed to increase production capacity to a substantial 1800 pouches of organic macadamia nuts per hour. This enhanced system will provide a critical solution to the existing limitations in packaging options currently available to farmers and processors, addressing a key bottleneck within the organic agricultural sector. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial improvement in the ability of Hawaii’s organic producers to compete effectively within both online and retail channels throughout Hawaii and the United States. By increasing production volume, the project will facilitate greater availability of these organic products to consumers, while simultaneously reducing the expenses associated with bringing organic agricultural commodities to market. This will benefit farmers and processors by expanding market access and bolstering their competitiveness. Ultimately, the project will support the growth of the overall organic agricultural market and provide consumers with a wider selection of organic products. The project’s success will contribute to a strengthened position for Hawaii’s organic producers within the broader consumer packaged goods landscape.

Project Summary: Only two dairies remain in Hawaii, and one plans to close, meaning Hawaii could end up importing all its milk. Neither of these dairies produces or distributes organic A2 milk. This raises concerns about Hawaii’s reliance on imported milk. Kula Organic A2 (KOA) Micro-Dairy is a solution for Maui residents. KOA will produce organic A2 milk, cheese, yogurt, and kefir, a fermented milk drink, cultured from kefir grains -- healthy options currently unavailable. KOA can produce up to 20 gallons of A2 milk daily developing a domestic market for organic A2 dairy. Most of Maui’s milk is A1 and imported, emphasizing the need for locally produced, economical, and environmentally sustainable dairy. The Micro-Dairy is operated by Hawaii Sustainable Farms' (HSF). The equipment will help Hawaii Sustainable Farms (HSF) to meet its goal to open and operate an organic, A2 micro-dairy on Maui, hire locally, distribute locally, and create new markets for organic A2 dairy on the island. HSF practices sustainable farming methods and is implementing its second USDA conservation plan. KOA aligns with growing interest in A2 milk and its potential health benefits. KOA Micro-Dairy will be the only provider of organic A2 milk in Hawaii.
llm_summary: Kula Organic A2 (KOA) Micro-Dairy is a project designed to establish a domestic supply of organic A2 milk on Maui, addressing a critical need within the island’s dairy market. The project involves the construction and operation of a micro-dairy facility, utilizing specialized equipment to produce a range of dairy products, including organic A2 milk, cheese, yogurt, and kefir, all cultured using kefir grains. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a local market for these products, reducing Hawaii’s reliance on imported dairy and offering consumers healthier options currently unavailable. This micro-dairy, operated by Hawaii Sustainable Farms (HSF), will benefit farmers and processors by providing a new sales channel for their products, and will provide consumers with access to a premium dairy product. The project aims to increase the availability of organic A2 milk on Maui, supporting the agricultural economy and creating new market opportunities for dairy producers. Ultimately, this initiative will enhance the overall local agricultural sector and contribute to a more resilient and sustainable food system for the island’s residents and stakeholders.

Project Summary: Symbrosia’s SeaGraze, a natural seaweed feed additive, reduces enteric methane emissions by over 80%, earning it recognition as the seaweed that could save the planet. USDA Organic certified, it provides unmatched value to ranchers and the environment. Cultivated in Kona, Hawaii, the fast-growing seaweed is processed into pellets, benefiting ranchers across the United States. This funding offers a unique opportunity for Symbrosia to advance its mission of reducing livestock methane emissions and promoting sustainability by increasing organic feed production. The goal is to expand post-harvest processing capacity by over 1600% , improving the market availability of domestically produced organic products. The funding will drive investment in expanded processing capacity, capturing a larger share of the organic feed supplement market. A targeted marketing initiative will attract more organic producers, offering a feed supplement that reduces greenhouse gases, saves on carbon credits for large-scale cattle ranching, and addresses social pressure on the cattle industry. This project will enhance the accessibility and market positioning of organic feed additives, placing the United States at the forefront of organic and climatesmart livestock practices. This initiative holds the potential to a drive significant reductions in livestock greenhouse gas emissions while fostering a sustainable and innovative agricultural industry.
llm_summary: Symbrosia’s SeaGraze project aims to significantly reduce livestock methane emissions through the utilization of a naturally-derived seaweed feed additive, representing a novel approach to sustainable agricultural practices. This initiative will involve the expansion of SeaGraze’s post-harvest processing capacity by over 1600%, enabling the production of a substantially larger volume of organic feed pellets cultivated in Kona, Hawaii. The anticipated outcome of this project is to enhance the market availability of domestically produced organic feed supplements, directly benefiting farmers and ranchers across the United States. By increasing the production volume, Symbrosia intends to capture a greater share of the organic feed supplement market, providing a valuable tool for reducing greenhouse gas emissions associated with livestock operations. This expansion will allow Symbrosia to deliver SeaGraze to processors and ultimately to consumers seeking sustainable agricultural products. The project’s goal is to position the United States as a leader in organic livestock practices, supporting the needs of ranchers and bolstering the supply of organic feed. The increased production capacity will result in a greater supply of SeaGraze, thereby allowing for wider adoption of this innovative feed additive within the agricultural sector and establishing a strong market presence for Symbrosia’s products.

Project Summary: This project requests funding support to complete the last critical investment in processing which will enhance MA’O Organic Farms (MA’Os’) capabilities to handle 10x more products while maintaining and eventually increasing a 65-product inventory while providing greater food flow handling to ensure highquality product is distributed to a greater diversity of market segments. MA’O is currently in year five of a ten-year expansion effort, starting in 2018 and ending in 2027. Through this effort, MA’O is growing internship participation in its college-career farm leadership programs, increasing organic food processing, and creating new full time farmer positions. The goal of this project is to maximize processing capabilities within MAʻO’s newly constructed wash-pack facility, by introducing product inventory management and 19 food safety technologies. This will streamline and support MAʻO’s ability to handle 10 times more products, while maintaining and eventually increasing product inventory and throughput of organic produce to ensure products are distributed to a greater diversity of market segments. At the same time, the project will nurture community information exchange and capacity building in technology and food safety to train and empower new young leaders for Hawai’i’s organic sector. This increases the supply of organic fruits and vegetables in the Hawaiian Islands, where 85-90% of food is imported, and local organic food is in high demand.
llm_summary: MA’O Organic Farms is seeking funding to finalize a critical investment in processing capabilities, designed to significantly enhance the farm’s operational scale and product handling. This project will maximize the potential of the newly constructed wash-pack facility by integrating product inventory management systems and nineteen specialized food safety technologies. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in MA’O’s processing capacity, allowing the farm to manage ten times more products while maintaining and ultimately expanding its 65-product inventory. This expansion will enable the efficient throughput of organic produce to a greater range of market segments, addressing a significant need within the Hawaiian Islands, where 85-90% of food is imported. This project directly benefits farmers, processors, and stakeholders involved in the organic sector, facilitating the movement of organic fruits and vegetables. By streamlining operations, the project supports the increased availability of locally produced organic agricultural commodities, strengthening the local food supply chain. The ultimate goal is to bolster the supply of organic produce within the Hawaiian Islands and to meet the high demand for domestically sourced organic food.

Project Summary: Kalona Creamery, LLC is requesting grant funds to expand organic milk production, handling, and processing capacity. This project will help expand the market for organic milk sourced from independent, small-scale dairy producers in Iowa, Missouri, Minnesota, and Wisconsin. Kalona Creamery sells branded organic milk products to retailers and distributors throughout the country. In addition, Kalona Creamery provides processing and milk handling services to a wide range of organic food companies in the upper Midwest. 23 This project will allow Kalona Creamery to increase processing services to organic dairy industry participants, including organic farmer-owned cooperatives and food companies. Grant funds will be spent on equipment to expand organic milk handling, storage, and processing capacity for organic milk, butter, yogurt, and cheese. Grant funds will also be spent on equipment to upgrade food-safety and wastewater handling programs in the company’s facilities. Ultimately, consumers will benefit from having increased access to high-quality organic dairy products sourced from small-scale, independent family farms.
llm_summary: Kalona Creamery, LLC is requesting grant funds to expand its organic milk production, handling, and processing capacity, addressing a critical need for additional market paths for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. This project will focus on acquiring equipment to significantly increase the company’s ability to handle, store, and process organic milk, alongside products such as butter, yogurt, and cheese, ultimately supporting the growth of its existing operations and the expansion of its services to a wider range of organic food companies. The planned investments will modernize food-safety and wastewater handling programs within Kalona Creamery’s facilities, ensuring adherence to stringent quality standards. The anticipated outcome is an increased supply of high-quality organic dairy products available to consumers throughout the country. These products will be sourced from independent, small-scale dairy producers in Iowa, Missouri, Minnesota, and Wisconsin. Farmers and ranchers participating in the project will benefit from increased market access for their organic milk. Consumers will gain greater access to a reliable source of organic dairy products, bolstering the supply chain for processors and other stakeholders in the organic food industry. The project’s success will be measured by the expanded volume of organic milk processed and distributed, directly contributing to the growth of the organic dairy sector and providing a strengthened position for Kalona Creamery within the national marketplace.

Project Summary: The goal of this project is to secure on-farm processing equipment to bring locally produced nutritious organic rolled oats to the consumer markets while preserving the product identity. For the past 2 years, A. Miller Farms and supply chain partners have searched locally for identity preserved organic rolled oats. This search has yielded no results implying a large market hole. With this grant A. Miller Farms can complete the initial pre-processing steps of hulling raw oats and separating them with a gravity table to distinguish the best quality for food grade specifications on-site. It can then finish processing these oat groats at Grain Place Foods in Marquette, NE, and bring the final product back to A. Miller Farms to distribute and market as organic identity preserved rolled oats. The Farm has a local distribution partner that already has demand for these identity preserved oats. Further market exploration will cover Iowa Schools and Hospital Systems. In addition, A. Miller Farms has also identified national retailers seeking identity preserved aspects that customers desire. Current processing of raw oats into a finished product at a small scale is not economically viable due to transportation costs to a dehuller facility and then to Grain Place Foods. Other consolidated commercial sources that have been identified are not able to process oats as identity preserved and do not intend to.
llm_summary: A. Miller Farms’ project aims to establish on-farm processing capabilities for organic rolled oats, addressing a significant market gap identified through a two-year search for locally sourced, identity preserved grains. The project will involve the purchase of equipment to perform initial processing steps, specifically hulling raw oats and utilizing a gravity table to separate high-quality grains for food-grade specifications. This initial processing will occur on-site, followed by completion of the oat groats at Grain Place Foods in Marquette, NE, ensuring the product maintains its identity preserved characteristics. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a new supply chain for organic rolled oats, supported by a local distribution partner with established demand. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers seeking a viable outlet for their organic oats and consumers desiring access to this specific product. Furthermore, A. Miller Farms intends to explore additional market opportunities, including demand from Iowa schools and hospital systems, as well as national retailers interested in identity preserved grains. This initiative directly addresses the need for expanded market paths for organic agricultural commodities, creating value for processors and stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of these grains. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of organic rolled oats produced and brought to market, solidifying A. Miller Farms’ position as a key supplier within the organic grain sector.

Project Summary: Fresh aronia berries are the flagship of Levi Lyle’s business. Blueberry, cranberry, and cherry fruit industries operate under a business model that has not served the infant aronia berry industry well. Iowa farmers have had to export aronia to Michigan where processing infrastructure exists. These locations require consolidation of produce into 100,000 pounds to conduct a “small run” of concentrate juice or consolidation of 1,000,000 pounds to gain access to cleaning and freezing facilities. Further challenges in aggregation and financial risks larger startups undertake exacerbate these challenges. The success of this 1- acre organic certified aronia crop develops out of a strong identity in place-based food. The business has expanded from farmers markets into health-food stores. For this project, Levi Lyle is partnering with a 10- acre organic certified grower to expand his Aronia Berry Organic Purée. The goal for this Aronia business is to successfully market a shelf-stable product created from the whole fruit ingredient, currently unavailable. Unique purée will be bottled in 16 ounces for retail. The Aronia Berry Organic Puree Project will bottle 4,000 gallons of whole berry puree for retailers partnered with this Aronia business. Market feasibility studies demonstrate the products currently available use highly processed concentrated juice, which requires a greater cost to produce in small batches, separates the juice from the fiber, and minimizes aronia’s health benefits located in the fiber and polyphenols. This project will benefit the 100+ aronia producers in the region who are without a market by growing to serve the needs of a struggling aronia industry.
llm_summary: Levi Lyle’s Aronia Berry Organic Puree Project aims to establish a new market for a shelf-stable product created from whole aronia berries, addressing a critical gap in the regional food supply chain. The project will involve the purchase of equipment necessary for processing 4,000 gallons of whole berry puree, intended for distribution to retail partners aligned with this aronia business. Anticipated outcomes include the successful creation and marketing of a 16-ounce bottle of aronia berry puree, offering consumers a product currently unavailable due to reliance on highly processed, concentrated juice formulations. This project directly benefits over 100 aronia producers in the region who lack established market channels, as well as the consumers seeking access to this unique product. The project’s success will provide a viable pathway for these producers to sell their harvest, supporting their livelihoods and contributing to a more robust aronia industry. Furthermore, the project seeks to stimulate demand for aronia berries, encouraging further production and benefiting processors and other stakeholders involved in the supply chain. By establishing a dedicated market for this whole-berry puree, Levi Lyle’s project provides a solution to the challenges faced by current aronia growers and introduces a valuable product to the retail market.

Project Summary: The Organic Grain Gateway of Iowa (OGGI) project will help stabilize the organic grains and livestock feed supply chain. It will offer new market access for Iowa’s organic grain farmers, reduce reliance on imports for the coastal organic livestock markets, and ultimately increase organic grain production in Iowa. This will be achieved by assembling a dedicated organic grain aggregation and marketing terminal in central Iowa 24 with existing direct access to Norfolk Southern, BNSF and Union Pacific railroads the only site in Iowa with this connectivity. By the end of the project, Iowa’s organic corn and soybean farmers will see an increased demand for organic products, specifically on the East and West Coasts which currently rely on imports to meet regional demand for these products. By connecting these three critical railways in one location, centrally located in the largest producing state of organic corn and soybeans, organic farmers in the state of Iowa will have direct access to new markets. Together, with the support of Iowa organic farmers, USDA NOP TOPP Partners, the Iowa Department of Agriculture, and The Organic Trade Association, the project will be a crucial step in sustaining the growth of domestic organic production by providing the infrastructure and market access needed.
llm_summary: The Organic Grain Gateway of Iowa (OGGI) project aims to stabilize the supply chain for organic grains and livestock feed by establishing a dedicated aggregation and marketing terminal in central Iowa, capitalizing on its unique connectivity to Norfolk Southern, BNSF, and Union Pacific railroads – the only such site in the state. This project will create new market access for Iowa’s organic corn and soybean farmers, significantly reducing reliance on imported products for the coastal organic livestock markets. The core of the initiative involves constructing this centralized terminal, strategically located in the state’s largest producing region for organic grains and soybeans. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in demand for Iowa-grown organic corn and soybeans, specifically targeting the existing needs of consumers and processors on the East and West Coasts. Iowa’s organic farmers will directly benefit from expanded market opportunities, allowing them to supply these regional markets with high-quality organic products. The project will support stakeholders involved in the production, processing, and distribution of organic grains and livestock feed. Ultimately, the OGGI project represents a crucial step in sustaining the growth of domestic organic production and will positively impact farmers and related businesses throughout the state by providing the necessary infrastructure and market access.

Project Summary: The purpose of this project is to create a marketplace to sell organic feeds. Currently, a gap exists in the Idaho supply chain between organic commodities that are being grown in the area and the organic feed being consumed. Specialized machines and equipment are used to turn various organic commodities into 20 precise rations and mixtures for feeds. Farmers grow organic crops intended for animal feed but are unable to sell locally because the ability and/or capacity to process the organic commodity into animal feed is unavailable. Thus, the farmer resorts to selling crops to feed processors out of the area, causing the organic feed consumer to buy out of the area as well. This creates significant added costs for both buyer and seller. This project would address the supply chain issue directly. The activities to be performed are the purchase and installation of various machinery and equipment to be used to convert organic crops efficiently and accurately into precise animal feeds. This would enable to create a marketplace for organic animal feeds. The marketplace would create deliverable organic feed products that would include formulated pellets, total mixed rations, and processed commodities that could be used individually or incorporated into the customer's mixed ration for their feeding operation. The expected outcomes would be an increased processing capacity in the area for organic crop farmers and increased consumption of local organic feeds.
llm_summary: The Idaho Organic Market Development Grant project aims to address a critical supply chain gap within the state, facilitating the efficient processing of organic crops into specialized animal feeds. This project will involve the purchase and installation of specialized machinery and equipment designed to convert a range of organic commodities into twenty precise rations and mixtures, suitable for various feeding operations. The anticipated outcomes include an increased processing capacity within the Idaho region, empowering local farmers to directly supply formulated pellets, total mixed rations, and processed commodities to consumers and processors. This initiative will directly benefit farmers by offering a viable local market for their organic crops, while simultaneously meeting the demand for high-quality, locally sourced organic feeds among ranchers and feed processors. Ultimately, this project seeks to reduce transportation costs and logistical complexities for both farmers and feed consumers, creating a more streamlined and efficient supply chain. The success of this project will lead to greater availability of organic animal feeds within Idaho, benefiting all stakeholders involved in the production and consumption of these essential agricultural products.

Project Summary: The project goal is to increase farmstead creamery processing capacity and, in doing so, to create a milk market for other organic producers to sell their milk to the North Sky Farm creamery. With the increased processing volume, North Sky Farm will be able to meet the expectations of a wholesale distributor allowing them to sell organic cheese to many more people. The project will increase cheesemaking capacity so they are able to buy milk from another dairy farm in addition to processing milk from their own farm. The project team will rearrange creamery space to accommodate larger equipment, update the wastewater system to accommodate a larger volume, increase personnel to process the larger volume of cheese, and work with a consultant to sell the increased volume of cheese through a distributor. In addition, North Sky Farm is creating a milk market for another producer. Increasing processing will allow them to reach the minimum volume needed to work with wholesale cheese distributors which will bring organic cheese to a much broader customer base. This project would double processing capacity. There are three main expected outcomes: 1) milk contracts offered to two organic dairy farms, North Sky Farm’s own dairy and one other organic dairy thus creating a milk market, 2) processing will expand to a level to be able to sell through a wholesale distributor so their cheese will be able to be sold in mainstream grocery stores over a wide geographic area, and 3) an increase in sales volume to a level where the organic creamery is economically sustainable and is able to continue to employ at least four, and likely more fulltime employees beyond the end of the project period. North Sky Farm will achieve these goals by making some key changes to increase production capacity to remove processing facility equipment bottlenecks that curtail manufacturing capacity.
llm_summary: North Sky Farm’s project aims to substantially increase its farmstead creamery processing capacity to establish a viable milk market for organic producers and facilitate the sale of their products. This expansion will involve key changes including rearranging creamery space to accommodate larger equipment, updating the wastewater system to handle increased volumes, and expanding personnel to manage the larger production scale. Furthermore, the project includes working with a consultant to secure a wholesale distribution agreement, allowing North Sky Farm to sell its organic cheese to a significantly broader customer base through mainstream grocery stores across a wide geographic area. The anticipated outcomes of this project include the establishment of milk contracts with two organic dairy farms – North Sky Farm’s own dairy operation and one additional organic dairy – creating a robust milk market and the achievement of processing capacity sufficient to meet the requirements for wholesale distribution. Ultimately, this project will increase sales volume to a level where the organic creamery is economically sustainable, supporting the employment of at least four, and potentially more, full-time employees beyond the project’s completion. The project will benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking access to domestically produced organic cheese. By increasing processing capabilities, North Sky Farm will contribute to a more accessible organic cheese market for stakeholders throughout the region.

Project Summary: Adelante Center’s Garfield Produce (GFP) sustainable hydroponics urban farm produces premium quality microgreens for regional distribution in its clean facility located in one of Chicago’s most distressed West Side communities. Its products are sustainably grown year round and sold to local hotels, hospitals, universities, and restaurants through 7 regional wholesale distributors. Garfield Produce is the largest and most profitable minority and disabled veteran owned farm in the Chicagoland area. This project will allow Adelante Centers Garfield Produce to make the key investments that will facilitate the implementation of a consumer-facing retail organic microgreen product, including brand development, marketing, and product promotion in new and existing distribution channels. The project will also allow GFP to upgrade equipment to facilitate organic packaging, handling, food safety, and environmental controls will complement this project’s marketing and partnership focus for local urban organic producers. Adelante will facilitate a oneday conference to network existing rural and urban organic producers with organic buyers to share best agricultural practices, leverage collective facilities closer to the target market, and establish and test an alternative logistics supply chain to reduce costs and increase access to the Chicago (and other) nearby market(s). This will allow both Garfield Produce products and a more extensive list of smaller local organic producers to build collective capacity to grow into larger, more profitable, urban consumer markets. The project will include a feasibility study to assess the cost and benefit of expansion into new markets for organic products in Milwaukee, St. Louis, and Indianapolis. These programs will increase local urban agriculture jobs, expand business capacity, and allow organic products to reach local consumers who would otherwise never have access to nor understand the benefit of, organic produce.
llm_summary: Adelante Center’s Garfield Produce (GFP) is undertaking a key initiative to establish a consumer-facing retail organic microgreen product line, driven by strategic investments in brand development, marketing, and promotional activities across existing and new distribution channels. This project will encompass the purchase and implementation of equipment designed to facilitate organic packaging, handling, food safety, and environmental controls, complementing the marketing and partnership focus on local organic producers. Anticipated outcomes include expanded market reach for GFP’s existing products through a network of regional wholesale distributors, and the establishment of a direct-to-consumer retail offering. The project aims to support farmers and processors involved in organic agriculture by increasing access to markets for their goods. Specifically, GFP will host a one-day conference to connect rural and urban organic producers with organic buyers, with the goal of sharing best agricultural practices, leveraging collective facilities, and establishing an alternative logistics supply chain. This initiative seeks to bolster the capacity of both GFP products and smaller local organic producers to grow into larger, more profitable operations within consumer markets. Furthermore, a feasibility study will assess the potential for expansion into new markets, including Milwaukee, St. Louis, and Indianapolis. The overall effect will be to increase the availability of organic agricultural commodities and enhance access for consumers to these products. GFP’s efforts will support stakeholders across the agricultural value chain, contributing to the growth of local organic production and distribution.

Project Summary: In early 2023, Wild Pansy Farm launched the Simply Indiana soup line, with support from a Specialty Crop Block Grant through the Indiana State Department of Agriculture. The company produces 60 gallons (600 servings) of soup weekly in a shared commercial kitchen, using beans and vegetables from a network of 10 Indiana and regional organic farms. Most of these farms are beginning farmer-, woman-, and or veteranowned. Wild Pansy Farm aims to expand processing to 1200 gallons per week by retrofitting the interior of an existing building and converting it into a purpose-designed soup manufacturing facility. This will help regional farms by providing a right-sized outlet to sell their organic produce at scale. Indiana Fresh Connect coordinates the delivery of Simply Indiana soup quarts to three food shelters in Jackson County, IN. By 22 moving to a purpose-designed processing space, Wild Pansy Farm can deliver to more food shelters. The new equipment will enable the soup to be served at schools in 18 southern Indiana counties, where eligibility for the Free and Reduced Lunch program is over 45%. Wild Pansy Farm will build annual processing capacity for $800,000 worth of produce and beans from the region’s organic growers, and configure the space to deliver 1,000,000 soup servings per year to its community, which is experiencing persistent poverty
llm_summary: Wild Pansy Farm launched the Simply Indiana soup line with support from a Specialty Crop Block Grant, aiming to expand processing capacity to 1,000,000 soup servings annually. This project involves retrofitting an existing building into a purpose-designed soup manufacturing facility, enabling the company to produce 1200 gallons of soup weekly from a network of 10 Indiana and regional organic farms. Anticipated outcomes include the processing of $800,000 worth of produce and beans from regional organic growers, providing a right-sized outlet for farmers and processors. The expanded capacity will allow for delivery to three food shelters in Jackson County, IN, and ultimately, to schools in 18 southern Indiana counties where over 45% of students are eligible for Free and Reduced Lunch programs. The project will benefit the local community by providing increased access to prepared food, and supporting regional agricultural stakeholders. This initiative directly addresses a critical need for market paths for organic commodities, and will contribute to increased consumption of domestically produced organic agricultural products. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of produce processed and the number of servings distributed, ultimately assisting communities experiencing persistent poverty.

Project Summary: Valley Malt, DBA Ground Up, is a women-owned flour mill in Holyoke, MA proposing OMDG funding for a Northeast Organic Roller Mill (NORM) dedicated to Northeast organic grains. The project will increase processing capacity, reduce energy consumption, reduce labor, and capture a growing market demand for roller milled organic flour and organic baked products. The goals of the project would include 1) the installation of a roller mill system at the current Valley Malt, DBA Ground Up (VM/GU) facility by 2025; 2) the sourcing, marketing, and sales of 5 million pounds of roller milled flour annually by the end of the project; 3) the development of organic value-added products that create market demand and reach 28 underserved populations in the region. These goals will align with larger interventions that have been ongoing in the Northeast to explore regional markets and demand for organic food grains. Multi-state collaborations between the Northeast’s public and private sectors in the last 15 years have supported the development of cereal grain cultivars adapted to the Northeast that are favored by bakers and farmers alike. Regional resources from university extensions, agronomists, and peer-to-peer networks across the region will support growers in providing 2,600 acres of organic grains for this project. The project will benefit stakeholders from the entire Northeast grain value chain. This includes small and medium sized organic and transitional growers, distributors of organic foods, commercial bakeries, institutional buyers, micro-bakeries, specialty food producers from underserved populations, and approximately 300,000 consumers of organic food in the Northeast.
llm_summary: Valley Malt, DBA Ground Up, is proposing a project to establish a Northeast Organic Roller Mill (NORM) dedicated to processing organic grains within the Northeast region. This initiative involves the construction of a new roller mill system at the Valley Malt, DBA Ground Up facility, with the goal of increasing processing capacity and reducing energy consumption. The project anticipates the annual sourcing, marketing, and sales of five million pounds of roller milled flour, directly supporting farmers and processors involved in the organic grain supply chain. Furthermore, the project aims to develop organic value-added products, stimulating market demand and reaching approximately 300,000 consumers of organic food within the Northeast. Key stakeholders, including small and medium sized organic and transitional growers, distributors, commercial bakeries, and institutional buyers, will benefit from this expansion. The project will leverage approximately 2,600 acres of organic grains provided by regional growers, creating a robust supply chain. This expansion will directly support the production and distribution of organic grain products throughout the Northeast, offering a viable market pathway for regional grain producers. The anticipated outcomes include increased access to roller milled flour and organic value-added products for consumers and businesses within the region.

Project Summary: This project will expand the capacity of Moon Valley Farm and its 40+ regional partner farms to grow, process, store and deliver organic legumes and grains to thousands of subscribers, direct market and wholesale customers across Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Virginia. Moon Valley Farm is a certified organic, year-round, diversified produce farm that grows legumes and grains on a small-scale and aggregates legume, grains, fruits, mushrooms, eggs and more from partner farms. The Farm wants to increase processing and aggregation of these crops to benefit its crop rotation plan, whole-farm planning, and to meet customers demand. However, the business lacks the equipment required to increase production, storage, and delivery of these specialty crops. Moon Valley Farm’s goals with this project are to expand capacity to process, aggregate, store and deliver high quality legumes and grains to meet regional customer demand with key pieces of equipment. This project will strengthen the community of farms, impact hundreds of acres, and increase the region’s food security and climate resilience.
llm_summary: Moon Valley Farm seeks to expand its capacity for the processing, aggregation, storage, and delivery of high-quality legumes and grains to meet substantial regional demand across Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Virginia. This project will involve the acquisition of key equipment necessary to scale operations, allowing the farm to significantly increase its output and broaden its offerings to include a wider range of processed products. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the volume of legumes and grains available to farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking locally sourced agricultural commodities. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be the farmers involved in the Moon Valley Farm network, as well as the processors who utilize these crops, and the consumers who represent the market for these goods. Furthermore, the project will strengthen the regional agricultural network, impacting hundreds of acres of farmland and contributing to greater food security within the area. The increased availability of these crops will support a more robust and resilient agricultural system, providing a valuable resource for various stakeholders. By expanding the farm’s capabilities, Moon Valley Farm aims to enhance its crop rotation plan and whole-farm planning efforts, ultimately improving operational efficiency and supply chain management.

Project Summary: Soybeans have been historically grown in the central United States, however, climate change is causing droughts in these areas and affecting yield. Maine is warming and has ample water supply, creating an increasingly ideal climate for soybeans. As a nitrogen-fixing crop, soybeans are an ideal rotation crop for other grains, providing nitrogen for the next year's crop and reducing the need for synthetic and manure fertilizers. Although Maine farmers want to produce more soybeans, they lack access to processing infrastructure to enable them to take advantage of the premium, food grade, organic soybean markets. Aurora Mills Farm (Aurora) is one of the leading organic small grains and legume growers in Maine. Aurora is also a value-added producer that processes and mills organic grains and legumes, providing flour, rolled oats, soybeans and field peas to numerous New England based institutions and food producers. Adding bean polishing, destoning and a second cleaner to create a gluten free cleaning line to the existing processing infrastructure will open up new market opportunities for Maine growers. They will be able to grow and access the organic soybean market by using Auroras processing infrastructure. Soybeans, the easiest legume to market, require a stain free, stone free bean. Increased weeds, inherent in organic production, contribute to more staining in the combining harvesting process. Aurora currently has the ability to remove the weeds in the cleaning process, but stained beans are still left. Polishing and destoning will provide Maine’s small grain and legume producers to access new gluten-free markets
llm_summary: Aurora Mills Farm (Aurora) is undertaking a project to expand organic soybean production and processing in Maine, addressing a critical market need for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. The project involves the acquisition and installation of specialized equipment within Aurora’s existing processing infrastructure, specifically focusing on bean polishing, destoning, and a second cleaning stage. This expansion will enable Aurora to create a dedicated gluten-free cleaning line, significantly improving the quality of Maine-grown soybeans to meet the stringent requirements of food-grade organic markets. The anticipated outcome of this project is to provide Maine farmers with access to a premium market channel for their soybeans, allowing them to capitalize on increasing consumer demand for organic products. This will directly benefit Maine’s soybean producers, processors, and ultimately, consumers seeking high-quality, organic ingredients. By improving the bean’s physical characteristics—removing stones and stains—the project will enhance the marketability of Maine-grown soybeans, allowing for wider distribution and increased revenue streams for the involved stakeholders. The project aims to strengthen Maine’s agricultural sector by facilitating the growth of a viable organic soybean supply chain, securing a new market opportunity for Maine agricultural products.

Project Summary: The economic viability of this farm is made stronger by the synergy of growing and marketing a legume such as edamame with two distinctive benefits: 1) the creation of a niche market for value-added fresh and frozen edamame, generating an additional diversified income benefit for the farm and 2) Utilizing the nitrogen-fixing ability of soybeans to fix and incorporate between 30 to 50 lbs. of nitrogen per acre into the soil. The project fulfills the need to purchase processing equipment and a transport van which plays a critical role in the storage and delivery of fresh and frozen edamame, ensuring the end product maintains the proper quality, safety, and shelf life throughout its final distribution channels such as long-established Farmers Markets and the numerous retail outlets the farm serves throughout the state of Maine
llm_summary: The OMDG project aims to strengthen the economic viability of the farm through the cultivation and marketing of edamame, capitalizing on two key benefits. Specifically, this initiative focuses on establishing a niche market for fresh and frozen edamame, thereby creating an additional revenue stream for the farm. Simultaneously, the project utilizes the nitrogen-fixing capabilities of soybeans, anticipating the incorporation of between 30 to 50 pounds of nitrogen per acre into the soil, enhancing soil fertility naturally. To achieve this, the project includes the purchase of critical processing equipment and a transport van. These items are essential for maintaining the quality, safety, and shelf life of the fresh and frozen edamame throughout its distribution, connecting the farm with established Farmers Markets and numerous retail outlets across the state of Maine. The anticipated outcome is an increased supply of edamame, benefiting farmers and consumers alike. The project will support stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of this agricultural commodity. The success of this project is expected to bolster the farm's operations and provide a valuable product to the marketplace.

Project Summary: This project's goal is to expand on-farm processing capacity to increase consumption of organic cheeses. To address the lack of availability of organic milk for purchase, Balfour Farm is expanding on-farm milk production to increase the farm’s on site processing. Proposed equipment purchases will replace existing equipment with larger capacity cheesemaking equipment to accommodate the planned 175% increase in milk production. The farm will increase the capacity for milk production from 12 cows to 20 cows by the end of 2025. The farm will replace the current oil-fired system, which is approximately 25 years old, with high efficiency propane system. This increases the volume of milk processed and reduces the time required per batch. A cleaner burning, efficient system will modernize process controls and be more a sustainable energy source.The automatic curd mill will solve two problems - workflow and employee fatigue. As more milk is processed, larger batches of cheese will take longer to mill the curds. The EBR curd mill will reduce curd cutting time. This will also reduce worker fatigue. The current hand operated mill places significant stress on the shoulder and arm joints while using. Replacing the mechanical cheese press with higher capacity pneumatic modelwill increase volume and provide for consistent process control, having a positive effect on product appearance, flavor, and texture.The farm’s increased organic milk processing will result in an annual cheese production increase of 7,745 lbs.
llm_summary: Balfour Farm’s project aims to significantly increase on-farm processing capacity for organic cheeses, directly addressing the limited availability of organic milk and fostering greater consumption of this product. The farm will achieve this expansion by acquiring and installing new, high-efficiency equipment, including a larger capacity cheesemaking system, a modern propane heating system to replace the existing oil-fired system, an automatic curd mill, and a high-capacity pneumatic cheese press. These upgrades will substantially increase milk processing volume and improve operational efficiency, resulting in an anticipated annual cheese production increase of 7,745 pounds. The project will benefit farmers by enhancing their ability to capture value from their organic milk production, while also providing consumers with greater access to locally produced organic cheeses. Processors will see a strengthened market for their goods and the farm’s stakeholders will benefit from the increased availability of organic dairy products. The upgraded equipment will streamline the cheesemaking process, reducing worker fatigue and maintaining consistent product quality, thereby impacting the appearance, flavor, and texture of the final cheese products. This expansion represents a strategic investment to bolster Balfour Farm’s capacity and respond to growing market demand for organic dairy goods.

Project Summary: This project will increase access for local organic products to large scale Northeast grocery chains by providing industry standard, cost effective, custom packaging of produce for small organic farms. Organic products in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic regions are significantly underrepresented in large scale grocery markets where the vast majority of organic food products are sold. Small organic farms in the region do not have access to automated packaging machinery that can portion and pack bulk produce into retail size, industry standard UPC labelled units for large scale retail sale. Currently, small organic farms are packaging by hand into expensive small run packages. Reducing packaging costs will allow these farms to increase production volume and sales revenue. This project will allow the purchased, installed and calibration of equipment to provide custom packaging for four farms with the following goals 1)to increase the market share of organic products in large scale grocery stores throughout the Northeast, 2) to decrease 27 unit cost of small organic farm product packaging for retail grocery sales making these products more competitive while increasing sales volume, 3) to increase labor efficiency by reducing or eliminating low skill packaging tasks, and providing higher skill and ultimately higher value tasks for workers on organic farms, and 4) to foster and strengthen connections between small organic farms to develop shared pathways towards expanded markets.
llm_summary: This project aims to significantly increase access for local organic products to large-scale Northeast grocery chains by providing industry standard, cost-effective, custom packaging of produce for small organic farms within the region. The initiative will involve the purchase, installation, and calibration of specialized equipment designed to produce retail-sized, UPC-labelled units of various produce items, tailored to the specific needs of four organic farms. This will directly address the current challenge faced by these farms, who are presently packaging produce by hand into expensive, small-run packages, leading to high unit costs. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a substantial increase in the market share of organic products within large grocery stores throughout the Northeast, alongside a reduction of 27 units in the cost of packaging these products for retail grocery sales, ultimately boosting sales volume for the participating farms. Furthermore, this project will improve labor efficiency by reducing the volume of low-skill packaging tasks, allowing for the reallocation of worker time towards more valuable operations. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the small organic farms themselves, who will gain improved access to larger markets and increased revenue potential. The project will also benefit consumers who will have greater availability of organic products within their local grocery stores, and processors who will have access to a greater supply of high-quality organic ingredients. Finally, the project will foster stronger connections among these organic farms, creating shared pathways towards expanded markets and strengthening the overall organic agricultural sector within the Northeast region.

Legal Name: Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association
Project Summary: This project aims to strengthen consumer and institutional demand for local, organic dairy products produced in the Northeast (NE) US which face challenges such as contract cancellations and rising production costs. The project seeks to address this crisis by expanding the farm-to-institution market for organic dairy, increasing the number of retail outlets promoting organic dairy, and implementing targeted consumer marketing efforts to boost demand for products made with NE dairy. The first main activity is to increase grocery retail partners by onboarding food co-ops, independent grocers, and large-chain supermarkets committed to promoting and selling organic dairy from the Northeast. The Northeast Organic Family Farm Partnership (NOFFP) will develop compelling program pitch materials, increase staff support to onboard and retain Retail Partners, and establish a retail peer group to share best practices in promoting organic dairy. The second main goal is to facilitate product innovation for bulk organic dairy. For this goal, NOFFP will collaborate with regional farm-to-institution partners to increase the number of participating colleges, K-12s, and hospitals buying NE organic dairy. Strengthening relationships between buyers, distributors, and processors will enable market developments, including the introduction of bulk formats for organic yogurt, cheese, and fluid milk, in response to institutional buyer demands. The final goal is to develop a marketing campaign through the development of new marketing strategies to engage consumers and educate them about the benefits of NE organic dairy. This includes creating brand awareness and loyalty for local organic dairy brands through Point of Sale (POS) marketing, consumer food demos, social media, and targeted messaging. The project is expected to benefit more than 286 organic family farms and 30 value-added organic processors.
llm_summary: The Organic Market Development Grant (OMDG) project aims to strengthen consumer and institutional demand for local, organic dairy products produced in the Northeast (NE) US, addressing challenges such as contract cancellations and rising production costs. This initiative will achieve this by expanding the farm-to-institution market for organic dairy, increasing the number of retail outlets promoting organic dairy products, and implementing targeted consumer marketing efforts to boost demand for products made with NE dairy. Specifically, the project will focus on onboarding food co-ops, independent grocers, and large-chain supermarkets committed to promoting and selling organic dairy, alongside facilitating product innovation for bulk organic dairy, including yogurt, cheese, and fluid milk formats. Anticipated outcomes include increased market access for over 286 organic family farms and 30 value-added organic processors, as well as expanded sales channels for these products. The project will benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the organic dairy supply chain by fostering new market opportunities and supporting the production of high-quality organic dairy goods. Through the development of targeted marketing campaigns utilizing Point of Sale (POS) marketing, consumer food demos, and social media, the project intends to create brand awareness and loyalty for local organic dairy brands. Ultimately, the project seeks to create a more robust and sustainable market for Northeast organic dairy, supporting the economic viability of farms and processors within the region.

Project Summary: Almar Orchards is a 4th and 5th generation, family-owned organic apple orchard in Michigan, where organic markets are limited. A washing and sorting line would enable Almar to access a new commodity market through baby and kid food company, Once Upon a Farm (OFarm). This partnership would result in increased domestic sourcing by companies like OFarm and serve as an aggregator for other growers in the region. With the ability to clean and sort apples for the commodity market, Almar projects its sales volumes of organic apples could increase by 3 times the current rate over the next 5 years. This increase is driven by other apple growers in the region, who would also benefit from the grant. Nearby growers would be able to aggregate their crop through this wash line, thereby gaining access to new commodity markets. The increased capacity provided by the wash line would also enable Almar to expand organic apple production onto 100 additional acres that are currently fallow or being leased by annual crop growers. This development would result in a future production increase beyond the 5 year projections. Given that Michigan is the third largest apple producer in the country, there is significant opportunity to expand organic production in the state if access to a viable market is present.
llm_summary: Almar Orchards is undertaking a project to establish a washing and sorting line, a key investment designed to significantly expand its reach into new commodity markets, specifically through a partnership with Once Upon a Farm (OFarm), a company producing baby and kid food. This initiative aims to increase Almar’s sales volumes of organic apples by a projected three times the current rate over the next five years, driven by increased demand from OFarm and the potential for aggregation of crops from other regional growers. The core of this project involves the construction of a washing and sorting line, enabling Almar to process apples to a standard suitable for the food industry. This development will also facilitate the expansion of Almar’s organic apple production onto an additional 100 acres currently unused or leased for annual crops, representing a substantial increase in overall production capacity. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened position for Almar Orchards and a broader supply of organic apples for the food market. This project will directly benefit farmers and processors within the region, providing access to a new revenue stream and the opportunity to scale up their operations. Furthermore, the increased production capacity will positively affect stakeholders throughout the supply chain. The project represents a strategic investment poised to unlock significant growth potential within Michigan’s apple industry and to support a broader expansion of organic agriculture in the state.

Project Summary: The primary goal of the project is to enhance current manufacturing capacity for USDA Organic Tomato Paste in tubes, thereby meeting the increasing demand for organic products. As the sole domestic producers of this unique product, under the Giovanni’s brand label, Giovanni’s is committed to providing consumers with a high-quality, organic, and locally sourced option using only domestically grown ingredients. The equipment upgrade aims to streamline the production process and increase efficiency to meet the rising demand for organic tomato paste in tubes. By investing in the tube filling equipment, Giovanni’s aims to achieve three objectives, which align with the purpose of the program: 1) Promoting sustainable agriculture through exclusive use of domestically grown organic tomatoes emphasizing the company’s commitment to promoting sustainable agricultural practices within the United States. By supporting this project, the program can encourage and endorse responsible farming methods that minimize environmental impact and conserve natural resources. 2) Strengthening domestic manufacturing by enhancing domestic manufacturing capabilities and reducing reliance on imports. As the only US manufacturer of USDA Organic Tomato Paste, this project directly aligns with this goal, of contributing to the growth and resilience of the domestic manufacturing sector. 3) Meeting consumer demand for organic 31 products: With an increasing number of consumers seeking organic and locally sourced food options, this project addresses this demand by providing a unique and certified organic tomato paste in user-friendly tubes. This helps to foster healthier eating choices and supports the program's aim of promoting organic products in the market.
llm_summary: Giovanni’s is undertaking a project to significantly enhance its manufacturing capacity for USDA Organic Tomato Paste in tubes, directly addressing the increasing consumer demand for organic products. This initiative centers around a key investment: the purchase and implementation of new tube filling equipment, designed to streamline the production process and increase overall efficiency. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial increase in the supply of Giovanni’s USDA Organic Tomato Paste, catering to a growing market segment seeking locally sourced, certified organic food options. This will benefit farmers who supply the domestically grown organic tomatoes, processors involved in the production of the paste, and ultimately, consumers who value high-quality, organic food products. By bolstering domestic manufacturing capabilities, Giovanni’s aims to reduce reliance on imports and solidify its position as the sole US producer of this specialized product. The increased availability of the USDA Organic Tomato Paste will meet consumer demand for organic products and contribute to the growth of the market for organically produced agricultural commodities. The project’s success will support a wider network of stakeholders within the food production industry.

Project Summary: Northern Michigan is home to many organic producers, yet no capability exists for organic producers to develop organic packaged products with the raw organic commodities they produce. The purpose of this project is to expand market access for new organic packaged products by establishing aggregation and comanufacturing services serving multiple organic producers in Northern Michigan initially, with continued growth throughout the Midwest. As a USDA Organic certified organic handler and processing facility, Cultured Ferments is well-positioned to introduce these services and transform a singular product line facility into one with the ability to package almost any viscous product in an organic format. This project will enable product development of organic kombucha made available in cans, along with existing glass bottle formats. The project includes the following activities: installation of a canning line to produce organic kombucha in canned format, partnering with area organic producers to provide co-manufacturing services, expanding delivery networks and maximizing efficiency, and serving area organic producers including small and underserved organic producers with access to new markets.The project is expected to expand networks for organic producers, particularly those in historically underserved areas, to develop and deliver organic packaged products, and provide them access new markets.
llm_summary: Cultured Ferments’ project aims to expand market access for new organic packaged products within Northern Michigan and the broader Midwest by establishing aggregation and co-manufacturing services for multiple organic producers. This initiative will involve the installation of a canning line specifically designed to produce organic kombucha in both canned and glass bottle formats, alongside the expansion of existing processing capabilities. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of new market pathways for organic producers, enabling them to develop and deliver their products to a wider range of consumers. The project will primarily benefit farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the organic production chain, facilitating access to established distribution networks and maximizing operational efficiency. Through this project, Cultured Ferments intends to support the growth of the organic sector by providing a centralized solution for packaging and manufacturing, allowing producers to focus on their core competencies – the production of organic commodities. Ultimately, the project seeks to increase the availability of organic products and create opportunities for farmers to reach new markets, establishing a robust supply chain for organic goods within the region.

Project Summary: The goal of this project is to enhance Granor Farm's capacity to handle, package, and distribute identitypreserved organic grains to various end-users. Granor Farm is seeking to meet the substantial demand from 29 its partners such as maltsters, millers, distillers, bakers, brewers, and other end users for certified organic rotational crops, with a focus on barley, wheat, and cereal rye. The project will purchase equipment allowing Granor Farm to weigh and batch identity-preserved grain with utmost care and cleanliness, ensuring precise filling of supersack totes. The built-in belt conveyor will eliminate lot contamination between crops and enable filling of multiple supersacks with high accuracy. The mobile design also allows for indoor filling during winter, enhanced operational safety and flexibility, and reduced weather-related delays. The implementation of the Brandt conveyor will eliminate excessive grain damage and contamination during packaging and post-harvest handling. By replacing traditional steel augers, the belt conveyor ensures the retention of no grain byproducts or extra kernels after operation, eliminating the need for grain purges while maintaining clean and contaminant-free grain lots. The improved capacity and safety measures will enable Granor Farm to meet growing market demands for organic products in Michigan and throughout the upper Midwest.
llm_summary: Granor Farm is undertaking a project to significantly enhance its capabilities in handling, packaging, and distributing identity-preserved organic grains to meet substantial demand from a network of 29 partners, including maltsters, millers, distillers, bakers, and brewers. This project will involve the purchase of specialized equipment, including a Brandt conveyor system, designed to precisely weigh and batch identity-preserved grain with utmost care and cleanliness, ensuring accurate filling of supersack totes. The integrated belt conveyor will eliminate lot contamination between crops and facilitate the efficient filling of multiple supersacks with high accuracy. The mobile design of the equipment will enable indoor filling during winter, enhancing operational safety and reducing delays caused by weather conditions. The implementation of this new system will allow Granor Farm to maintain clean and contaminant-free grain lots, retaining no grain byproducts or extra kernels after operation, thereby eliminating the need for grain purges. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial increase in Granor Farm’s capacity to supply certified organic rotational crops, particularly barley, wheat, and cereal rye, to processors and stakeholders throughout Michigan and the upper Midwest. This expanded production capacity will directly benefit farmers and processors seeking access to high-quality organic grains, ultimately providing consumers with a greater selection of organic agricultural products. The project’s success will contribute to meeting the needs of these stakeholders and bolstering the supply of organic ingredients for various applications.

Project Summary: There is no certified organic hay and forage available for purchase within 200 miles of Weinrich Farm, and very little available anywhere in Michigan. Consequently, producing organic beef, lamb, or goat is currently not an option for farms in the area. This project will upgrade and expand the hay and forage making capacity of the Weinrich Farm, LLC, creating the only large-scale organic producer of hay and forage in northern Michigan. Newer and better hay and forage equipment will enable them to rapidly cut, bale and transport, making the business more efficient with existing organic transition pasture. It will also allow them to bring hundreds more acres into organic production over three years. This equipment will kick-start a supply chain for organic, grass-fed ruminants in this region. The project will allow Weinrich Farm to transition their own ruminants to organic feed, eventually enabling them to produce organic grass-fed beef. It will remove a barrier to organic certification for other local small farms who cannot currently access organic hay and forage. This project will create new revenue streams for several existing organic vegetable farms in northern Michigan that have under-utilized pastures which could be used for organic hay, forage, and straw. The project will also support the expansion of organic wheat in the area by enabling the production of forages as a profitable complement in a crop rotation.
llm_summary: Weinrich Farm, LLC, is undertaking a significant project to establish itself as the sole large-scale producer of certified organic hay and forage within northern Michigan, addressing a critical market need. This project will involve the acquisition of new and enhanced hay and forage equipment, including advanced cutting, baling, and transport systems, to dramatically increase production capacity and efficiency, ultimately enabling the transition of hundreds more acres into organic pastureland over a three-year timeframe. The anticipated outcomes of this project include the creation of a robust supply chain for organic grass-fed ruminants, supporting ranchers and processors in the region. Furthermore, Weinrich Farm intends to transition its own herd to organic feed, with the eventual goal of producing organic grass-fed beef. This initiative will also positively impact numerous existing organic vegetable farms in northern Michigan who possess underutilized pastures suitable for producing hay, forage, and straw, thus generating new revenue streams for these stakeholders. The expanded production of organic hay and forage will facilitate the incorporation of wheat into crop rotations, maximizing land utilization and profitability. The successful completion of this project will benefit consumers by increasing the availability of locally sourced, organic ruminant products within the region and support the growth of the organic livestock sector.

Project Summary: Great Lakes Garlic Farm is a USDA Certified Organic garlic, grains, and vegetable farm in Grand Traverse County, in Northern Michigan. The operation includes a state-inspected commercial processing facility where it currently dehydrates, grinds, and hand-fills spice jars to create value-added products. The community has a lack of available dehydrated and shelf stable local organic products. By expanding processing capacity of organic ingredients, producing, and storing organic livestock feed, and establishing end-user markets for rotational crops, this project will ease existing bottlenecks and increase supply of several organic ingredients and products. Additional processing equipment will facilitate new product development of value-added products including additional dehydrated vegetable powders, cubed and minced shelf-stable products, and alternative flours. It will also introduce production and storage of organic livestock feed, enabling area farms to produce more organic animal protein to be made available for consumers in the community. This project will enable access to new markets through increased processing and these new product offerings, which can include developing value-added products for other organic farms in the community. Furthermore, establishing an end-user market for organic rotational crops strengthens Great Lakes Garlic Farm’s organizational capacity and ability to process organic ingredients from other organic farms in the community and further diversifies the local food system
llm_summary: Great Lakes Garlic Farm’s project aims to significantly expand organic agricultural production and processing capabilities within Grand Traverse County, Michigan. This initiative involves the purchase and installation of additional processing equipment, specifically designed to increase capacity for dehydrating, grinding, and hand-filling spice jars, as well as establishing a dedicated facility for producing and storing organic livestock feed. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the supply of dehydrated and shelf-stable organic ingredients, alongside the development of new value-added products such as vegetable powders, cubed and minced products, and alternative flours. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors within the local agricultural sector by enabling them to produce and market more organic animal protein, and to process a greater volume of organic grains and other rotational crops. Furthermore, Great Lakes Garlic Farm intends to develop end-user markets for these crops, bolstering the farm’s operational capacity and facilitating collaboration with other organic farms in the community. This enhanced processing infrastructure and expanded product offerings will ultimately serve the needs of consumers seeking locally sourced organic goods. The project’s success will be measured by increased production volumes and broadened market access, contributing to a more robust and reliable supply chain for organic agricultural commodities within the region, and strengthening the entire local food system.

Project Summary: The goal of the project is to purchase equipment to increase the capacity of Maple Drive Farms’ gluten-free, certified organic cleaning facility. The most pressing need is to increase the capacity to clean, dehull, and separate organic buckwheat, e.g., to separate the hull from the edible groat (much like separating the meat of a nut from its shell). The funds will be used to acquire grain cleaning and processing equipment, specifically a second dehuller, a separator, new cleaning screens, a bucket elevator, ten bottom bins, a welded steel aerated grain bin, and upgraded downspouts and grain valves. The increased processing capacity and improved down spouting and valves should allow Maple Drive Farms to increase organic 32 dehulling capacity from around 50,000 pounds per year to at least 100,000 pounds per year, creating a higher product yield without compromising quality. The new storage and conveyance equipment will also substantially increase capacity to clean other organic gluten free grains, such as organic oats, soybeans, corn, and popcorn.
llm_summary: Maple Drive Farms’ project aims to significantly increase the capacity of its certified organic cleaning facility to meet growing demand for processed organic grains.
