The funds will be utilized to acquire essential equipment, including a second dehuller, a separator, new cleaning screens, a bucket elevator, ten bottom bins, and a welded steel aerated grain bin, alongside upgraded downspouts and grain valves. These investments are specifically designed to expand the facility’s ability to process organic buckwheat, enabling a projected increase in dehulling capacity from approximately 50,000 pounds per year to at least 100,000 pounds per year. Furthermore, the improved equipment will substantially enhance the facility's capacity to clean and process other organic gluten-free grains such as organic oats, soybeans, corn, and popcorn. This expansion will allow Maple Drive Farms to optimize yield and ensure a higher volume of processed organic grains are available for sale. The increased production capacity directly benefits farmers and processors involved in the organic grain supply chain, and ultimately provides greater access to processed organic grains for consumers. This project supports the efficient scaling of organic grain production, offering a strengthened market position for Maple Drive Farms and bolstering the organic grain sector as a whole.

Project Summary: The poject goal is to create a robust organic soybean market tailored to organic growers, crushers, and manufacturers in the Great Lakes Region. This initiative aims to improve market accessibility and encourage higher consumer consumption of domestic food grade organic vegetable oil. To achieve this goal, Quality Roasting (QR) plans to develop an organic soybean oil refining line with the capacity to process over 18 million pounds of organic oil per year. The refining process of soybean oil involves degumming, bleaching, and deodorization to remove impurities and enhance the oil’s quality, taste, and stability. This refining line will be an expansion of the existing soybean crush process, establishing a more extensive organic soybean market for over 1,400 growers in the region. Moreover, this project will expand the market opportunities for crude organic soybean oil by establishing a local market for the five existing soybean crush plants within the Great Lakes Region. Furthermore, the supply of refined organic vegetable oil will increase, benefiting 22 manufacturers who package the oil for consumers. QR initiated its organic program in July 2020, and there has been a remarkable increase in the production of organic soybean meal and oil. From a first- ear output of a few hundred tons, the company has scaled up to produce over 17,000 tons of organic soybean meal and oil in 2022.
llm_summary: Quality Roasting’s project aims to establish a robust organic soybean market specifically tailored to organic growers, crushers, and manufacturers within the Great Lakes Region. This initiative will achieve this by developing a new organic soybean oil refining line, designed to process over 18 million pounds of organic oil annually, incorporating degumming, bleaching, and deodorization processes to enhance the oil’s quality and stability. The project will significantly expand market opportunities for over 1,400 farmers who produce organic soybeans, while simultaneously creating a local market for the five existing soybean crush plants within the region. Furthermore, this expansion will support 22 manufacturers who package the refined organic vegetable oil for consumer sale. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in the supply of refined organic vegetable oil, benefiting both the agricultural producers and the food manufacturers. This project’s success will be measured by the volume of organic soybean oil processed and the growth in consumer demand for domestically produced organic vegetable oil. Ultimately, Quality Roasting’s endeavors will support the entire value chain, from the soybean farmers to the manufacturers, representing a key investment in the regional organic food sector.

Project Summary: The project will add additional processing capacity for creating milled organic field pea fiber. Field peas are legumes used in organic rotational cropping systems. The organic market for field peas is being developed and expanded through uses of their components including milled flours, low and high protein content proteins, starches, and fibers. Organic pea fibers are primarily used in value-added markets in a milled, flour format. When peas are processed, the outer fibrous layer is removed and separated from the inside of the pea. This outer fibrous layer is called the pea hull and is very light, taking up a lot of space for storage and is only marketable to livestock at little to no value. The proposed project will add a fiber milling line to an 33 existing organically certified pea handling facility that produces pea hulls but does not have the ability to mill the hulls into a marketable product. The proposed pea milling project will be added to an existing building footprint and be ready to process 2023 crop organic peas into organic pea fiber.
llm_summary: The proposed project aims to establish a new fiber milling line within an existing, organically certified pea handling facility, significantly expanding the potential market for organic field pea fiber. This project will add a dedicated milling operation, constructed within the facility’s current footprint, designed to process 2023 crop organic peas into a marketable fiber product. The core of this initiative involves the conversion of pea hulls – the light, fibrous outer layer removed during pea processing – into a valuable commodity. Currently, these hulls are considered a byproduct with minimal market value, representing a substantial storage challenge for farmers. By implementing this milling line, the facility will transform this byproduct into organic pea fiber, catering to demand from processors and other stakeholders within the organic market. This development will benefit farmers by providing a new outlet for their crop, while also assisting processors seeking organic ingredients. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a stream of income for farmers and the provision of a key ingredient for a variety of organic food and product applications. Ultimately, this project intends to bolster the organic market for field peas, supporting a broader range of consumers who seek organic products.

Project Summary: McKaskle Family Farm LLC is an organic processing and organic farming entity located in Pemiscot County, MO. The project will expand, modernize, and upgrade the processing, packaging, and handling by the McKaskle Family Farm LLC facility for organic rice and popcorn. This equipment will double the capacity of organic popcorn meal and organic rice flour processing and increase overall income and profitability of McKaskle Family Farm.
llm_summary: McKaskle Family Farm LLC is undertaking a significant project to expand and modernize its organic processing facility located in Pemiscot County, Missouri, with the primary purpose of increasing the production capacity for organic rice and popcorn. This initiative will involve the purchase and construction of new equipment designed to double the output of organic popcorn meal and organic rice flour, directly impacting the farm’s overall income and profitability. The upgraded facility will substantially enhance the farm’s ability to process and package these commodities, allowing for increased sales and expanded market reach. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial boost to the farm’s operational efficiency and financial performance, positively affecting the farmers involved in the production of these organic grains. The project will benefit stakeholders throughout the supply chain, including processors and distributors, by providing a greater supply of certified organic rice and popcorn ingredients. Ultimately, this expansion will support the production of valuable agricultural commodities, benefiting consumers who seek organic grains. The expanded capacity will allow McKaskle Family Farm LLC to serve a wider customer base and contribute to the availability of domestically produced organic rice and popcorn.

Project Summary: Cold Springs Organics, LLC is requesting funds to install a pelleting line at their facility near Bozeman, MT. Certified organic livestock feed has been identified as a critical barrier to growing the organic livestock market. Organic livestock farmers looking to transition to organic have been faced with record high feed prices over the past three years while organic crop producers have experienced whiplash prices for their certified organic crops. Cold Springs Organics is looking to bridge this disconnect through the expansion of its grain handling operation by purchasing, installing and operating an alfalfa and complete feed pelleting facility. This project will work to both increase the overall supply of organic feed available across Montana and the Northwest Region. It will also allow Cold Springs Organics to expand market access for both crop growers and livestock raisers. By pelletizing perennial legumes like alfalfa, and offering consistent prices to farmers year over year, they will expand the overall organic feed processing capacity in the region, offering more options to livestock producers and crop growers. Cold Springs Organics will increase market access by shipping the pelletized feed via rail. They will expand the opportunities for crop growers to sell a wide variety of leguminous and cereal feed crops that maximize the soil health of the farm all while producing livestock feed at a price point that is commercially viable for broiler, layer, hog, and dairy producers.
llm_summary: Cold Springs Organics, LLC is requesting funding to establish a critical piece of infrastructure – a pelleting line – at its Bozeman, Montana facility, designed to address a significant gap in the organic livestock feed market. This project will involve the purchase, installation, and operation of a dedicated alfalfa and complete feed pelleting facility, directly responding to the challenges faced by organic farmers seeking to transition to organic production. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to substantially increase the overall supply of certified organic feed available across Montana and the wider Northwest region, offering a commercially viable option for broiler, layer, hog, and dairy producers. Specifically, Cold Springs Organics intends to pelletize perennial legumes like alfalfa, enabling farmers to maximize soil health while producing feed that meets the demands of livestock operations. By utilizing rail transport for shipping the pelletized feed, the company aims to expand market access for both crop growers and ranchers, allowing them to sell a wide variety of leguminous and cereal feed crops. This expanded capacity will ultimately benefit stakeholders throughout the agricultural supply chain. The project’s success will be measured by increased access to organic feed for producers, contributing to the growth of the organic livestock market, and supporting the economic viability of farms and processors within the region.

Project Summary: The primary goal of this project is to propel Big Sandy Organics, LLC (BSO) towards sustainable growth and innovation within the organic market. Through strategic initiatives, BSO aims to enhance processing capacity and redefine market dynamics, fostering a resilient and thriving organic ecosystem. To achieve this, the project will focus on two pivotal objectives. First, BSO will undertake a comprehensive Processing Capacity Expansion effort. This involves the reconfiguration of its processing facility, including the removal of interior barriers and the acquisition of advanced equipment. The result will be a substantial increase in processing capacity from 150lbs to 1000lbs per hour, facilitated by streamlined automation. This capacity expansion will enhance product quality, reduce labor-intensive processes, and drive down production costs. Simultaneously, BSO will expand the organic market by promoting collaborative product development and empowering new entrants. Through close collaboration with producers and handlers, BSO will diversify its product range and invigorate innovation. The introduction of accessible continuous processing systems will break down market entry barriers, stimulating demand and encouraging new organic producers to join the fold. In essence, this project seeks to position BSO as a trailblazing force in the organic sector, marked by enhanced processing capabilities and a vibrant market landscape. By addressing current limitations and fostering collaboration, the project envisions a future where BSO stands as a beacon of organic excellence, enriching consumer choices and cultivating a sustainable organic market ecosystem.
llm_summary: Big Sandy Organics, LLC (BSO) is undertaking a strategic project designed to facilitate sustainable growth and innovation within the organic market, focusing on enhancing processing capabilities and reshaping market dynamics to establish a resilient and thriving organic ecosystem. This project will realize substantial improvements through a comprehensive Processing Capacity Expansion effort, specifically involving the reconfiguration of its processing facility, the removal of interior barriers, and the acquisition of advanced equipment, ultimately increasing processing capacity from 150 pounds to 1000 pounds per hour via streamlined automation. This expansion will improve product quality, reduce reliance on labor-intensive processes, and lower overall production costs, benefiting farmers and processors alike. Simultaneously, BSO aims to expand the organic market by fostering collaborative product development and empowering new market entrants, with the introduction of accessible continuous processing systems intended to break down barriers to entry and stimulate demand. This initiative directly supports stakeholders involved in the aggregation, processing, and distribution of organic agricultural commodities. The anticipated outcomes include increased availability of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, supporting farmers, ranchers, and food processors. By bolstering the supply chain and stimulating market activity, the project will positively impact consumers’ access to a broader range of organic ingredients, creating a more robust and vibrant organic market landscape.

Project Summary: Amaltheia Organic Dairy, LLC is seeking funding to provide wholesome, organic pasteurized goat milk to the public in this health-conscious community. Amaltheia is a sustainably focused, organic family farm that has been handcrafting organic goat cheeses for over 20 years. In 2005, the company was certified organic which aligned with the owners’ values and the needs of the public they served. While they currently only sell cheeses, they would like to expand their offerings by selling pasteurized goat milk to consumers and grocery stores. The goals of the project include 1) expanding local access to organic goat milk, 2) expanding regional access to organic goat milk, and 3) increasing resiliency of Amaltheia Organic Dairy. The funding will be used to purchase equipment for a glycol chiller, a bottler, a plate chiller, and bottles. This will allow Amaltheia to sell 2,500 gallons during the first year and increase that amount over coming years to meet demand. Offering organic milk will help address both a local and regional need in the organic market.
llm_summary: Amaltheia Organic Dairy, LLC is seeking funding to expand its operations and provide wholesome, organic pasteurized goat milk to the public, addressing a recognized need within the local and regional organic market. This project will focus on increasing access to organic goat milk for consumers and retailers alike, achieved through the purchase of essential equipment including a glycol chiller, a bottler, a plate chiller, and specialized bottles, allowing the farm to initially produce and distribute 2,500 gallons of milk annually, with the capacity to significantly increase output to meet growing demand. The anticipated outcomes of this project include expanding the availability of organic goat milk, bolstering the resilience of Amaltheia Organic Dairy, and strengthening the market for organic agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be farmers, processors, and stakeholders within the agricultural sector, as well as consumers seeking access to this particular product. Amaltheia Organic Dairy’s expansion is strategically positioned to support the needs of regional markets and the broader demand for organic dairy. By increasing production capacity and distribution channels, the farm intends to build a stronger market position and enhance its operational sustainability, ultimately supporting the continued production of high-quality organic goat milk.

Project Summary: The project purpose is to fully convert Cream of the West to 100% organic and to continue the organic expansion of sister company, Gruff, over the next three years. Activities to be performed include working with the local organic farming community to establish new connections and outlets for local organic crops, expanding access for underserved communities to organic foods, building a new sales team, attending trade shows, hiring additional plant personnel, and increasing social media and web presence. Cream of the West will educate by working with school children through local nonprofit organizations and local farmers to bolster organic processing and develop current nutritional whole food classes for an exponentially increasing audience using education and social media. The expected outcomes are an increase in current organic sales, creation of new full-time positions, and establishment of new buyers in the form of brokers, distributors, wholesalers, food service operations and retailers. The intended beneficiaries are local Montana farmers, processors, industry partners, local school children, plant staff, the community of Harlowton, Montana, and organic consumers.
llm_summary: Cream of the West’s primary purpose is to fully convert the company to 100% organic and continue the organic expansion of its sister company, Gruff, over the next three years. This project will achieve this through several key activities, including establishing new connections with the local organic farming community to secure outlets for their crops, expanding access to organic foods for a wider range of consumers, building a dedicated sales team, participating in relevant trade shows, and increasing the company’s social media and web presence. Furthermore, Cream of the West will proactively engage with the community through collaborations with local nonprofit organizations and farmers to bolster organic processing and develop educational programs for a growing audience, focusing on nutritional whole foods. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in current organic sales, the creation of new full-time positions within the organization, and the establishment of new buyers, such as brokers, distributors, wholesalers, and food service operations, alongside retailers. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative encompass local Montana farmers, processors, industry partners, plant staff, and the community of Harlowton, Montana, alongside organic consumers. The project will support the growth of organic grain and livestock feed production, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. Ultimately, Cream of the West intends to strengthen the local organic supply chain and broaden market access for organically produced goods, supporting the economic viability of Montana farmers and fostering a robust organic food system.

Project Summary: Vilicus Farms will purchase equipment to support the farm in maintaining, expanding, and creating new markets in Montana (and beyond) for organic rye, grains, legumes, organic animal feed, and organic seed. This investment significantly upgrades the farm’s seed cleaning capacity, in both quantity and quality, and increases operational efficiency by locating all cleaning equipment at one site with dedicated storage and handling. These changes enable the farm to maintain and expand direct sales of identity preserved, single origin organic rye and grains to craft distillers and farms who wish to offer grains and legumes as part of their vegetable Community Supported Agriculture (CSA’s). Screenings will be sold as animal feed, creating a new product for the farm and new farm-to-farm relationships. The farm will clean seed for on-farm use and potential sales to other farmers, to begin building a market for organic seed, which does not currently exist. Because of the limited organic processing infrastructure in Montana the farm will be able to support crop cleaning needs for other organic producers. This will help the farm and others take advantage of larger out of state market opportunities for organic grains. This project will impact at least 15 small farms and craft businesses.
llm_summary: Vilicus Farms will undertake a significant investment to enhance its capacity for the production and marketing of organic rye, grains, legumes, organic animal feed, and organic seed, ultimately supporting the farm’s growth and expansion within Montana and beyond. This project involves the acquisition of new equipment designed to substantially upgrade the farm’s seed cleaning capabilities, increasing both the quantity and quality of screenings produced. A key component of this investment is the consolidation of all cleaning equipment onto a single site, accompanied by dedicated storage and handling facilities, thereby dramatically improving operational efficiency. The anticipated outcome of this project is a strengthened position for Vilicus Farms to maintain and expand direct sales of identity preserved, single origin organic grains to craft distillers and farms utilizing grains and legumes within their Community Supported Agriculture programs. Furthermore, screenings will be utilized as animal feed, generating a new revenue stream and fostering relationships with other farms. Recognizing a critical gap in the market, Vilicus Farms will also clean seed for on-farm use and potential sales to other farmers, initiating the development of a market for organic seed. This initiative will support the farm’s ability to capitalize on larger out-of-state market opportunities for organic grains and provide essential processing support for other organic producers. The project is expected to positively impact at least fifteen small farms and craft businesses, bolstering the overall organic agricultural sector. These farmers, processors, and stakeholders will benefit from increased access to high-quality organic grains and seed, creating new avenues for revenue generation and market access. The increased capacity for seed cleaning will enable Vilicus Farms to support the organic production needs of other farms, contributing to a more robust and resilient organic agricultural supply chain.

Project Summary: Casey Bailey is a certified organic farm of about 6000 acres. The farm grows a mix of grasses and legumes and uses perennial alfalfa to offset weed cycles while adding nitrogen back to the soil. Casey Bailey grows wheat, barley, peas, lentils, chickpeas, the perennial grass Kernza, and grass finished organic cattle. The farm tends to be a 50/50 split between grasses and nitrogen fixing legumes. Currently, farm growth is limited due to a lack of storage facilities. This project will allow the farm to purchase on farm storage facilities which will enable a greater diversity of crops with improved ability to handle them efficiently. This will result in 100 fewer miles traveled for processing, an increase in annual income, 540,000 pounds more organic legumes processed on site, and a 9,000 bushel increase in storage. Overall, this project will help increase consumer access to organic legumes by increasing processing infrastructure for organic legumes. Project goals include 1) strengthening and expanding farm capacity 2) increasing consumer access to organic legumes.
llm_summary: Casey Bailey, a certified organic farm spanning 6000 acres, is undertaking a project to substantially enhance its operational capacity and market reach. The core of this initiative involves the purchase of on-farm storage facilities designed to accommodate a greater volume of crops, specifically focusing on increasing the processing of organic legumes. This expansion will facilitate the handling of a wider range of crops, including wheat, barley, peas, lentils, chickpeas, and Kernza, alongside the farm’s existing grass-finished organic cattle operation. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a reduction of 100 miles in transportation distances for processing, an increase in annual income, and the ability to process 540,000 pounds more organic legumes directly on the farm, alongside a 9,000 bushel increase in overall storage capacity. These improvements will directly benefit farmers and processors involved in the production and handling of these organic commodities. Ultimately, this project seeks to improve consumer access to a greater supply of organically grown legumes. The increased capacity will allow Casey Bailey to effectively meet growing market demand for these products, supporting the operations of farmers and processors alike.

Project Summary: Organic feed provides countless benefits to livestock and consumers alike, with outcomes including higher nutrient content, improved animal health, and environmental benefits. Unfortunately, there are few organic feed mills that meet the needs of small producers in the Southeast United States, prioritizing the use of local when possible and only domestic ingredients. This increases the demand placed on small organic feed mills. Reedy Fork Farm is already providing high quality feed to consumers in over forty states. This project’s objectives are to expand existing markets by increasing efficiency in production, by increasing storage capacity, while improving and maintaining the quality of the organic products. Reedy Fork Farm is a small organic feed mill that faces significant efficiency and storage capacity needs. This proposal will allow them to purchase equipment that will improve the quality of the product, leading to customer satisfaction and quality livestock outcomes. By implementing these objectives, Reedy Fork Farm will provide a much needed increase in access to consumers and production to support the development and expansion of new and existing markets, as evidenced by an increase of between 600,000-900,000 pounds, or a 25% increase in sales.
llm_summary: Reedy Fork Farm seeks to expand its operations to meet growing demand for high-quality organic feed, a critical need within the Southeast United States livestock market. This project will focus on increasing production efficiency and expanding storage capacity, achieved through the purchase of specialized equipment designed to enhance product quality and streamline operations. The anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in the volume of organic feed produced, projecting a rise of between 600,000 and 900,000 pounds – representing a 25% expansion in sales – which will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the organic livestock sector. Ultimately, this project will provide increased access to organic feed for consumers and support the development of new and existing markets. By strategically increasing production capacity, Reedy Fork Farm aims to solidify its position as a key supplier within the region, facilitating the growth of the organic feed supply chain and positively impacting the economic viability of operations reliant on organic ingredients. This expanded capacity will also allow for the delivery of high-quality feed to a broader customer base, ensuring consistent product availability and supporting the overall success of stakeholders within the organic livestock industry.

Project Summary: The goal of this project is to mitigate the risk of sprout damage to vulnerable organic grain crops grown for a food-grade and seed market by providing infrastructure for an on-farm grain drying system, thus enabling Horton Farm to choose a harvest window and help avoid crop loss due to pre-harvest sprouting which damages the quality of grain for food-grade application and for viable seed germination. Specifically, Horton Farm has been growing Appalachian White Wheat, a regionally adapted hard white winter wheat variety for Carolina Ground flour mill since 2018. This variety came out of the USDA-Agricultural Research Service Uniform Bread Wheat trials and has respectable yields, a good disease package, and a strong market, but as a white wheat, it lacks the dormancy period at maturity that red wheats contain, so the crop is at a higher risk of pre-harvest sprouting. To build a resilient food-grade grain-based value chain in the South, Horton Farm needs this critical infrastructure to minimize the risk of relying solely on good weather during the harvest window of June - July. Since 2012, Horton Farm in relationship with Carolina Ground, has been producing high quality stone-ground flour made from certified organic grains grown predominantly in North Carolina and surrounding southern states, and serving bakeries throughout the southeast.
llm_summary: Horton Farm’s project aims to mitigate the risk of sprout damage to Appalachian White Wheat, a regionally adapted hard white winter wheat variety cultivated since 2018 for Carolina Ground’s certified organic flour production, by constructing an on-farm grain drying system. This system will enable Horton Farm to strategically manage its harvest window, specifically during June and July, thereby minimizing pre-harvest sprouting and preserving the quality of the grain for both food-grade applications and viable seed germination. The project will provide critical infrastructure for a resilient value chain, supporting farmers in producing high-quality stone-ground flour for bakeries throughout the Southeast. The anticipated outcome is an increased capacity to consistently deliver certified organic grain, benefiting stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of this wheat. This project will directly support the producers of Carolina Ground flour, as well as the consumers who purchase their products. Furthermore, it strengthens the overall supply chain for organic grains within the region. The successful implementation of this system will enhance Horton Farm’s ability to reliably meet the demand for Appalachian White Wheat, representing a significant investment in the continued production of a valued agricultural commodity.

Project Summary: The purpose of Anchor’s processing improvement project is to increase the market for US producers by expanding organic storage and processing capabilities across Anchor Ingredients Co., LLC’s ( Anchor) supply chain through improvement of current processes and installation of new equipment. This will be done through three activities. The first is to improve the product drags at internally owned facilities. This will allow for increased efficiency in moving organic products through value-add processing, storage, and inbound/outbound transit. Anchor’s current product drags cannot be operated in certain weather conditions which causes significant downtime. Additionally, these old/malfunctioning drags leak/spill product, causing additional work to re-clean spilled product as well as unnecessary loss of product. This goal will be completed over a two-week span at Hillsboro and Buffalo, ND locations in which the old drags will be disassembled, and the new clean product drags will be re-installed. The second activity is to install and update processing equipment, over six months. The new processing equipment will expand the channel for value-added organic products and increase organic storage capacity. Prior to Anchor acquiring the facility, it was not certified organic and didn’t have processing capabilities. The third activity is to create a new organic value-added product, by installing pelletizing processing equipment. Pelletizing hulls compresses the hulls into small, dense pellets. These pellets take up less space compared to loose hulls, allowing for more efficient storage and transportation. Pelletizing will increase Anchor’s storage capacity, and decrease the number of truck shipments to customers, as trailers are able to hold more pelletized product than non-pelletized product. It also allows customers to store these pelletized hulls more efficiently, thus creating additional capacity.
llm_summary: Anchor’s processing improvement project aims to significantly expand the market for US producers by enhancing organic storage and processing capabilities throughout its supply chain. This initiative will be executed through three key activities, beginning with a comprehensive upgrade of existing product drags at the company’s Hillsboro and Buffalo, ND locations, a two-week operation involving disassembly and re-installation of new, clean product drags. Subsequently, over a six-month period, Anchor will install and update processing equipment, enabling the creation of a new organic value-added product – pelletizing hulls – which will compress loose hulls into dense pellets, dramatically increasing storage capacity and reducing the number of truck shipments to customers. The pelletizing equipment will allow customers to store these pelletized hulls more efficiently, and will increase Anchor’s storage capacity. Finally, the project will deliver increased market access for farmers and ranchers, as well as processors and other stakeholders involved in the organic agricultural supply chain, by creating a new channel for value-added organic products. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened position for Anchor and its producers, with a greater ability to meet consumer demand for organic ingredients and reduce logistical inefficiencies in the distribution of organic agricultural commodities, ultimately benefiting consumers who seek organic options.

Project Summary: Healthy Oilseeds is a small family-owned business that processes flaxseed, hempseed, borage, and other minor oilseeds. They cold press expel, mill, sift, and clean oilseeds. The products that come from processing are oils and protein, separating the organic oil from the organic protein. Healthy Oilseeds processes organic oilseeds 24 hours per day, 7 days per week and are not able to keep up with the demand for orders. The goal is to increase oilseed processing capability with the purchase of an additional head press increasing production to their facility. The expansion will also provide a larger organic market for organic producers to have another place to sell and market their organic crops. The upper Midwest is the key growing area for organic specialty oilseeds with Healthy Oilseeds being in the upper Midwest and buying directly from the producer. There is great demand for Healthy Oilseeds organic flaxseed and hempseed oil products grown and processed in the United States and they can supply these products that are certified USDA Organic and Primus Food Safety Certified. Organic producers and organic ingredient customers have trust in Healthy Oilseeds company and its products. The project will help supply the consumer demand and create a clear market channel for organic production of oilseeds to be processed close to where the seeds are grown.
llm_summary: Healthy Oilseeds is undertaking a project to substantially increase its oilseed processing capability through the purchase of an additional head press, directly addressing the high demand for its certified USDA Organic and Primus Food Safety Certified flaxseed and hempseed oil products. The expansion will allow Healthy Oilseeds to process organic oilseeds 24 hours per day, 7 days a week, significantly improving its ability to fulfill orders and capitalize on existing market needs. Anticipated outcomes of this project include a substantial increase in the supply of domestically produced organic oil and protein, benefiting farmers who grow these specialty oilseeds and processors who utilize them. Healthy Oilseeds’ enhanced capacity will provide a clear market channel for organic production, enabling farmers to efficiently market and sell their crops, while also benefiting consumers seeking these certified organic ingredients. The project directly addresses the need for increased organic oilseed processing, supporting stakeholders throughout the supply chain – from seed producers to those utilizing the final products. Ultimately, this investment will bolster the availability of certified organic oil and protein, and contribute to a more robust market for organic oilseed production in the upper Midwest region.

Project Summary: The requested equipment is intended to significantly increase the amount of NH grown organic grain and value-added grain products available in the NH and Northeast market. In 2022, Westwick Farming LLC Tuckaway Farm received and conducted a USDA Value-Added Production planning proposal surveying the growing, harvest, post-harvest, processing, and market challenges in the NH grain shed along the mid-tier value chain and the potential of growing a NH Grain Collaborative. Appropriately scaled equipment was identified as a main bottleneck in meeting and expanding this market. This equipment will address identified gaps in grain transport, processing, and packaging capacity, all of which will allow growth in the 39 marketplace for organic grain farmers and value-added producers, and increased access to organic culinary grains for consumers.
llm_summary: Westwick Farming LLC Tuckaway Farm’s project aims to significantly increase the supply of organically grown grain and value-added grain products available within the New Hampshire and broader Northeast market. The requested equipment will address critical gaps in grain transport, processing, and packaging capacity, directly supporting the growth of the marketplace for organic grain farmers and value-added producers. Specifically, this investment will provide the necessary tools to expand operations across the mid-tier value chain, encompassing growing, harvest, post-harvest handling, processing, and market distribution. The anticipated outcome is the increased availability of organic culinary grains for consumers and a strengthened position for stakeholders involved in the production and sale of these goods. The project will benefit farmers and processors by providing the means to meet current and future market demands, ultimately enhancing the volume of organic grain products accessible to consumers. This investment will bolster the capacity of value-added producers to create and market a wider range of products from organically grown grains, solidifying the position of New Hampshire as a key source for these commodities within the region.

Legal Name: THE BUTCHER BLOCK, INC. DBA NORTH COUNTRY SMOKEHOUSE
Project Summary: North Country Smokehouse (NCS) is a vertically integrated organic meat producer committed to sustainable agriculture. The purpose of this project is to introduce two new innovative organic pork products to the domestic organic market, enhance the domestic organic supply chain, and support local economies by creating and retaining jobs. Through strategic product development, supply chain enhancement, and community engagement, the project aims to create improved market accessibility and awareness of organic meat products, thereby increasing demand and consumption. While the company currently produces more than 2 million pounds of organic meat annually, the proposed project is expected to increase production capacity by 175,000 pounds annually for three years. Activities include the procurement and installation of new processing equipment, development of distinctive packaging designs, and coordination of retail merchandising to optimize product visibility. Project activities will focus on strengthening the domestic organic supply chain and elevating public awareness about organic farming through an extensive, evidencebased marketing strategy consisting of print and digital advertising, public relations, and incentives offered to wholesale distributors. Community engagement efforts will involve collaborating with local staffing agencies and technical institutes to source local production talent, advertising job opportunities to the local Claremont community, and hiring and training local residents for new production and warehousing roles. The expected project outcomes include the introduction of innovative organic pork products to the market, creation of new, full-time employment opportunities, and enhanced public awareness about organic farming, animal welfare, and sustainability. Overall, the project intends to revolutionize the organic pork market, boost domestic organic supply chain, and create local jobs. These outcomes are expected to benefit producers, buyers, and consumers, making organic products more accessible, desirable, and appreciated nationwide. An estimated 4,000 producers, 11,000 buyers, and 15 million consumers will be informed about organic products, while 12 producers will increase, and 110 buyers will execute additional business transactions to meet increased demand.
llm_summary: North Country Smokehouse (NCS) is undertaking a project to introduce two innovative organic pork products into the domestic organic market, thereby enhancing the domestic organic supply chain and supporting local economies by creating and retaining jobs. The project involves the procurement and installation of new processing equipment, along with the development of distinctive packaging designs, and coordination of retail merchandising to optimize product visibility. Anticipated outcomes include the introduction of these new products, the creation of approximately 12 full-time employment opportunities, and an enhanced level of public awareness regarding organic farming practices, animal welfare, and sustainability. NCS aims to benefit farmers, processors, and consumers by increasing market accessibility and demand for organic meat products. The project is expected to increase production capacity by 175,000 pounds annually over three years, with an estimated 4,000 producers and 15 million consumers receiving information about organic products. Furthermore, 11,000 buyers are anticipated to execute additional business transactions to satisfy the heightened demand. NCS intends to strengthen the domestic organic supply chain and elevate public awareness about organic farming through a comprehensive marketing strategy utilizing print and digital advertising, public relations efforts, and incentives offered to wholesale distributors. Ultimately, NCS seeks to revolutionize the organic pork market, benefiting all stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic meat products.

Project Summary: The purpose of this project is to strengthen Two River Gourmet Mushrooms’ rural organic specialty mushroom processing, infrastructure, and distribution. Restaurants, supermarkets, and specialty stores increasingly offer organic mushroom products, creating a demand-driven market. However, there is a clearly defined challenge centered around expanding infrastructure and capacity as well as processing, storage, specialized equipment, and handling/shipping, which have not kept up with the demand for organic specialty mushrooms. The specialized equipment will allow Two River Gourmet Mushrooms to scale processing to meet local demand and ensure reliable, safe, and exclusive Organic Delivery of its product to expanding consumers. This equipment will make certain that they are able to scale production in successful processing of high-quality organic mushrooms, meeting the demands of the target market. The dedicated delivery van will break the market access barrier that exists because of handling/shipping bottlenecks. This will also greatly streamline supply chain processes, from harvest to distribution, to reduce post-harvest losses and ensure efficient delivery of organic mushrooms to consumers. These expanded capabilities will set an example of sustainable agricultural production. It will also allow for the generation of employment opportunities within the local community, including farm workers, technicians, and sales personnel. The project's success will contribute to the economic growth of the region.
llm_summary: Two River Gourmet Mushrooms’ project aims to strengthen its operations by expanding its organic specialty mushroom processing capabilities, infrastructure, and distribution networks to meet growing market demand. This initiative will involve the acquisition of specialized equipment, including systems for processing, storage, and handling/shipping, enabling the company to scale production and ensure reliable delivery of its organic mushrooms to consumers. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in the volume of mushrooms produced and distributed, ultimately benefiting farmers, processors, and retail stakeholders who supply and sell the product. Specifically, Two River Gourmet Mushrooms intends to streamline its supply chain processes from harvest to distribution, reducing post-harvest losses and guaranteeing efficient delivery of these mushrooms to consumers. This expansion will also address existing market access barriers, facilitated by a dedicated delivery van. The overall impact will contribute to the economic growth of the region and provide employment opportunities for local stakeholders, including farm workers and sales personnel. By enhancing its processing capacity and distribution network, Two River Gourmet Mushrooms will position itself as a key supplier of high-quality organic mushrooms to meet evolving consumer preferences and support the growth of the organic market.

Project Summary: Sunny State Products, Inc. (SSP) plans to add a high-capacity electric eye color and infrared (IR) sorter to enhance the ability to clean organic food grade grain crops. As the organic food processing industry has increasingly added higher technological equipment, the need to improve the quality of organic food grains has increased substantially. Adding a color/IR sorter will allow SSP to clean and transform organic grain to the high-quality standards required by the food grade grain industry. Organic grains typically have a higher percentage of foreign material, organic matter, diseased and unacceptable kernels due to the organic growing conditions. The addition of a higher technologically advanced machine will enable SSP to accept more organic crops and convert the crops to a usable organic commodity in the food grade grain industry. 41 This project will also reduce the processing cost of the plant to provide organic food grain at a cheaper cost to current customers and to market to new customers in the organic food grade grain market. SSP will be able to provide more organic grain and incorporate more organic farmers into their already large group of organic farms to make cheaper organic food grade grains possible. New York
llm_summary: Sunny State Products, Inc. (SSP) is undertaking a project to install a high-capacity electric eye color and infrared (IR) sorter, a key investment designed to significantly enhance the cleaning and quality control processes for organic food grade grain crops. This new equipment will allow SSP to transform organic grains, which often contain higher percentages of foreign material, organic matter, and unacceptable kernels due to their origin, into a commodity suitable for the food grade grain industry. The anticipated outcome of this project is a reduction in the overall processing costs at the SSP plant, enabling the company to offer organic food grain at a more competitive price to existing customers and to attract new clients within the organic food grade grain market. Ultimately, this will facilitate the acceptance of a greater volume of organic crops and integrate more farmers into SSP’s existing network of organic farms, resulting in more affordable organic food grade grains. SSP intends to increase the availability of organic grain and support a wider range of stakeholders within the organic grain sector. By improving the quality and consistency of the processed grain, SSP aims to positively impact the businesses of processors and farmers, as well as the consumers who utilize organic food grade grain products. The project’s success will be measured by the increased throughput of organic crops and the resulting ability to meet the stringent quality standards demanded by the food grade grain industry.

Project Summary: Breadtree Farms was founded in 2019 with a mission to build the organic chestnut industry to a watershed scale in the Northeast. This project will increase organic chestnut consumption by unlocking key gaps bottlenecks that currently constrain the growth of the Northeast organic chestnut industry. Chestnuts are a historically important, high-value staple food source that has been recently marginalized in the U.S. due to the 1904 introduction of c. parasitica (chestnut blight). A century of breeding has delivered hybrid trees well-suited for commercial organic production, which can yield 1,500-3,500 lbs./acre of a nutrient-dense, gluten-free perennial starch crop. Given growing consumer interest in grain alternatives, gluten-free 43 ingredients, and local/sustainable foods, Savanna Institute identifies a present-day market opportunity for a +50,000% increase over current production. A growing number of Northeast farmers (particularly historically underserved farmers) see organic chestnut agroforestry systems as a key strategy for diversifying agricultural landscapes and enterprises. The project will conduct a feasibility/technical development study for a best-in-class, global organic chestnut processing facility and complete key improvements to a Breadtree-owned, on-farm facility to deliver processing capacity for organic chestnuts. The project will allow the purchase and installation of specialized processing, handling, storage, and distribution equipment. Also, conducting outreach at buyer-engagement events, regional local food events festivals markets, product demonstration days targeted at handlers, organic consumar package goods, food advocacy marketing professionals-Increase regional producer coordination best practices through technical workshops, farm consultation visits, webinars, focused on best practices for product consistency, marketing, post-harvest processing coordination. Through this project, Breadtree and a national coalition of partners will address: the lack of existing in-region commercial processing capacity; demand for product development and strengthened supply-chain connections between buyers, consumers, handlers and producers; the need for improved supply-chain coordination between producers by building enhanced processing capacity, developing new paths-to-market, and engaging producers, while building relationships with consumers, handlers, and culinary professionals to increase market access and consumption. These interventions would transform the Northeast’s organic chestnut industry and contribute to important strategic growth of organic chestnut industries in other U.S. regions.
llm_summary: Breadtree Farms’ project aims to significantly increase organic chestnut consumption within the Northeast by addressing critical bottlenecks in the industry’s growth. This initiative will encompass the construction of a best-in-class, global organic chestnut processing facility and key improvements to a Breadtree-owned, on-farm facility, allowing for the purchase and installation of specialized processing, handling, storage, and distribution equipment. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial expansion of organic chestnut production, projected to increase regional availability and bolster supply-chain connections between buyers, consumers, handlers, and producers. The project will directly benefit farmers seeking to diversify agricultural landscapes and enterprises, as well as consumers interested in accessing a nutrient-dense, gluten-free perennial starch crop. Furthermore, the project seeks to strengthen relationships between stakeholders across the entire chestnut value chain, enhancing market access and consumption rates. This intervention has the potential to transform the Northeast’s organic chestnut industry, establishing a new model for organic chestnut production and contributing to broader growth opportunities within the U.S. organic chestnut sector.

Project Summary: As capacity in the middle of the organic supply chain has not kept up with demand for organic products, there are a limited number of suppliers for feed grains in Central New York for dairy and livestock operations. These funds will be utilized to integrate a blower system, inventory scales, and supporting elements into the current operation at Gianforte Farm, LLC. While the facility currently grinds corn and soybeans for livestock feed, there is no efficient load out equipment for these feed commodities, leading to an overall lack of capacity and agility in the ability to supply current and future feed customers with organic feed. By integrating a continuous-flow system with the ability to efficiently load out, regional organic livestock and dairy producers will have an additional reliable, consistent, and competitive source of domestically/locally produced organic feed. This project enhances the regional organic supply chain and its resiliency, improves the local agricultural economy, and provides current and future feed buyers with additional options for purchasing domestic organic feed (which may be more cost-effective due to less transportation costs). In addition, this capacity expansion will result in an increase in purchasing of organic corn and soybeans from other local operations, thus enhancing the impact of this project while also keeping feed inputs local.
llm_summary: Gianforte Farm, LLC is undertaking a critical project to expand the capacity for organic feed production within Central New York, addressing a significant limitation in the regional supply chain for dairy and livestock operations. This initiative will integrate a continuous-flow system, incorporating blower systems, inventory scales, and associated elements, into the farm’s existing operation, which currently processes corn and soybeans for animal feed. The anticipated outcome is to significantly improve the farm’s ability to efficiently load out feed commodities, providing regional organic livestock and dairy producers with a dependable and competitive source of domestically produced organic feed. This expansion will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the organic livestock and dairy sectors, as well as supporting a more resilient supply chain. By increasing the availability of organic feed, the project aims to stimulate greater purchasing activity among stakeholders within the organic feed market. This enhanced capacity will allow for a more streamlined operation, reducing bottlenecks and increasing responsiveness to customer demands. Ultimately, the project will contribute to a more robust and reliable supply of organic feed, benefitting consumers who seek these products and furthering the economic vitality of the local agricultural community.

Project Summary: Farmer Ground Flour buys and processes a diversity of organic grain crops, paying a premium to local farmers and providing a market for organic crops not otherwise grown in New York. Farmer Ground Flour contracts with local farmers for hard wheat, which is traditionally grown in western states, to produce bread flour for the Northeast market. By shortening the supply chain and reducing food miles, the carbon footprint of their flour is reduced relative to the industry standard. This project will help Farmer Ground Flour increase its annual grain cleaning and milling capacity, increasing the volume of grain purchased. By upgrading grain cleaning and flour milling systems simultaneously, they will have greater capabilities from start to finish without bottlenecks. A new grain cleaner will enable Farmer Ground Flour to process crops for long-term storage efficiently and with less waste, and a new pair of mills will increase their hourly milling capability.
llm_summary: Farmer Ground Flour’s project aims to substantially increase its capacity for grain cleaning and milling, ultimately expanding the volume of organic crops procured from local farmers. This initiative involves the purchase and installation of a new grain cleaner, designed to efficiently process crops for long-term storage while minimizing waste, and a pair of new mills which will significantly boost the company’s hourly milling capabilities. The anticipated outcome of this project is a strengthened supply chain and reduced carbon footprint compared to standard industry practices, directly benefiting farmers who supply the company and consumers who purchase its organic flour products. By streamlining operations and eliminating bottlenecks, Farmer Ground Flour will be able to meet increased market demand, supporting a greater number of processors and other stakeholders within the organic grain sector. The project’s success will provide a reliable market for organic wheat, encouraging further investment in local organic production and strengthening the overall organic grain supply chain. This enhanced capacity will allow Farmer Ground Flour to effectively serve a growing customer base, contributing to the availability of organic flour products for consumers.

Project Summary: Norwich Meadows Farm has been one of the most important suppliers of fresh, local, organic produce to the New York City region for more than two decades. The number of viable farms providing fresh local produce to this region is small and at risk of getting smaller due to intense pressure from national/global competition and increasingly difficult business conditions. It is safe to say that there is no other local farm providing the diversity, quality, and quantity of organic produce that Norwich Meadows Farm brings to 42 market each year. One key to their success has been continuous development of new markets, resulting in a uniquely diversified marketing program including direct sales at farmers’ markets, Community Supported Agriculture’s direct sales to restaurants and retail stores, and specialty wholesale distribution. Recently Norwich Meadows Farm has partnered with commercial kitchen operators and chefs to pilot a range of processed products using vegetables and fruits from the farm; these market tests have shown that there is a significant opportunity for unique organic processed products including sauces, purees, broths, dried/pickled products, and juices to be marketed through existing channels. They have already begun the process of building a 6,000+ square foot packinghouse; this structure will also be the home of a planned food hub. This project will allow for the purchase of equipment for a commercial kitchen to be in this building.
llm_summary: Norwich Meadows Farm’s project aims to expand its capacity for producing and marketing organic agricultural commodities, capitalizing on its established market presence and unique approach to supplying fresh produce to the New York City region. This initiative will involve the purchase of equipment for a commercial kitchen, to be housed within the farm’s newly constructed 6,000+ square foot packinghouse and planned food hub. The farm is building this facility to support the development of a range of processed products, including sauces, purees, broths, dried/pickled products, and juices, utilizing the farm’s existing harvest. These processed goods will be marketed through existing channels, increasing the value of the farm’s output and benefiting farmers by creating additional sales opportunities. The anticipated outcome is a significant expansion of the farm’s operations, allowing it to meet growing consumer demand for organic food products and strengthen its position as a key supplier. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and consumers who value access to high-quality organic agricultural commodities. By increasing the volume of processed products available, the project will positively impact the agricultural supply chain and offer greater access to fresh, organic ingredients for retailers and food service establishments. The project will strengthen the farm’s ability to deliver value to its stakeholders while contributing to the overall growth of the organic food sector in the region.

Project Summary: The goal is to purchase wool equiment to create a market for wool in the horticultural industry to replace products currently used with more sustainable, certifiable organic products that will benefit both sheep and crop farmers. The only regional aggregator of wool from shearing has stopped buying wool. Sheep farming in Ohio is increasing, and with it, wool production. Coarse and low-grade wool can substitute soil amendments and weed suppression materials used in horticulture. Wool stores up to 33% of its weight in water and slowly releases water once the surrounding environment drops below 65% relative humidity, is fully degradable, contains Nitrogen, Calcium, Magnesium, Iron, Sulfur, and other Micro Nutrients. Felted wool mats can replace plastic weed barriers. They can regulate soil temperatures, prevent moisture loss, add fertilizer, act as a pest barrier to slugs and snails, and provide excellent weed prevention. Shredded wool can be mixed with seed to be a delivery method for habitat restoration, landscaping, and crop establishment. Soil and potting mixes are currently amended with peat, vermiculite, and perlite to increase the water-holding capacity and provide aeration. Adverse ecological impacts resulting from to these soil amendments include the depletion of peat bogs and the high carbon footprint of vermiculite and perlite from transportation and overseas mining operations. Wool pellets can provide aeration, hold moisture, and are naturally high in nitrogen making them the perfect slow-release, all-natural fertilizer.
llm_summary: The project aims to establish a market for wool within the horticultural industry, offering a sustainable alternative to existing soil amendment and weed suppression materials. This initiative will involve the purchase of wool equipment, specifically designed to facilitate the processing and utilization of locally produced wool. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a valuable market for Ohio’s increasing wool supply, capitalizing on its unique properties – namely, its ability to store and release water, its natural nutrient content, and its degradability. Farmers and ranchers will benefit from a viable outlet for their wool, while consumers will gain access to a natural, effective soil amendment. Wool pellets, in particular, will provide aeration and nitrogen-rich fertilization, addressing the current reliance on peat, vermiculite, and perlite, which have significant environmental drawbacks. Shredded wool can be used as a delivery method for habitat restoration and crop establishment. Felted wool mats offer a practical solution for weed prevention and soil temperature regulation. The project will support the utilization of wool as a sustainable material for horticultural applications, creating a market for this resource and reducing the environmental impact associated with traditional soil amendment practices, ultimately benefiting stakeholders involved in agricultural production.

Project Summary: In 2022, U.S. farmers produced more than 2.35 billion tons of grain feed to serve domestic and international livestock producers (USDA Economic Research Service). Still, less than 1% of the grain feed produced in the United States is organic, despite strong and consistent growth in U.S. demand for organic food. With more than 82% of U.S. households buying organic products regularly (Organic Trade Association), the Organic Center notes that driven by growth in demand for U.S. organic livestock feed the U.S. has become a substantial net importer of organic products. In fact, U.S. imports of grain feed have steadily increased over the past decade, growing from 40% in the 2011/2012 crop year to 60% in the 2021/2022 crop year. This is primarily due to the major barriers that exist to producing, processing, and marketing organic grain feed, namely higher costs of production and lack of processing and marketing infrastructure. To meet current U.S. consumer demand and expand opportunities to build the U.S. organic grain feed market, Grange Cooperative will perform the following activities: 1) expand its processing capacity to create more and better markets for organic producers and 2) execute marketing and promotional activities that will help to build commercial markets for U.S. organic grain feed products. This project’s goals (deliverables and expected outcomes) include achieving 2,000 additional tons of organic grain feed processed and a $1,655,000 increase in domestic organic grain feed sales by the end of the project period.
llm_summary: Grange Cooperative will undertake a project focused on expanding the U.S. organic grain feed market to meet growing domestic and international demand. The core activities of this project include expanding processing capacity to create enhanced market opportunities for organic producers, alongside the execution of targeted marketing and promotional initiatives designed to establish robust commercial markets for U.S. organic grain feed products. This initiative anticipates achieving a significant increase in the supply of organic grain feed, specifically aiming to process an additional 2,000 tons and generate a $1,655,000 rise in domestic organic grain feed sales by the conclusion of the project period. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the production and distribution of grain feed. Ultimately, this project intends to benefit consumers who seek organic livestock feed options, and a broader range of stakeholders within the agricultural industry. By increasing the volume and availability of U.S. organic grain feed, Grange Cooperative will contribute to meeting existing market needs and support the growth of the organic livestock sector within the United States.

Project Summary: Camas County Mill has been certified organic since inception of the mill in 2011. Organic is an important and rapidly expanding part of their mill business. Organic farming is important to Camas County Mill because it provides wholesome food to people with minimal disruption to the soil. Camas County Mill currently processes organic wheat, spelt, rye, emmer, oats, and buckwheat. These are all milled into flour as well as flakes. Currently, they operate four 950mm Engsko mills producing flour as well as a Roastech roaster flaker that produces flaked grains. This project will allow Camas County Mills to purchase equipment to meet increasing demand for healthier organic options. They are currently providing the grains intact with hull and bran to consumers. Having the ability to dehull and pearl barley themselves will 45 increase their organic offerings. The goals of this project include: 1) increasing interest and access to ancient grains in the form of pearled organic grains, 2) furthering organic grower base with organic crop options, 3) increasing resiliency of Camas County Mill and other organic farms, and 4) increasing consumer access to organic meat. This project will allow Camas County Mill to increase annual gross income, increase processing capacity by 15%, and increase the number of organic products processed by 125,000 pounds.
llm_summary: Camas County Mill has initiated a project to significantly expand its organic grain processing capabilities, driven by increasing consumer demand for healthier food options and a desire to bolster the organic agricultural sector. This project will see the purchase of equipment enabling the mill to dehull and pearl barley, thereby increasing its organic offerings and expanding its product line. The anticipated outcomes of this initiative include a 15% increase in processing capacity, the processing of 125,000 additional pounds of organic products annually, and a substantial increase in annual gross income. These improvements will directly benefit farmers supplying the mill with organic grains, as well as consumers seeking access to a wider range of organic grain products. The project’s success will also strengthen the resilience of Camas County Mill and other organic farms within the region. By facilitating the production of pearled barley, Camas County Mill will better serve the needs of processors and other stakeholders involved in the organic grain supply chain. Ultimately, this project aims to broaden access to organic grains for consumers and solidify Camas County Mill’s position as a key player in the organic food market.

Project Summary: The Oregon Organic Coalition will lead a multi-sector project to grow the market for organic products from the Pacific Northwest (PNW). This project represents a major collaboration with partners including the Oregon Department of Agriculture, Organically Grown Company, Hummingbird Wholesale, the Good Food Foundation, Tilth Alliance, the Oregon Farm-to-School & School Garden Network, and others to promote Oregon and Washington-produced organic food and strengthen organic market channels. Its purpose is to drive consumer demand for organic products and expand valuable markets for organic producers, targeting the specialty/craft food and farm-to-school markets. While building organic market position across the entire food sector, it will focus on products with identified opportunities for significant growth, including barley and other grains, fruits and vegetables, hazelnuts, and wine grapes. Key activities will include assisting organic producers to become market-ready for wholesale sales, supporting their attendance at trade shows, and connecting them to buyers with values-based purchasing goals. Partners will also conduct strategic communications to educate consumers about the organic label and the benefits of organic food, strengthen organic food in the PNW identity and brand image, and build demand for crops and varieties that are regionally adapted, high-performing, and profitable for organic producers. The project will benefit organic producers through improved value chain coordination, promotion, and increased connections to high-value markets. It will also benefit small and mid-scale craft food manufacturing businesses, people served by farm-to-institution programs, and the public, through greater access to organically produced food.
llm_summary: The Oregon Organic Coalition will lead a comprehensive project designed to significantly grow the market for organic products originating from the Pacific Northwest. This initiative, a major collaboration involving organizations like the Oregon Department of Agriculture, Organically Grown Company, Hummingbird Wholesale, the Good Food Foundation, Tilth Alliance, and the Oregon Farm-to-School & School Garden Network, focuses on expanding market channels for Oregon and Washington-produced organic food, with a particular emphasis on specialty and craft food manufacturing businesses. The project’s primary goal is to drive increased consumer demand for organic products, specifically targeting high-growth opportunities within key agricultural sectors, including barley and other grains, fruits and vegetables, hazelnuts, and wine grapes. To achieve this, the Coalition will support organic producers in becoming prepared for wholesale sales and facilitate their participation in trade shows, effectively connecting them with buyers who share values-based purchasing goals. The anticipated outcomes include enhanced value chain coordination and increased access for farmers to high-value markets, bolstering the position of organic food within the region’s identity and brand image. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be the farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the organic food supply chain, as well as consumers who will gain greater access to organically produced food. By strategically promoting regionally adapted, high-performing, and profitable crops, the project aims to strengthen the organic sector and improve overall market dynamics.

Legal Name: Cascade Pacific Resource Conservation and Development
Project Summary: The Oregon Organic Hazelnut Collective (OOHC) will develop a brand for Oregon Organic Hazelnuts and create educational marketing materials to be distributed to stakeholders in the hazelnut industry as well as to food and health influencers. The project objectives include 1) creating and distributing branded educational materials on the benefits of domestically grown organic hazelnuts in comparison to similar products 2) securing long-term customers that can purchase large volumes of hazelnuts each year through events and marketing campaigns for restaurants, community markets, influencers, etc. and 3) addressing 46 the infrastructure bottleneck in the supply chain. These materials would 1) educate stakeholders and consumers on the ethical and environmental issues surrounding imported nuts 2) advertise the health and environmental benefits of organic hazelnuts versus other nuts and nonorganic hazelnuts, and 3) ensure that consumers who purchase products with this label know that their hazelnuts originate from domestic, sustainable, and ethical sources. With these branded educational materials, the OOHC will increase the visibility of this crop at local markets, festivals, and food and health fairs. With an increased public presence, OOHC aims to establish lasting relationships between health and environmental influencers, American hazelnut growers, and small business owners, who can purchase larger quantities of hazelnuts each year. Effective branding, distribution of marketing materials, and events showcasing organic hazelnuts will have the long-term effect of addressing infrastructure bottleneck issues that currently exist in the supply chain. While hazelnut farmers can increase their harvest, when they attempt to develop independent sales channels, they are turned away by processors who are not interested in shelling and returning small batches of hazelnuts. With an increased demand in the market, there would be an opportunity for farmers to increase their production and for a new processing plant devoted to organics to come online.
llm_summary: The Oregon Organic Hazelnut Collective will develop a brand and educational marketing materials to elevate the visibility and market access for Oregon Organic Hazelnuts. This project aims to increase the demand for domestically grown organic hazelnuts by creating branded materials that educate stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and consumers, regarding the benefits of choosing Oregon Organic Hazelnuts compared to imported alternatives. Specifically, the OOHC will produce marketing materials highlighting the ethical and environmental advantages of sourcing hazelnuts within the United States. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is to secure long-term purchasing commitments from restaurants, community markets, and health and environmental influencers, ultimately contributing to a strengthened market position for Oregon Organic Hazelnuts. Furthermore, the project seeks to address a supply chain bottleneck by encouraging increased hazelnut production amongst farmers and stimulating the development of a new processing plant dedicated to organic hazelnuts. The beneficiaries of this project include Oregon hazelnut farmers seeking expanded sales channels and processors interested in handling small batches of hazelnuts. Ultimately, the increased public awareness generated through this brand and marketing campaign will support sustainable production and market development within the hazelnut industry, leading to greater accessibility and demand for domestically grown organic hazelnuts.

Project Summary: Pocono Organics intends to increase the production of Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC) microgreens for processing into a value-added freeze-dried microgreen powder called PowerGreens. The processing method, combined with appropriate packaging systems, extends the microgreens’ shelf life exponentially, maintains their high-nutritive attributes, protects the product’s food safety, and supports the product quality of an innovative organic product. The equipment requested for processing and packaging will expand product market potential to nationwide retail and wholesale outlets through unique channels. It will ensure the shelf stability of increased production quantities and reduce energy consumption for storage and distribution by eliminating refrigeration needs. The product will be sold directly to consumers through physical and online stores and additional regional and national retailers. Various sized packaging options will expand organic market opportunities for wholesale target markets including juice bars, fitness centers, bakeries, dietary supplement companies, and health care institutions. A mixture of hemp, broccoli, and sunflower microgreens are grown in two-week successions, year-round using greenhouse operations. This production system supports the USDA’s climate smart action goals by minimizing water usage and carbon emissions in a controlled indoor environment. The PowerGreens processing results in a nutrient-rich organic food source that can be produced and aggregated throughout the entire year, providing expanded market opportunity to organic farmers during colder months and creating strong supply chain security. The equipment requested will improve production and processing efficiencies resulting in minimal product loss, safe product preservation, and expanded organic market potential.
llm_summary: Pocono Organics intends to significantly expand the production of Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC) microgreens, specifically a two-week succession of hemp, broccoli, and sunflower varieties grown year-round within a controlled greenhouse operation, to create a value-added product: PowerGreens. This project involves the acquisition of specialized equipment for processing and packaging these microgreens, designed to dramatically extend their shelf life, maintain nutritional integrity, and safeguard food safety while simultaneously reducing energy consumption by eliminating refrigeration needs. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in the market potential for PowerGreens, allowing for distribution through national retail channels, including juice bars, fitness centers, bakeries, dietary supplement companies, and healthcare institutions, alongside direct sales to consumers via physical and online stores. This expanded production capacity will benefit farmers and processors alike, creating a more secure supply chain and addressing a critical need for organic ingredients.
