The equipment will minimize product loss, ensure safe preservation, and ultimately boost the organic market opportunities for these stakeholders. The resulting PowerGreens product represents a nutrient-rich organic food source readily available throughout the year, providing a key market access point for organic agriculture, and supporting the growth of the organic ingredient sector within the food industry.

Project Summary: The PA Flax Project (PAFP) is a woman-owned cooperative business whose mission is to reestablish the fiber flax industry in Pennsylvania by initiating new organic production and processing capacity. Through this project, PAFP will engage with the beginning, middle, and end of the fiber flax supply chain. Growing high-quality fiber flax has a proven history in Pennsylvania, yet there is little to no infrastructure dedicated to the harvest and post-farm processing of fiber flax in the country – often called the ‘missing middle’. As it stands, PAFP sees no way to bring Pennsylvania's fiber flax to market. PAFP will support and educate producers, and work to build out the middle of the supply chain bringing Pennsylvania's organic flax for linen to market through planning and research of a long line fiber flax scutching mill. PAFP envisions this cooperatively owned mill providing an additional income stream to producers after their crop leaves the farm. With the support of partners, PAFP hopes to open the door to this high-value market for Pennsylvania farmers and manufacturers, putting 12,000 acres of organic fiber flax into production. PAFP will leverage its industry connections to establish contracts for domestic and international buyers of fiber flax and coproducts produced in its cooperatively owned mill. This project aims to establish the first complete organic fiber flax supply chain in the Eastern U.S.
llm_summary: The PA Flax Project (PAFP) aims to reestablish the fiber flax industry in Pennsylvania by initiating new organic production and processing capacity, addressing a critical gap in the supply chain. This project will focus on establishing the first complete organic fiber flax supply chain in the Eastern U.S., encompassing the acquisition of land for organic flax cultivation, and the development of a long-line fiber flax scutching mill – a facility designed to process flax into valuable fibers. Anticipated outcomes include the production of approximately 12,000 acres of organic flax, which will then be processed and made available for use in manufacturing. The primary beneficiaries of this project are Pennsylvania farmers, processors, and manufacturers who will gain access to a high-value market for their flax and coproducts. Furthermore, this initiative will support the development of a robust domestic supply chain, increasing the availability of organic fibers for various applications. The project seeks to create economic opportunities for farmers and establish a sustainable market for Pennsylvania-grown flax, ultimately benefiting consumers seeking organic materials for textiles and other products. Through the construction and operation of the scutching mill, PAFP intends to generate additional revenue streams for producers and strengthen the overall viability of the fiber flax industry in Pennsylvania.

Project Summary: Tuscarora Grain CO LLC (TGC) will purchase and install a Century Pellet Mill. This mill will increase local capacity for pelletizing currently underutilized organic byproducts into new value-added products with ready markets. The project will build the organic livestock feed supply chain capacity, remove barriers to new organic market development, and benefit organic producers by accomplishing the following: Objective 1: Install organic-approved pelletizing equipment capable of processing 24 tons per day. Objective 2: Improve organic supply chain capacity and organic product development in Pennsylvania by providing thirdparty processing to local organic producers and feed mills. Objective 3: Increase the Pennsylvania organic community’s access to organic amendment by 2.500 tons per year. These objectives will empower local organic grain producers and feed mills to engage with new markets through access to previously unavailable contract pelletizing. It will create a new market for domestically produced organic byproducts 48 by expanding TGCs capacity for processing, aggregation, and distribution. Additionally, it will reduce potential waste from grain and animal processing by offering value-added product development opportunities.
llm_summary: Tuscarora Grain CO LLC (TGC) will undertake a project focused on increasing local capacity for pelletizing currently underutilized organic byproducts into new value-added products with established markets. The core of this initiative involves the purchase and installation of a Century Pellet Mill, a piece of equipment designed to process 24 tons of organic material daily. This project anticipates a range of positive outcomes, including the expansion of the organic livestock feed supply chain and a significant increase in the availability of organic amendment within Pennsylvania – specifically aiming to deliver 2,500 tons annually. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be local farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the organic grain and livestock feed sectors. By providing access to contract pelletizing services, TGC will empower these businesses to engage with new markets, effectively reducing potential waste from grain and animal processing and fostering the development of valuable, domestically produced organic products. Ultimately, the project seeks to strengthen the organic supply chain and support the growth of organic operations throughout Pennsylvania, creating new opportunities for the sale of organic products and improving access to markets for local producers.

Project Summary: Snipes Farm and Education Center requests funds to produce organic, value-added products. Snipes Farm is USDA/PCO Certified Organic and runs a successful on-farm market and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) membership program. The Center has organic produce contracts with senior centers, hospitals, and social service agencies, to address hunger relief and food insecurity in the region. Snipes has experienced increased demand for its organic produce over the past 5 years and needs to add organic value-added products to their offerings. Products include tomato & hot sauces, applesauce, berry jams, pickled vegetables, teas, herbs, herbal products, and dehydrated products. Improved equipment will initiate the 49 production of value-added organic products for its customers. In the past 5 years the Center’s overall organic produce sales increased 20%. At their on-farm market, Snipes sells value-added products bought in from other local farms and producers (honey, syrup, apple butters, herbal products), but none are certified organic. As one of the few certified organic farms in the area, the Center is well positioned to meet customer demand for organic value-added products, except for the for lack of efficient production equipment. The Center’s overall organic vegetable sales have increased 155% since 2015 due to contracts to grow and deliver food. They employ regenerative agriculture methods to address soil health and climate change concerns.
llm_summary: Snipes Farm and Education Center is seeking funding to establish a new line of organic value-added products, capitalizing on the farm’s existing USDA/PCO Certified Organic status and successful on-farm market and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program. The project will involve the purchase and installation of improved equipment specifically designed to facilitate the production of approximately 49 items, including tomato & hot sauces, applesauce, berry jams, pickled vegetables, teas, herbs, herbal products, and dehydrated products, expanding the farm’s offerings beyond fresh produce. Anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in overall organic produce sales, building upon the farm’s five-year growth of 20% in organic vegetable sales and the current contracts it holds with senior centers, hospitals, and social service agencies, representing a crucial avenue for addressing food insecurity within the region. These efforts will directly benefit farmers and processors by creating new market opportunities for their certified organic goods, while simultaneously providing a wider range of organic products to consumers. The project will directly address the need for additional market paths and supports the production of goods for sale at the farm’s on-farm market, which currently sources value-added products from other local farms. The anticipated outcome is a significant expansion of the farm’s reach and ability to serve its existing customer base, as well as attract new consumers seeking organic options. Ultimately, Snipes Farm and Education Center aims to strengthen its position as a key supplier of certified organic goods within the region, supporting a reliable source of food for its beneficiaries.

Project Summary: The proposed project outlines a transformative shared-services Farmgate-to-Market channel marketing system in Southeastern North Carolina, focusing on the constrained availability of organic crops. The initiative targets small, beginning, disadvantaged, and BIPOC farmers, strategically addressing economic disparities, social equity, and sustainable farming practices. The project aims to empower underserved communities, stimulate economic growth, and enhance climate-smart agriculture. Centered on a 150-mile radius from Wallace, NC, the project targets an area with low per capita income and a significant BIPOC population. It aims to fill market gaps for limited-availability organic crops like specialty beans, peppers, and herbs. By establishing a shared-services model, the project fosters collaboration among farmers, providing access to resources, transportation, marketing, and expertise. This approach empowers farmers, enhances efficiency, and reduces costs, ensuring direct market channels and incentives for organic producers. Partnerships with local organizations, agricultural offices, and community leaders ensure engagement and address historic disparities. The project supports disadvantaged communities by connecting farmers directly to purchasers, expanding markets, and increasing consumption of locally produced organic products. The project boasts a seasoned team with expertise in agriculture, supply chains, and marketing, collaborating with local partners for a holistic approach. Overall, the project aims to create a lasting positive impact by empowering marginalized farmers, fostering sustainability, and promoting equity opportunities in Southeastern North Carolina.
llm_summary: The proposed project aims to establish a transformative shared-services channel marketing system focused on Southeastern North Carolina’s limited organic crop availability, specifically targeting small, beginning farmers, those facing economic challenges, and those from BIPOC communities. This initiative will focus on filling market gaps for specialty crops such as beans, peppers, and herbs within a 150-mile radius of Wallace, NC, an area characterized by lower per capita income and a significant population of the targeted groups. The project will foster collaboration among farmers by providing access to transportation, marketing support, and expert advice, ultimately increasing the efficiency and reducing the costs associated with reaching market channels. Anticipated outcomes include expanded market access for these farmers, boosting the volume of locally produced organic products available to consumers. The project’s intended beneficiaries include the farmers themselves, as well as those seeking to purchase these goods. Furthermore, the project seeks to create a robust network of stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of these crops. This system will support the growth of local processing operations and improve the overall supply chain for organic agricultural commodities within the region, supporting the economic viability of the farmers and connecting them directly with purchasers. The project’s success is predicated on strengthening local agricultural production and increasing the availability of organic products within the target area.

Project Summary: Plants to Food is a manufacturing service partner for plant-based food brands. They bring over 25 years of manufacturing expertise and excellence in the areas of product formulation, testing, labeling, packaging, distribution, and more. Plants to Food has been cooking, blending, infusing, and packaging premium food products for over 25 years. In addition to product and packaging capabilities, they also offer R&D, labels, and nutritional software that creates nutrition fax panels per FDA guidelines. Plants to Food’s temperaturecontrolled production facility is state-of-the-art with an innovative warehouse management process. This includes a dedicated pick and pack fulfillment line for direct-to-consumer and a separate pallet racking system for storage and carrier pallet loads. As the company continues to expand, they are constantly looking for new ways to accommodate growing demands. This project will include the purchase of a Rotary Fill and Seal Machine for Premade Doypack as well as a Piston Filler for Liquids and Pastes. This machine will increase processing by roughly 12,000 units per month. It will allow Plants to Food to take on seven new customers and supply four new jobs at its factory. Overall, Plants to Food will see a 10% increase in processing with this new machinery. With this purchase, its factory will see an increase in processing capacity by 4,500 pounds a month. As Plants to Food continues to grow, it receives an influx of orders beyond what the facility can currently produce. As a co-manufacturing business, this new equipment will not only help expand Plants to Food processing but also the processing of the various organic food companies they are partnered with.
llm_summary: Plants to Food is undertaking a significant expansion project to bolster its manufacturing capabilities and meet growing demand for plant-based food products. The core of this project involves the purchase of a Rotary Fill and Seal Machine for Premade Doypack, alongside a Piston Filler for Liquids and Pastes, representing a substantial investment designed to dramatically increase processing capacity. This equipment acquisition is projected to elevate processing volume by approximately 12,000 units per month, enabling Plants to Food to accommodate seven new customer accounts and fulfill four existing jobs within its factory. Furthermore, the enhanced machinery is anticipated to result in a 10% overall increase in processing, adding 4,500 pounds of product monthly. These improvements will benefit farmers, processors, and stakeholders within the organic food industry by allowing Plants to Food to handle larger volumes and support a wider range of product offerings. The expanded capacity will positively impact the food supply chain, offering greater options for consumers seeking plant-based goods. This project directly supports the production of organic ingredients, which ultimately strengthens the positions of the farmers and ranchers involved in supplying those ingredients.

Project Summary: Berrybrook Organics, LLC (Berrybrook) is a certified organic farm and value-added processing company. Throughout their 24 years producing and marketing organic value-added grains, meats, and eggs, their reputation for product quality and consistency has earned them a loyal customer base, extensive marketing experience, and valuable relationships with wholesale clients. The equipment requested addresses two needs: supply chain management/improvement through the purchase of a delivery vehicle, and processing efficiency through the purchase of an Egg Grader machine for organic egg processing. Berrybrook currently supplies Grade A organic eggs to two local grocery stores and nine Sioux Falls wholesale and retail customers. Last year, about 95% of total eggs produced were sold to these outlets. In addressing these two areas of need, Berrybrook will reach new organic markets, increase processing efficiency for their organic goods, and ensure a quality, safe organic product to consumers.
llm_summary: Berrybrook Organics, LLC is undertaking a project to enhance its operations and expand its market reach through strategic investments in key equipment. The core of this project involves the acquisition of a delivery vehicle to improve supply chain management and efficiency, alongside the purchase of an Egg Grader machine specifically designed for the processing of their organic eggs. These investments are anticipated to yield significant outcomes, including the ability to supply existing local grocery stores and nine wholesale and retail customers with a consistent and high-quality organic product, while also opening pathways to reach new organic markets. Ultimately, Berrybrook’s efforts will benefit farmers and ranchers who provide organic grains and livestock products, as well as processors and stakeholders involved in the organic food sector. The project will directly support consumers seeking organic food options and contribute to the overall growth of the organic agricultural industry by streamlining operations and increasing production capacity. Berrybrook Organics aims to strengthen its position as a reliable supplier of organic products, bolstering the availability of these commodities to a wider range of customers and contributing to the expansion of the organic market.

Legal Name: Tiffany Leigh Stanley (A Different Chick Farm & Orchard)
Project Summary: A Different Chick Farm and Orchard (ADCFO) has been growing produce since 2016 and has been certified organic since 2020. They are known for their hot pepper processing and have developed a line of spice blends, hot sauces, and pepper jelly made from their produce. The processing of these products can easily triple the value of the produce over fresh sales alone. The goals of this project are to purchase equipment to allow for greater processing volume of hot sauces and spice blends and deliver them to a wider geographic region in northeast Tennessee, western North Carolina, and southwest Virginia, including regional grocery outlets. This project aligns with the program purpose by increasing domestic organic supply chain capacity, expanding capacity for processing, and improving the ability to comply with regulatory requirements and quality standards. Additionally, it will allow access to processing equipment for other organic producers in the area.
llm_summary: A Different Chick Farm and Orchard (ADCFO) is undertaking a project focused on expanding its capabilities for processing organic produce and increasing its market reach. The project involves the purchase of equipment specifically designed to enhance the volume of hot sauces and spice blends that ADCFO produces, utilizing their certified organic peppers. Anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in the value of the farm’s output through processing, moving beyond fresh sales and establishing a broader distribution network across northeast Tennessee, western North Carolina, and southwest Virginia, targeting regional grocery outlets. This expansion will benefit farmers and processors by providing new market avenues for their organic peppers, increasing the overall value of the agricultural commodities produced. The project aims to improve ADCFO’s ability to meet regulatory requirements and maintain quality standards, thereby supporting the operational efficiency of the farm. Ultimately, the success of this initiative will positively affect stakeholders within the region by providing access to a wider range of organically processed spice products and contributing to a strengthened local supply chain.

Legal Name: RKH GIN LLC, dba Woolam Gin
Project Summary: RKH Gin LLC, dba Woolam Gin is a primarily woman owned ginning facility that has processed organic cotton for 33 years, being the first United States to do so. It is located in a high poverty area in Lynn County, Texas and serves other high poverty areas including Dawson and Terry Counties. Woolam Gin is seeking a grant award to purchase and install equipment to expand the services and improve processing to increase production of organic cotton for farmers which will improve overall market production of the beneficial product. The overarching project purpose is to improve efficiency, therefore improving outcomes for farmers and the organic market. The equipment will increase production from 25 bales an hour to up to 40 bales an hour. The increase in processing will improve the housing time of cotton in the warehouse which will improve the grades and facilitate earlier entry into the marketplace, benefiting farm producers, processors, and consumers. The faster processing will improve turnaround for the farmer and further increase production possibilities. The primary partners and collaborators of the project will include participating organic farmers, the project manager, project supervisor, gin manager and other supporting human resources workers. This grant award will create improved markets and expand processing capacity which in turn will enrich market availability and further development of production resources and production.
llm_summary: Woolam Gin is seeking a grant award to purchase and install equipment that will expand its organic cotton processing services, aiming to increase production efficiency and ultimately benefit farmers and the organic market. The project will equip the facility with machinery designed to elevate production from the current rate of 25 bales per hour to a potential capacity of 40 bales per hour. This expansion is crucial to improving the housing time of cotton within the warehouse, which will positively impact the grades achieved and facilitate earlier entry into the marketplace for processors and ranchers. By accelerating the processing timeline, Woolam Gin will significantly improve turnaround for farmers, unlocking greater production possibilities and bolstering the overall market availability of organic cotton. The anticipated outcomes include enhanced market access for cotton producers and improved access to this valuable commodity for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers in Lynn County, Texas, and surrounding areas including Dawson and Terry Counties, as well as the processors and stakeholders involved in the organic cotton supply chain. Woolam Gin’s investment will directly contribute to strengthening the organic market and supporting the production of this agricultural commodity.

Project Summary: Steelbow Farm is seeking to broaden its delivery range and increase local food access and supply chain resilience by procuring a delivery vehicle. The overarching purpose of the proposed project is to expand access to local, organic produce by eliminating the current constraint of distance and delivery radius, while simultaneously addressing the growing demand for product in the current marketplace. Currently, Steelbow Farm has demand for their product that exceeds their capacity because they do not have a vehicle and therefore have a limited delivery range. This bottleneck is hampering Steelbow Farm’s ability to rise to the organic market demands. They believe access to this equipment would drastically improve access to organic produce, as they could radically increase their customer base and range. For context, currently, within Travis County, only .06% of food is produced locally. The Austin and Travis County areas are seeing a decline in the amount of vegetable farms and farmland, which are disappearing at an alarming 16.8 acres a day. Amidst these startling statistics, this business is thriving and demand for their produce is extremely high. Steelbow Farm wants to be able to meet the market demand and fill the gap within the local food system. As organic vegetable producers, they are striving to increase the percentage of local food consumed within their community.
llm_summary: Steelbow Farm is undertaking a project to broaden its delivery range and increase local food access, aiming to address a critical bottleneck in the supply chain for organic produce within Travis County and the wider Austin area. The primary purpose of this project is to procure a delivery vehicle, which will enable Steelbow Farm to significantly expand its reach and meet the growing demand for its organic products. This acquisition represents a key step in fulfilling market demands and addressing the diminishing local food production landscape, where farmland is disappearing at an alarming rate. Anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the availability of locally sourced organic vegetables and fruits, directly benefiting farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders within the agricultural sector. By expanding its delivery capabilities, Steelbow Farm intends to become a more prominent supplier of organic produce to consumers and processors seeking reliable access to high-quality, locally grown goods. The project directly supports efforts to bolster the local food system and increase the proportion of locally consumed agricultural commodities. Ultimately, Steelbow Farm’s success will contribute to strengthening the entire ecosystem of local food production and distribution, facilitating greater access to fresh, organic food for a variety of consumers and supporting the continued operation of related businesses.

Legal Name: Armagh Fine Foods LLC dba Armagh Creamery
Project Summary: The primary goal of this project is to enhance and expand the production capabilities of Armagh Creamery organic farming and dairy operations. By acquiring essential equipment, the project aims to achieve increased efficiency, product diversification, and expanded distribution. This equipment will enable Armagh Creamery to venture into new product lines, including heavy cream and butter, expand production of existing products, and streamline the production process, reducing the workload on current employees and enhancing overall efficiency for creating new butter product lines. The acquisition of a delivery vehicle will significantly improve distribution capabilities, allowing Armagh Creamery to reach local retailers and drop locations in Central, North, and West Texas. This expansion will promote the availability of organic dairy products to a wider consumer base. The specific objectives of this project are two-fold: 1) to scale yogurt production to the full daily capacity of 10,000 units per day, two days a week. This increase will enable the creamery to supply more retailers throughout Texas and cater to the growing demand in the direct-toconsumer market and 2) to expand raw milk and cream production to 600 gallons a day for 3-4 days a week, resulting in a weekly output of 1800 to 2400 gallons. This expansion will further support the directto-consumer market and provide ample resources for the planned heavy cream and butter product lines.
llm_summary: Armagh Creamery’s primary purpose is to enhance and expand its organic farming and dairy operations through strategic equipment acquisition, aiming to significantly increase production capabilities and broaden distribution channels. The project will involve the purchase of essential equipment, including a delivery vehicle, to support a range of operational improvements. Anticipated outcomes include scaling yogurt production to 10,000 units per day, two days a week, and expanding raw milk and cream production to 600 gallons a day for 3-4 days a week, resulting in a weekly output of 1800 to 2400 gallons. This expansion will allow Armagh Creamery to effectively supply more retailers throughout Texas, strengthen its position in the direct-to-consumer market, and provide ample resources for planned heavy cream and butter product lines. The project is designed to benefit farmers, processors, and consumers by increasing the availability of organic dairy products. The anticipated increased production volume will provide greater supply to retailers and direct-to-consumer channels. Furthermore, the acquisition of a delivery vehicle will dramatically improve distribution capabilities, allowing Armagh Creamery to reach local retailers and drop locations across Central, North, and West Texas, thereby supporting the operation of the creamery and benefiting stakeholders within the agricultural sector. This expanded capacity for organic dairy production represents a key initiative to meet growing consumer demand for these products.

Project Summary: Triple J Organics is a minority-owned certified organic citrus orchard in Mission, Texas established in 1995. Triple J manages 25 acres of certified organic citrus groves, primarily of Ruby Red grapefruit and early season oranges, as well as Navel Oranges, Meyer Lemons, Tangerines, and Tangelos in smaller quantities. This project will increase consumption of locally produced organic orange juice in the Rio Grande Valley and increase the profitability and long-term viability of Triple J Organics through special purpose equipment purchases that allow Triple J to process 32,000 lbs. of “waste”, or seconds, oranges into fresh juice and deliver it safely to customers in the Valley. The project will target school districts as potential customers, as well as supermarkets, restaurants, health food stores, daycare facilities, and eldercare facilities as needed. Beneficiaries include Triple J Organics, local schools and businesses who purchase the new product, as well as other organic citrus growers in the Valley who may be able to cooperate and aggregate to produce a higher margin value-added product.
llm_summary: Triple J Organics, a certified organic citrus orchard established in Mission, Texas in 1995, is undertaking a project to increase the consumption of locally produced organic orange juice within the Rio Grande Valley and bolster the company’s long-term viability. This initiative centers around the purchase of specialized equipment designed to process 32,000 pounds of “seconds” oranges—fruit that doesn't meet typical market standards—into fresh juice. The project anticipates a significant increase in the availability of this juice for consumers and businesses within the Valley, including school districts, supermarkets, restaurants, health food stores, daycare facilities, and eldercare facilities. The primary beneficiaries of this project include Triple J Organics, local schools and businesses who will purchase the new product, and other organic citrus growers in the Valley who may collaborate to increase the value of their production. Furthermore, this project aims to establish a new market channel for citrus fruit, offering a solution for surplus oranges and enhancing the economic prospects for citrus farmers and processors. The anticipated outcome is a heightened demand for fresh, locally sourced organic orange juice and a strengthened position for Triple J Organics as a producer and distributor within the regional market. This will create a valuable product for stakeholders and contribute to the overall economic strength of the citrus industry in the Rio Grande Valley.

Project Summary: The Texas Department of Agriculture (TDA) will use a multi-faceted approach to promote local organic producers in the produce, grains, dairy, and fiber markets. Though these industries are each unique in their production, the issues they experience are similar. These challenges include, but are not limited to, lack of knowledge among consumers of each industry’s availability/benefits, existing gaps between producers and buyers that result in barriers for growth, and an absence of public resources that assist organic farmers from promoting themselves more efficiently. Through this project, TDA will increase local consumer knowledge, support activities to develop new markets, increase demand for domestically produced organic agricultural products, and provide additional market paths for organic farmers in Texas. Goals of this project include: 1) increase public knowledge of Texas organic agriculture industry, 2) provide opportunities to improve market share and sales of local organic producers, and 3) build new connections between Texas producers and potential buyers to accomplish these goals. TDA Marketing will produce new marketing materials targeted for the organic industry, assist organic producers with attending trade shows relevant to their respective industries, facilitate business to business interactions, and run a social media campaign that highlights each industry. These activities will strengthen the relationships between Texas organic 54 crop/product producers and buyers, as well as better inform the public on the availability and benefits of Texas organic products. These relationships would aid in ongoing efforts to strengthen the supply chain, build on current opportunities with Texas agriculture associations, assist historically underserved communities, and increase demand for locally produced organic products. To further assist the organic industries of Texas, TDA will assist in the production of the Field View Organics program. This program aims to identify organic operations across the state and mark them for aerial spraying companies to help prevent potential chemical drift or contamination of organic crops. By supporting this initiative, TDA will protect the current organic producers across the state and alleviate potential concerns for new members wanting to enter the industry.
llm_summary: The Texas Department of Agriculture will implement a comprehensive project to bolster local organic producers across the produce, grains, dairy, and fiber markets. This initiative will focus on increasing public knowledge of Texas organic agriculture, supporting activities designed to improve market share and sales for local organic producers, and establishing new connections between Texas producers and potential buyers. Specifically, TDA will produce targeted marketing materials, assist producers in attending relevant trade shows, and facilitate business-to-business interactions, alongside a social media campaign showcasing the benefits of Texas organic products. The anticipated outcomes include strengthened relationships among organic farmers and buyers, and increased demand for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. Key beneficiaries of this project will be Texas farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the organic agriculture sector. A significant component of this project is the Field View Organics program, which will identify organic operations for aerial spraying companies to mitigate potential chemical drift and contamination, thereby safeguarding existing producers and encouraging new entrants into the industry. By fostering expanded market opportunities and safeguarding the integrity of organic production, the Texas Department of Agriculture aims to elevate the status and profitability of local organic agriculture within the state.

Project Summary: This project aims to increase the American consumer awareness of organic yaupon tea as a replacement for imported tea via the food service sector. An Organic Yaupon Marketing Plan will increase opportunities for consumer exposure to organic yaupon tea while also allowing for additional customers, buyers, and parties to participate in the domestic organic yaupon tea industry. Yaupon is a caffeinated plant native to North America and rich in polyphenols and antioxidants like imported tea. By using a hybrid of traditional tea preparation methods, organic yaupon tea has an almost indistinguishable flavor profile from imported green and black tea served in both hot and iced tea. Cat Spring Yaupon has created a cohesive marketing and outreach plan to increase the amount of organic yaupon tea served in restaurants, cafes, hotels, and spas. This plan incorporates the opportunity to promote and support additional organic yaupon producers through the American Yaupon Association while also supplying to tea companies who would otherwise be selling imported tea to their food service customers. This will also allow restaurants to substitute imported tea on their menus with organic yaupon tea thus giving their customers and guests an opportunity to sample and fall in love with the incredible domestic organic yaupon tea.
llm_summary: Cat Spring Yaupon is undertaking a comprehensive marketing initiative designed to elevate consumer awareness of organic yaupon tea as a viable alternative to imported tea products within the food service sector. This project centers on increasing the availability of organic yaupon tea through strategic partnerships with restaurants, cafes, hotels, and spas, with the ultimate goal of substituting imported tea selections on menus and offering consumers a premium domestic option. The core of this initiative involves establishing relationships with processors and farmers to secure a consistent supply of certified organic yaupon tea, supporting the growth of the domestic organic yaupon tea industry. Anticipated outcomes include a significant rise in the consumption of organic yaupon tea, benefiting farmers and stakeholders involved in its production, and expanding market opportunities for domestic organic agricultural commodities. By facilitating the substitution of imported tea with organic yaupon tea, Cat Spring Yaupon aims to positively impact consumers who seek a flavorful and healthful beverage choice. The project directly assists processors by providing a new sales channel and strengthens the overall supply chain. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, processors, and consumers who desire access to a high-quality, domestically produced tea option.

Project Summary: Spicy Organic LLC, a dedicated provider of premium organic spices, herbs, and grains, proposes to purchase and install machinery equipment to streamline its production processes, enhance efficiency, and expand market reach. The proposed equipment will significantly boost processing capabilities, reduce manual labor, and improve the availability of organic ingredients in both domestic and emerging markets. By introducing a semi-automatic auger filler machine, production output is projected to increase substantially from 60 pouches to 900 pouches per hour. This advancement will not only result in enhanced efficiency and productivity but also bolster the domestic market demand for the company’s organic ingredients. The Band Sealer will mark a significant leap towards improving overall efficiency and output. As pouches are sealed seamlessly and rapidly, Spicy Organic anticipates an increase in processing efficiency, enabling them to explore untapped markets and create new avenues for expanding the demand for their organic ingredients. The inclusion of a forklift machine will revolutionize this aspect of the company’s operations. With the ability to efficiently move and store organic ingredients, Spicy Organic expects a notable surge in production output. The inkjet coding machine and conveyor system are poised to streamline this process, augmenting efficiency, and output. This will ensure precise and timely labeling, bolstering the availability and marketability of their products within the domestic market. The proposed enhancements will not only elevate processing efficiency but also facilitate entry into untapped markets, increasing the demand for Spicy Organic’s premium organic ingredients.
llm_summary: Spicy Organic LLC proposes a significant investment in new machinery equipment designed to substantially improve its production processes and expand its market reach for premium organic spices, herbs, and grains. The core of this project involves the acquisition of a semi-automatic auger filler machine, projected to increase production output from 60 to 900 pouches per hour, alongside a band sealer, an inkjet coding machine, a conveyor system, and a forklift machine. These additions are anticipated to dramatically boost processing capabilities, minimize reliance on manual labor, and create a more efficient system for managing the storage and movement of organic ingredients. Specifically, the auger filler will allow for a substantial increase in the volume of pouches produced, while the band sealer and related equipment will streamline the sealing process, contributing to heightened operational efficiency. The forklift machine will revolutionize the movement and storage of ingredients, ensuring a smoother flow throughout the production process. Furthermore, the inclusion of the inkjet coding machine and conveyor system will allow for precise and timely labeling, boosting the availability and marketability of Spicy Organic’s products within the domestic market. These improvements are expected to benefit farmers, processors, and ultimately, consumers who seek high-quality organic ingredients. By increasing production capacity and improving operational efficiency, Spicy Organic aims to meet growing market demand and expand its reach within the organic ingredients sector, contributing to a broader availability of these goods.

Project Summary: The Organic Marketing Institute (OMI) expands the marketplace for organic agricultural products by supporting innovative certification programs that extend the third-party organic certification baseline into novel product categories. OMI promotes third-party certifications that enhance National Organic Program (NOP) standards and offer transparency and full supply chain traceability while benefiting the environment. The Organic Plus Trust (OPT) Certified Grass-Fed Organic Livestock Program has set the first national standard for grass-fed, organic ruminant livestock production for meat and dairy that builds upon USDAcertified organic dairy standards and helps differentiate farmers’ products. An end-to-end, third-party certification, it verifies all production and handling of certified products from farm through processing to sale. Grass-fed Organic Certification has seen initial producer interest and customer satisfaction due to the market stability, transparency, trust, and climate benefits of the products certified. There is demonstrated need and opportunity to scale the certification as a value add for organic producers, retailers, and customers. With funding from USDA, OMI will support farmers and brands, having the OPT Grass-Fed Organic Certification, with expanded marketing and promotional support. OMI will do this by enhancing supplier relationships, creating a marketing strategy that promotes the climate benefits, third-party integrity, full-supply chain traceability and regenerative characteristics of the products, and executing robust consumer marketing efforts. With these efforts, to grow the market for Grass-Fed, organic dairy products, supporting an additional 50 farmers per year and engaging an additional 10 brands over the course of the grant.
llm_summary: The Organic Marketing Institute (OMI) is undertaking a project to expand the marketplace for organic agricultural products by supporting innovative certification programs focused on enhancing the standards for grass-fed, organic ruminant livestock production. This initiative will establish the OPT Grass-Fed Organic Certification, a comprehensive, end-to-end third-party verification system encompassing all stages of production – from the farm through processing and sale – for certified organic dairy products. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased market stability, enhanced transparency, and strengthened consumer trust within the organic sector, particularly for grass-fed organic products. Specifically, OMI will provide expanded marketing and promotional support to farmers and brands holding this certification, with the goal of supporting an additional 50 farmers and engaging an additional 10 brands over the course of the grant. This will benefit stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and consumers, by offering a clear pathway to market for high-quality organic dairy products. The project aims to increase consumer awareness and demand for these products, ultimately driving growth within the organic dairy industry. The success of the program hinges on fostering strong supplier relationships and executing targeted marketing campaigns that highlight the inherent value of the certification – its full-supply chain traceability, integrity, and the positive characteristics of the produced goods. This expanded market opportunity will provide greater access to consumers who prioritize these attributes, supporting the viability of organic dairy operations and contributing to a more robust organic marketplace.

Project Summary: Grain farming is returning to the region, and the tide is rising. There are a growing number of bakeries and distilleries in Vermont and the region needs organic grain that is grown and processed locally. Many farmers cannot grow grain because they lack the capacity to clean, dry, and/or store grain. The grain drying machine and grain cleaning machine will be a great help and be used to process the grain of many farms. The purchase and installation of more efficient grain drying and cleaning equipment to replace less efficient equipment and hand labor will allow Thornhill Farm to 1) accept and purchase more organic grain from farmers on the day of harvest, and after, to dry and clean the grain, 2) to support the re-emergence of local and regional grain production in Vermont, New York, and Maine, 3) to inc usrease local organic grain market availability by making a greater amount of grain and flour available on the market for baking and spirits, and 4) to ultimately, support Northeastern grain farmers, organic agronomy and soil health, and increase regional grain markets, all of which help mitigate climate impacts through reducing climate miles, increasing organic agronomy practices, reducing exposure to flooding and drought through water-soil interactions, and sequestering carbon.
llm_summary: Thornhill Farm’s project aims to bolster the resurgence of local grain production within Vermont, New York, and Maine by acquiring and installing more efficient grain drying and cleaning equipment. This investment will enable the farm to accept and purchase organic grain directly from farmers upon harvest and in the subsequent days, facilitating the drying and cleaning of this grain. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in the availability of organic grain and flour for use by bakers and spirit producers, thereby expanding the regional market for these products. Specifically, Thornhill Farm will contribute to supporting Northeastern grain farmers and strengthening the organic agronomy practices within the region. The project will improve local grain markets, with the goal of reducing transportation distances and positively impacting soil health through enhanced water-soil interactions. Ultimately, this initiative will support the increased production of organic materials, benefiting farmers, processors, and other stakeholders throughout the Northeast. By providing a reliable source of processed organic grain, Thornhill Farm seeks to establish a more robust and localized supply chain, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and supporting a greater volume of organic goods available for market consumption.

Legal Name: Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont
Project Summary: The Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont (NOFA-VT), in partnership with Vermont Way Foods (VWF) and Food Connects (FC), proposes to grow, and develop markets for Vermont’s organic producers in three ways 1) expanding access to promising identified markets throughout the Northeast by developing sales channels to large retailers and other wholesale buyers with consumer bases that are validated by 56 market research to value and support the qualities inherent in Vermont organic food, 2) by developing new dairy, maple, and other Vermont organic wholesale products to be branded and marketed under the VWF brand and distributed regionally by FC, and 3) increasing consumer awareness and demand for organic food through targeted marketing and promotions in Vermont and throughout the Northeast. Key outcomes include new and expanded wholesale markets for Vermont organic producers, including an overall increase in the percentage of organic products sold through the Food Connects food hub, and increased sales of VWF organic products. Additionally, the project will result in increased awareness of and preference for locally produced organic food among regional consumers. Key beneficiaries of the project include organic dairy producers, organic dairy processors, additional food hubs (certified organic handlers), and organic maple producers. As VWF scales its production and increases sales capacity, they expect these initial producers to see increased sales to VWF, and ultimately, for VWF to onboard additional producers and processors. The project will leverage support from Migrant Justice to support the coordination of Milk with Dignity certification of VWF dairy products which aim to engender consumer trust in the values-aligned brand.
llm_summary: The Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont (NOFA-VT), in partnership with Vermont Way Foods (VWF) and Food Connects (FC), proposes a project focused on expanding market access for Vermont’s organic producers through three key strategies. Specifically, the project will develop new sales channels to large retailers and wholesale buyers across the Northeast, leveraging existing market research to validate the quality and value of Vermont organic food. Simultaneously, VWF will establish new dairy, maple, and other Vermont organic wholesale products, branding and marketing them under the VWF brand and distributing them regionally through FC. Furthermore, the project aims to increase consumer awareness and demand for organic food through targeted marketing and promotional efforts within Vermont and throughout the Northeast. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of new and expanded wholesale markets for Vermont organic producers, a resulting increase in the percentage of organic products handled through the Food Connects food hub, and increased sales of VWF organic products. The primary beneficiaries of this project are organic dairy producers, organic dairy processors, organic maple producers, and additional food hubs (certified organic handlers). The project will support the growth of VWF’s production capacity, with the expectation that initial producers will see increased sales to VWF, leading to the potential onboarding of further producers and processors. This initiative seeks to bolster the market for Vermont’s organic agricultural commodities, ultimately benefiting farmers and consumers alike. The project will facilitate the efficient aggregation, processing, and distribution of Vermont organic products, contributing to a strengthened regional organic food supply chain.

Project Summary: This project will increase the domestic and international market share for organic wines produced in Washington State and it will double the capacity of Wilridge Winery’s production facility, thereby increasing the local market for USDA certified-organic wine grapes in Washington generally, and in the Yakima area specifically. By increasing demand and, therefore, the premium paid, for USDA certified-organic wine grapes, the project will encourage other wine-grape producers in Washington to initiate the USDA organic certification process. Starting with a market study and the development of a marketing plan in year one, Wilridge Winery will identify the factors constraining the expansion of organic Washington wines into the growing organic wine market. At the same time, the project will double the capacity of Wilridge Winery’s USDA certified-organic processing facility in preparation for the implementation of the marketing plan. In year two Wilridge Winery will implement its marketing plan to persuade wine distributors (wholesalers), retailers, and consumers to purchase more organic Washington wine. The marketing plan will include intentional outreach to the highly diverse local viticulture community in the Yakima area which includes beginning farmers, socially disadvantaged farmers, limited-resource farmers, and tribal farmers. As a mentor in the Northwest Transition to Organic Partnership Program (TOPP), Wilridge Winery is committed to fostering strong connections in the local supply chain. By increasing the market share for organic Washington wines, this project serves the organic community at large by expanding the organic wine market, expanding the market for locally grown wine grapes, and encouraging partners to pursue organic certification.
llm_summary: Wilridge Winery’s project aims to substantially increase the market share for organic wines produced in Washington State and to double the capacity of its processing facility, thereby bolstering the local market for USDA certified-organic wine grapes within the Yakima area. The core of this initiative involves a two-year plan beginning with a comprehensive market study and the development of a detailed marketing plan designed to persuade wine distributors, retailers, and consumers to increase their purchases of organic Washington wine. Simultaneously, Wilridge Winery will be constructing a significantly expanded processing facility, increasing its production capacity to meet anticipated demand. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a substantial rise in market share for organic wines from Washington State, alongside an increase in the volume of locally grown wine grapes sold. This project will directly benefit wine-grape farmers, processors, and other stakeholders within the wine industry, as well as consumers seeking organic wine options. By increasing demand, Wilridge Winery intends to incentivize other wine-grape producers in Washington to pursue USDA organic certification, further expanding the overall market for certified organic agricultural products. The project’s success will be measured by a demonstrable increase in the availability and sale of organic wine grapes, contributing to a stronger and more robust local wine industry.

Project Summary: The Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (PSFHC) is a farmer owned cooperative, incorporated in 2016, with a mission to support and champion local, family scale farms by providing a direct connection with buyers in the region seeking high quality, locally produced food. PSFHC member-producers include over 80 farmers, ranchers, and value added agricultural producers providing products sourced from the Puget Sound region of Western Washington. PSFHC purchases produce from its member-producers and then markets, sells, and distributes to a diverse customer base. PSFHC is focusing on the development of a strategic financial plan for sustainable expansion. This plan includes development of processing services that will add value to member-producers products, and provide them with enhanced and competitive market access. The strategy addresses the critical need for an efficient means to prepare certified organic and conventional produce for sale as fresh cut or frozen. The 50% of produce sold through PSFHC is certified organic, the forthcoming certification of its facility will ensure organic segregation strategies comply with use of this equipment towards producing certified organic products. PSFHC will utilize funds to purchase appropriate processing equipment that will create the capacity for the organization to provide this needed service as they expand member-producers' benefit offerings.
llm_summary: The Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative is undertaking a strategic project focused on sustainable expansion and enhanced market access for its member-producers, comprising over 80 local farmers, ranchers, and value-added agricultural producers throughout the Puget Sound region of Western Washington. This initiative will see the purchase and implementation of specialized processing equipment, specifically designed to prepare certified organic and conventional produce for sale as fresh-cut or frozen goods, addressing a critical need within the region’s agricultural supply chain. The anticipated outcome is to significantly increase the value of member-producers’ products by offering a prepared product line, ultimately benefitting farmers and increasing their sales potential. The Food Hub will create capacity for certified organic segregation strategies, ensuring compliance with equipment usage and facilitating the production of certified organic products. The cooperative’s strategy aims to bolster the ability of its stakeholders to meet consumer demand for prepared agricultural products, thereby benefiting both processors and consumers. Through this project, the Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative seeks to expand its reach and improve the overall efficiency of the regional food system, providing access to new market opportunities for its members and supporting the success of the agricultural community.

Legal Name: Lukens Farms, Inc. DBA Grace Harbor Farms
Project Summary: Grace Harbor Farms is a vertically integrated farm and food business. From the farm to the grocery store, they control their products through every stage of the supply chain. They sell wholesale and deliver directly 80% of their volume, using a distributor for the other 20% of clients that they cannot service easily themselves. Grace Harbor Farms is a trusted name in the greater Puget Sound area and have established a strong relationship with PCC Natural Foods, Whole Foods, Safeway, Albertsons, QFC, Fred Meyer, Town &Country, Haggen, and local independent Co-Ops. There is a strong demand for their conventional milk products and Grace Harbor Farms is now ready to partner with their organic dairy neighbors to bring more 58 organic dairy products to market. The addition of this equiment will allow Grace Harbor Farms to meet that demand.
llm_summary: Grace Harbor Farms is undertaking a project to significantly expand its offerings of organic dairy products, driven by strong market demand within the greater Puget Sound area and a strategic partnership approach. This initiative involves the purchase of specialized equipment designed to support the increased production capacity required to meet anticipated consumer requests for organic dairy. The anticipated outcome of this project is a substantial increase in the availability of organic dairy products, catering directly to the established customer base of Grace Harbor Farms, which includes wholesale distributors and retail partners such as PCC Natural Foods, Whole Foods, Safeway, Albertsons, QFC, Fred Meyer, Town &Country, Haggen, and local independent Co-Ops. This expansion will benefit farmers and ranchers involved in the production of organic dairy, as well as consumers seeking these products. Grace Harbor Farms intends to work closely with its organic dairy neighbors to optimize production and distribution, ensuring a wider range of organic dairy options are accessible to the market. Ultimately, this project aims to bolster the supply of organic dairy, strengthening Grace Harbor Farms’ position as a trusted supplier and providing more options for stakeholders in the agricultural and food sectors.

Project Summary: Snowgrass Farm, woman-owned and located in rural Eastern Washington, seeks to purchase equipment with implements to expand processing and post-harvest activities in the winter months by providing access to their high tunnels during the winter and enabling them to grow year-round, increasing yearly production by 30%. The equipment will enable Snowgrass Farm to transport produce, planting materials, the washing, packing, processing, and storage of harvested crops. With winter access, they can grow continuously harvestable crops in their 2,760 sq ft heated tunnel, producing over 1,000lbs of produce the first winter. Improved accessibility will also increase spring production with earlier planting in both the heated and nonheated tunnels. Snowgrass Farm will sell directly to its rural community through local grocers and food banks, while also creating winter farm positions. This region does not have any organic farmers growing in winter despite the demand. Currently, Snowgrass doesn’t grow between October and April due to cold 59 temperatures and heavy snowfall. While a propane heater in a high tunnel was installed, the tunnels remain blocked by snow and inaccessible for propane refilling.
llm_summary: Snowgrass Farm, a rural Eastern Washington operation, seeks to secure equipment to significantly expand its processing and post-harvest activities, specifically to capitalize on access to their high tunnels throughout the winter season and increase overall yearly production by 30%. The project involves the purchase of equipment designed to facilitate the transportation of produce and planting materials, as well as the washing, packing, processing, and storage of harvested crops. With this investment, Snowgrass Farm anticipates producing over 1,000 pounds of produce during its first winter season within its 2,760 square foot heated tunnel, a substantial increase given the current limitation of operations between October and April due to cold temperatures and snowfall. This equipment will allow for continuous harvesting and production, ultimately benefiting local farmers and consumers by providing a consistent supply of fresh produce. The project aims to address a critical market need in the region, where there is currently no organic production occurring during the winter months. By increasing spring production through earlier planting in both heated and nonheated tunnels, Snowgrass Farm intends to supply local grocers and food banks, supporting the livelihoods of regional stakeholders and expanding market access for their products. The anticipated outcomes include a measurable rise in overall production and the establishment of a viable winter operation, strengthening the farm’s position within the local food system.

Project Summary: Through this project, Mainstem Malt will launch a new certified organic malt line that coordinates an ecologically responsible grain value chain from farmer to buyer. As a unique Certified B Corp malt company sourcing exclusively from Salmon-Safe certified farmers, Mainstem came to market in 2017 to provide regional producers with a premium market for grains being grown with exceptional water quality and habitat conservation practices. Since its founding, the company has made significant purchases of domestically grown Northwest grain all while retaining elevated transparency throughout the grain valuechain and simultaneously developing the market for domestic malt. Mainstem Malt aims to build upon this successful model to develop expanded markets for certified organic grain producers in the Cascadia Region. Together with a diverse set of partners, Mainstem Malt will increase domestic organic supply chain capacity for organic barley. The project will accomplish this by expanding expert staff capacity, building, and maintaining relationships with certified organic growers and processors, establishing new markets for organic malt, and developing and executing a marketing plan that differentiates organic, regionally grown, and produced malt to both buyers and end consumers. Mainstem Malt has commitments from certified organic and transitioning-to-organic growers who recognize the value of barley within a feed grain rotation and are seeking high-end markets for their crops as well as long-standing relationships with certified organic craft beverage makers. Paired with a growing demand for organic in the craft beverage sector, Mainstem Malt is eager to build out this important regional market.
llm_summary: Mainstem Malt is undertaking a project to launch a new certified organic malt line, aiming to establish an ecologically responsible grain value chain from farmer to buyer within the Cascadia Region. This initiative will focus on increasing domestic organic supply chain capacity by expanding relationships with certified organic growers and processors, establishing new markets for organic malt, and executing a targeted marketing plan that differentiates organic, regionally grown, and produced malt to both buyers and end consumers. The project anticipates creating greater demand for domestically produced organic barley and expanding market access for farmers who are utilizing barley within a feed grain rotation and seeking high-end markets for their crops. Key to this endeavor is securing commitments from certified organic and transitioning-to-organic growers, alongside longstanding relationships with certified organic craft beverage makers, capitalizing on the growing consumer interest in organic products within the beverage sector. Mainstem Malt expects to strengthen the position of processors and other stakeholders involved in the organic grain supply chain, ultimately benefiting consumers who seek high-quality malt products. By facilitating the production and distribution of certified organic malt, Mainstem Malt will support the economic viability of regional agricultural operations and contribute to a robust domestic market for organic goods.

Legal Name: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics
Project Summary: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics is an organic family farm in rural eastern Washington. The farm grows, packs, and sells fruit. Production has expanded in response to a greater demand for quality local organic fruit from buyers, doubling the volume of fruit to process and sell. There is a need to increase packaging capacity. The project proposes to purchase a small packing line to wash and dry the fruit, rather than manually cleaning the fruit by hand. This will benefit the farm, its employees, other producers, buyers, and the local community. This will allow River Valley Organics to expand its markets to include additional 60 buyers and sell more fruit to current buyers. In addition, this will allow the business to offer packing services to other local organic growers, expanding their markets as well. Fruit availability, quality and freshness will be enhanced by packaging it in a timely manner. Employees will be able to sort and weigh the cleaned fruit instead of wiping each piece clean, which will be less physically demanding. By shifting job duties, River Valley Organics will be able to retain employees while increasing output. The estimate is that with this equipment, they can package four times as much fruit in a day as they currently do, making it more cost-effective. This will allow River Valley Organics to pack 600 boxes per day (according to manufacturer data), rather than the maximum 150 per day currently possible by hand-wiping each piece of fruit. By becoming more economically sustainable, the business will be able to continue to provide employment to local people in this impoverished rural area.
llm_summary: George J Otte DBA River Valley Organics is undertaking a project to significantly enhance its fruit packing capabilities through the acquisition of a specialized washing and drying packing line. This investment addresses the farm’s expanded production volume, doubling the amount of fruit processed and prepared for sale, and directly responds to increased demand from buyers. The anticipated outcome of this project is a fourfold increase in daily fruit packaging capacity, enabling the farm to process a maximum of 600 boxes per day, compared to the previous maximum of 150 boxes achieved through manual wiping. This expansion will allow River Valley Organics to serve an additional 60 buyers and improve the availability and freshness of its products for existing customers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farm’s employees, who will be able to perform more efficient sorting and weighing tasks, and the broader group of farmers and processors involved in the local organic fruit supply chain. Furthermore, this enhanced capacity will allow River Valley Organics to provide packing services to other local organic growers, thereby broadening market access for these producers and strengthening the overall organic agricultural sector. The increased output from this project will improve the economic viability of River Valley Organics and support continued employment opportunities within the rural community, benefiting the local economy and supporting the livelihoods of those involved in the production and distribution of organic fruit.

Legal Name: Bickford Farms Inc. dba Meadowlark Organics
Project Summary: This project’s goal is to expand the on-farm cleaning and handling capacity to facilitate market pathways for diversified organic grain growers in the Upper Midwest. Bickford Farms Inc. dba Meadowlark Organics has successfully cultivated certified organic, food-grade grains and run a wholesale and direct marketed flour business since 2016. Significant progress has been made toward addressing the need for grain cleaning and storage infrastructure in the region by constructing granary (grain cleaning facility) and on-farm flour mill, Meadowlark Community Mill. Vertical integration enables storage, cleaning, milling, packaging, and distribution from a single location. One-third of the 1,000-acre farm produces culinary grains, and an additional $150,000 of grain are sourced annually from regional farmers to meet demand. A flour mill produces and distributes approximately 13,000 pounds of flour per week. Together, they make locally grown organic grain accessible across the Upper Midwest. While the existing infrastructure has enabled growth, Meadowlark Organics’ granary needs a gravity table, optical sorter, and connecting bucket elevator to clean a wider variety of grains with improved precision, and increased capacity. These purchases will serve area farmers who are seeking markets for their diverse crops such as wheat, rye, corn, buckwheat, and dry beans. With this funding, it will enhance grain cleaning equipment, and strengthen partnerships with local organic farmers. This project will advance market paths for domestic organic agricultural producers, contribute to crop rotation diversity, and promote sustainable farming practices in this region.
llm_summary: Meadowlark Organics’ project aims to expand on-farm cleaning and handling capabilities to facilitate market pathways for diversified organic grain growers in the Upper Midwest. This initiative involves the purchase of critical equipment, including a gravity table, an optical sorter, and a connecting bucket elevator, to enhance the precision and capacity of the Meadowlark Community Mill. The organization’s existing infrastructure, encompassing a granary and flour mill, already supports the processing of approximately 13,000 pounds of flour weekly and the handling of 1,000 acres of culinary grains, supplemented by an additional $150,000 of grain sourced annually from regional farmers. The anticipated outcome is increased access to locally grown organic grain for a range of crops such as wheat, rye, corn, buckwheat, and dry beans, benefitting farmers and processors seeking viable market options. This project will strengthen partnerships with local organic farmers and create a more robust supply chain for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. Ultimately, the expanded capabilities will serve a broader range of stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic grains, contributing to increased availability and demand for these products across the region.

Project Summary: The DeLong Co., Inc. (DeLong) has spent 35 years working in the organic market, building, and maintaining relationships with producers, transportation companies, and end users. DeLong aims to revolutionize the consumption of domestically grown organic grains and livestock feed. The project provides direct access to the Union Pacific Railroad and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, which offer seamless connectivity to all Class 1 railroads in the U.S. Through critical investments in infrastructure, equipment, and transportation capabilities, the project aims to address the barriers of limited storage capacity, inadequate quality control measures, segregation challenges, traceability, and transportation constraints while stimulating increased demand for organic products within the U.S. This project is expected to create over 36 million pounds of organic corn demand by increasing current storage capacity by 140,000 bushels, implementing proper equipment to segregate organic corn from conventional corn, and adding railcars throughout the threeyear project duration. The project seeks to create positive impacts for organic grain producers within DeLongs customer base. DeLong has purchased organic grain from 697 producers in Wisconsin and Illinois, 70 of whom are small producers with less than 300 acres of land. Providing producers with increased benefits is of the utmost importance to DeLong. Ultimately, DeLong hopes to share these project findings and successes with existing and future producers to both eliminate entry barriers and provide a net increase in domestic consumption of organic grain.
llm_summary: DeLong Co., Inc. has initiated a project to revolutionize the consumption of domestically grown organic grains and livestock feed, addressing critical barriers within the supply chain. This ambitious undertaking centers around strategic investments, including the acquisition of direct access to the Union Pacific Railroad and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, alongside the construction of new infrastructure, equipment, and the addition of railcars, totaling approximately 140,000 bushels of increased storage capacity over the three-year project duration. The primary goal is to stimulate a significant increase in demand for organic products, specifically aiming to generate over 36 million pounds of organic corn demand. DeLong’s efforts will directly benefit farmers and ranchers who supply organic grain, as well as processors and other stakeholders involved in the organic feed market. By expanding storage capacity and implementing segregation measures for organic corn from conventional corn, DeLong will enhance quality control and traceability throughout the supply chain. The project anticipates a net increase in domestic consumption of organic grain, ultimately supporting producers who currently supply DeLong with organic grain from 697 producers, including 70 small producers with less than 300 acres of land. DeLong’s intention is to share these project findings and successes with existing and future producers, effectively eliminating entry barriers and fostering growth within the organic grain market.

Project Summary: Over the past three years, craft malt processing has grown by nearly 10 million pounds and is expected to continue increasing in the coming years. This means since 2019, craft malt production in North America has grown by 60% according to research conducted by the Craft Maltsters Guild. To date, there are no craft malt operations in Wisconsin, much less an organic craft malt operation. Currently, organic craft breweries purchase their grain and malt from out of state or even abroad. Other craft breweries are not necessarily able to trace their malt to the Midwest region. This project seeks to develop a craft malt operation in Wisconsin, the first of its kind. This operation will secure local grains from farmers in Wisconsin and process the grains into malt to be used by local craft breweries in the state. Craft malting is on the rise nationwide, and there is currently a void in Wisconsin to fill the gap between grain farmers and the abundance of craft breweries in the state. This malt operation in collaboration with a local farmer has a 500lb batch capacity to start and can directly be entirely purchased by a local craft brewer in Madison, WI. The equipment will enable Meristem Malt to take grain from surrounding farms to clean, process, and then transport the finished malt product to craft breweries and distilleries. The operation might expect to produce 8-10 tons of quality malt per week in future expansions in line with the capacity of other craft malt houses across the 62 country. The malt would go to craft breweries and distilleries, and over time could grow into a market for home brewers. The deliverable will be processed local grain as malt and delivered to a local craft brewery for testing and brewing. These brewers who value the opportunity to use local ingredients are beneficiaries, as well as the local farmers seeking to sell organic barley in the future. This creates a local value-added market for organic grain growers while allowing brewers to connect with a local product and use it to tell a value chain story.
llm_summary: Meristem Malt’s project seeks to establish the first craft malt operation in Wisconsin, addressing a significant gap in the regional supply chain for craft breweries. This initiative involves the construction of a facility capable of producing high-quality malt from locally sourced grains, beginning with a 500-pound batch capacity and designed to scale up to potentially 8-10 tons per week. The operation will acquire grain from nearby Wisconsin farms and transform it into malt, directly supplying local craft breweries and distilleries with a regionally produced ingredient. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of a local value-added market for organic grain growers and increased access to fresh, local ingredients for brewers. Farmers will benefit from a new sales channel for their organic barley, while consumers will gain access to craft beverages utilizing regionally produced malt. Processors will have a reliable supply of malt, and stakeholders involved in the craft beverage industry will be able to connect with a local product, allowing them to highlight the origins of their ingredients. This operation is expected to initially supply a single brewery in Madison, WI, with the potential for expansion to serve a wider range of craft beverage producers and, in the future, home brewers seeking access to high-quality malt.
